versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a physics class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a physics class.

Man: We've been talking about the law of inertia. An object moving in a straight line will continue to move in a straight line unless it is acted upon by another force. So what does this mean in the real world? Let's look at something many people do all the time, riding a bicycle. Think about riding along in a straight line. Once the bike is moving, inertia will keep it going in a straight line. But we don't just ride in straight lines, do we? We turn at corners and steer around things that are in our way. So how do you get the bicycle not to go straight? Easy, right? Don't you just need to turn the front wheel in the direction you want to turn? In fact, if you only turn the front wheel, you're likely to end up on the pavement. The wheel will turn, but because of inertia, your body and the rest of the bike will want to keep moving straight ahead. So how does a cyclist avoid this? The key is to lean in. Weight needs to shift in the direction of the turn so that the force of gravity can work against the force of inertia. Professional cyclists who move at high speeds need to hit a sweet spot. They must lean more to keep their bicycles from sliding out of turns, but not too much. At a certain point, gravity will bring both rider and bicycle down to the ground.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class. Often when we think of mummies, we think of ancient Egyptians and their elaborate methods of preserving bodies. We used to think Egyptians were the only people practicing mummification during the Bronze Age about 4,000 years ago, because typical mummies are found in places with very dry climates like Egypt. But then archaeologists discovered a site in Scotland with evidence of mummification, and Scotland is wet and rainy. This site is called Cladh Hallan, the only place in Britain where we found prehistoric Bronze Age mummies. Researchers unearthed skeletons there, including a man and a woman from around 1500 BCE. Since these were just skeletons, the researchers did not realize at first that they had actually been mummies. Radiocarbon dating revealed that the man and woman had died several hundred years before being buried. Normally, such a long wait would turn a body into a pile of bones, not an actual skeleton. So their bodies must have been purposely preserved for hundreds of years before burial. The bodies were preserved, mummified in a peat bog. Peat bogs are like swamps, except their conditions prevent organic materials like bodies from fully breaking down. Prehistoric people in Scotland used to preserve animal fat like butter in peat bogs, so they definitely had the concept.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段考古学课的讲座。想到木乃伊，我们常想到古埃及人及其精心的遗体保存方法。我们曾以为青铜时代约四千年前只有埃及人做木乃伊，因为典型木乃伊出现在埃及这类极干燥气候的地方。但考古学家在苏格兰发现有木乃伊化证据的遗址，而苏格兰潮湿多雨。该遗址叫 Cladh Hallan，是英国唯一发现史前青铜时代木乃伊的地方。研究者在那里挖出骨架，包括约公元前一五〇〇年的一男一女。因为只是骨架，研究者起初没意识到它们其实曾是木乃伊。放射性碳测年显示这对男女在下葬前数百年就已死亡。通常这么久的等待会把身体变成一堆碎骨，而不是完整骨架。所以他们的身体必定在下葬前被有意保存了数百年。身体是在泥炭沼泽中保存、木乃伊化的。泥炭沼泽像沼泽，但其条件阻止身体等有机物完全分解。苏格兰史前人曾在泥炭沼泽中保存动物脂肪如黄油，所以他们肯定有这个概念。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Narrator
transcriptSentences.text: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class.

transcriptSentences.text: Often when we think of mummies, we think of ancient Egyptians and their elaborate methods of preserving bodies.

transcriptSentences.text: We used to think Egyptians were the only people practicing mummification during the Bronze Age about 4,000 years ago, because typical mummies are found in places with very dry climates like Egypt.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 我们曾以为青铜时代约四千年前只有埃及人做木乃伊，因为典型木乃伊出现在埃及这类极干燥气候的地方。

transcriptSentences.text: But then archaeologists discovered a site in Scotland with evidence of mummification, and Scotland is wet and rainy.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但考古学家在苏格兰发现有木乃伊化证据的遗址，而苏格兰潮湿多雨。

transcriptSentences.text: This site is called Cladh Hallan, the only place in Britain where we found prehistoric Bronze Age mummies.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 该遗址叫 Cladh Hallan，是英国唯一发现史前青铜时代木乃伊的地方。

transcriptSentences.text: Researchers unearthed skeletons there, including a man and a woman from around 1500 BCE.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 研究者在那里挖出骨架，包括约公元前一五〇〇年的一男一女。

transcriptSentences.text: Since these were just skeletons, the researchers did not realize at first that they had actually been mummies.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 因为只是骨架，研究者起初没意识到它们其实曾是木乃伊。

transcriptSentences.text: Radiocarbon dating revealed that the man and woman had died several hundred years before being buried.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 放射性碳测年显示这对男女在下葬前数百年就已死亡。

transcriptSentences.text: Normally, such a long wait would turn a body into a pile of bones, not an actual skeleton.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 通常这么久的等待会把身体变成一堆碎骨，而不是完整骨架。

transcriptSentences.text: So their bodies must have been purposely preserved for hundreds of years before burial.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 所以他们的身体必定在下葬前被有意保存了数百年。

transcriptSentences.text: The bodies were preserved, mummified in a peat bog.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 身体是在泥炭沼泽中保存、木乃伊化的。

transcriptSentences.text: Peat bogs are like swamps, except their conditions prevent organic materials like bodies from fully breaking down.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 泥炭沼泽像沼泽，但其条件阻止身体等有机物完全分解。

transcriptSentences.text: Prehistoric people in Scotland used to preserve animal fat like butter in peat bogs, so they definitely had the concept.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 苏格兰史前人曾在泥炭沼泽中保存动物脂肪如黄油，所以他们肯定有这个概念。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker mainly discuss?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者主要讨论什么？

choices.label: The differences between Egyptian and Scottish mummies
choices.labelZh: 埃及与苏格兰木乃伊之间的差异
choices.explanationZh: Egypt 是对比引入。

choices.label: The discovery of prehistoric mummies in a surprising location
choices.labelZh: 在一个意外地点发现的史前木乃伊
choices.explanationZh: 正确：Scotland wet climate 中发现 Bronze Age mummies。

choices.label: The processes that gradually turn mummies into skeletons
choices.labelZh: 将木乃伊逐渐转变为骸骨的过程

choices.label: The reasons that Bronze Age people practiced mummification

questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者对苏格兰有何暗示？

choices.label: Its climate is not favorable for typical methods of preserving bodies.
choices.labelZh: 其气候不利于保存遗体的典型方法
choices.explanationZh: 正确：Scotland wet and rainy，不像 dry Egypt。

choices.label: Its rainy weather makes archaeological research challenging.
choices.labelZh: 其多雨天气使考古研究具有挑战性
choices.explanationZh: 没有说研究困难。

choices.label: Its oldest skeletons date back to around 4000 B.C.E.

questions.promptText: According to the speaker, what did radiocarbon dating reveal?

choices.label: A pile of bones belonged to two different people.
choices.labelZh: 一堆骨头属于两个不同的人
choices.explanationZh: 发现的是 skeletons。

choices.label: A man and a woman had died around 1500 B.C.E.
choices.labelZh: 一男一女约在公元前1500年死亡
choices.explanationZh: 1500 BCE 是 skeletons date，关键发现是死后数百年才埋。

choices.label: Two objects that looked like skeletons were not made of bone.
choices.labelZh: 两个看起来像骸骨的物体并非由骨头构成
choices.explanationZh: 无此说法。

choices.label: Two people were buried long after they had died.
choices.labelZh: 两个人在死后很久才被埋葬
choices.explanationZh: 正确：died several hundred years before being buried。

choices.label: To point out an animal fat frequently used to preserve bodies
choices.labelZh: 指出一种常用于保存遗体的动物脂肪
choices.explanationZh: butter 是 animal fat，但用于说明人们知道 peat bog 保存有机物。

choices.label: To show that ancient people understood a property of peat bogs
choices.labelZh: 表明古人了解泥炭沼的某种特性
choices.explanationZh: 正确：他们用 peat bog 保存 butter，说明有保存有机物的概念。

choices.label: To help illustrate how swamps break down organic material
choices.labelZh: 帮助说明沼泽如何分解有机物质
choices.explanationZh: peat bog 防止分解。

choices.label: To suggest an ingredient possibly used in a prehistoric burial ritual
choices.labelZh: 暗示史前葬礼仪式中可能使用的一种成分
choices.explanationZh: 没有说用于 burial ritual。

versions.transcript: Often when we think of mummies, we think of ancient Egyptians and their elaborate methods of preserving bodies. We used to think Egyptians were the only people practicing mummification during the Bronze Age about, oh, 4,000 years ago, because typical mummies are found in places, for example, with very dry climates like Egypt. But then archaeologists discovered a site in Scotland with evidence of mummification, and Scotland is, well, wet, rainy. This site is called Cladh Hallan, the only place in Britain where we found prehistoric Bronze Age mummies. So researchers unearthed skeletons at Cladh Hallan, including a man and a woman from around 1500 BCE. Since these were just skeletons, the researchers didn't realize at first that they had actually been mummies. That realization came after doing a test called radiocarbon dating on the bones. Radiocarbon dating revealed that the man and woman had died several hundred years before being buried. Normally, such a long wait would turn a body into a pile of bones, not an actual skeleton, like what was found. So their bodies must have been purposely preserved for hundreds of years before burial. Why? Well, who knows? But we do know how. The bodies were preserved, mummified in a peat bog. Peat bogs are kinda like swamps, except their conditions prevent organic materials like bodies from fully breaking down. They stay more intact. Prehistoric people in Scotland used to preserve animal fat like butter in peat bogs. So they definitely had the concept.

transcriptSentences.text: Well, who knows?

transcriptSentences.textZh: 尸体是在泥炭沼泽中被保存并木乃伊化的。

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a business podcast. When launching a new business, entrepreneurs face countless decisions, from choosing a target market to deciding which features to include in their first product. These choices can be overwhelming, especially when resources are limited and time is short. To address these challenges, some startups adopt a strategy that emphasizes speed, experimentation, and customer feedback. This approach, known as the Lean Startup methodology, was popularized by Eric Ries and has gained traction in the tech world and beyond. One of its core practices is building a minimum viable product, or MVP. This is a basic version of a new product that can be released quickly to gather feedback from early users. The goal is to learn what works and what doesn't, so that future development is guided by actual user experience rather than assumptions. Another key principle is validated learning. Instead of doing traditional market research like surveys or focus groups, entrepreneurs test their ideas by putting the product out in the real world. This helps them figure out whether their product actually meets the needs of their customers. In all fairness, I should point out that this approach isn't perfect. Rapid iteration and constant feedback can sometimes lead to confusion or a lack of clear direction. And in the pursuit of efficiency, some teams may cut corners, which could affect product quality. Still, many entrepreneurs find the Lean Startup methodology helpful for navigating the uncertainties of launching a new business.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a science podcast.

Woman: Let's talk a bit about bird migration. Migratory birds travel vast distances between their breeding and wintering grounds, often covering thousands of miles. These journeys are driven by the need to find suitable habitats with adequate food supplies and favorable climate conditions. One of the most remarkable aspects of migration is a bird's ability to navigate accurately over such long distances. Birds use a variety of navigational cues, such as the position of the sun, stars, and, incredibly, Earth's magnetic field. Certain bird species have a special protein in their eyes that allows them to see magnetic fields, and this helps them stay on course. Migratory birds play key roles in ecosystems by dispersing seeds and controlling pests, so their decline can cause imbalances throughout food webs. Of course, a migration over hundreds or even thousands of miles will be fraught with risk. Obvious dangers include harsh weather conditions, predators, and the risk of exhaustion and starvation. Less obviously, human activities also pose significant threats to migratory birds. Habitat destruction, pollution and climate change have led to a decline in many migratory bird populations. At night, light pollution can disorient birds that navigate by the stars, causing them to become lost or collide with buildings. Protecting key habitats and reducing light pollution are a few of the steps that can help safeguard migrating birds. Solutions include bird friendly building design and programs that encourage turning off unnecessary lights during peak migration seasons.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段科学播客的讲座。

女：我们来谈一点鸟类迁徙。候鸟在繁殖地与越冬地之间飞行遥远距离，常达数千英里。这些旅程受寻找食物充足、气候适宜的栖息地驱动。迁徙最非凡的方面之一是鸟在如此长距离上精确导航的能力。鸟使用多种导航线索，如太阳位置、星辰，以及——难以置信地——地球磁场。某些鸟种眼中有特殊蛋白质，使它们能看见磁场，从而帮助保持航线。候鸟通过传播种子与控制害虫在生态系统中起关键作用，因此其衰退可导致整个食物网失衡。当然，数百甚至数千英里的迁徙充满风险。明显危险包括恶劣天气、捕食者，以及精疲力竭与饥饿风险。不那么明显的是，人类活动也对候鸟构成重大威胁。栖息地破坏、污染与气候变化已导致许多候鸟种群下降。夜间，光污染可使靠星辰导航的鸟迷失方向，导致迷路或撞上建筑。保护关键栖息地、减少光污染是有助守护候鸟的若干步骤。解决办法包括对鸟友好的建筑设计，以及在迁徙高峰季节鼓励关闭不必要灯光的项目。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an anthropology class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an anthropology class. For most of its history, anthropology put humans at the center. Animals were treated as resources, symbols, or background, important only for what they meant to us. Classic anthropology focused on how people hunted, herded, or mythologized animals, reinforcing a sharp divide: humans belonged to culture and animals to nature. Early studies of Arctic hunting rituals examined how seals symbolized spiritual beliefs and social bonds without asking about the seals’ own behaviors or ecological roles. Multispecies anthropology flips that perspective. It sees humans and other species, animals, plants, even fungi, as co-participants in shared worlds. Instead of reducing nonhumans to cultural symbols, it highlights their agency. Studies of mushroom foraging in Siberia show fungi, trees and humans forming interdependent networks. Life is not a human story with animals or plants in the background; it is a web of relationships among many kinds of beings. Next, the speaker will explore how this perspective reshapes research methods.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段人类学课的讲座。在其历史的大部分时间里，人类学把人类放在中心。动物被当作资源、符号或背景，重要之处仅在于它们对我们意味着什么。经典人类学关注人们如何狩猎、放牧或神话化动物，强化了鲜明分野：人类属于文化，动物属于自然。早期对北极狩猎仪式的研究考察海豹如何象征精神信仰与社会纽带，却不问海豹自身行为或生态角色。多物种人类学翻转了这一视角。它把人类与其他物种——动物、植物甚至真菌——视为共享世界中的共同参与者。它不把非人类简化为文化符号，而强调其能动性。西伯利亚采蘑菇的研究显示真菌、树木与人类形成相互依赖的网络。生命不是以动植物为背景的人类故事；它是多种存在之间关系的网。接下来，讲者将探讨这一视角如何重塑研究方法。

Instead of reducing nonhumans to cultural symbols, it highlights their agency, their ability to act, adapt, and influence human lives. Take the studies of mushroom foraging in Siberia. versions.transcriptZh: 在人类学的大部分历史中，人类一直处于中心地位。 动物被视为资源、符号或背景，其重要性仅限于它们对我们的意义。 经典人类学关注人们如何狩猎、放牧或神化动物，从而强化了人与动物之间鲜明的界限：人类属于文化，动物属于自然。 早期对北极狩猎仪式的研究，考察了海豹如何象征精神信仰和社会联系，但没有涉及海豹自身的行为或生态作用。 这种方法深入了解了人类的意义建构，但忽视了物种间关系的复杂性。 多物种人类学则颠覆了这一视角。 它将人类和其他物种，动物、植物，甚至真菌，视为共享世界中的共同参与者。 它没有将非人类简化为文化符号，而是强调它们的能动性，即它们行动、适应和影响人类生活的能力。 以西伯利亚蘑菇采集研究为例。 在这里，真菌、树木和人类构成了相互依存的网络。 生命不是一个以动物或植物为背景的人类故事；它是一个由多种生命形式组成的相互关系网络。 接下来，演讲者将探讨这一视角如何重塑研究方法。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a materials science class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in a materials science class. Big-city skyscrapers are so tall they seem to defy gravity, right? Well, they're made possible by a material called reinforced concrete, really a feat of modern engineering. Reinforced concrete integrates two very different materials: concrete and steel. Concrete has excellent compressive strength, meaning it can be squeezed hard without breaking, the same way that a chair doesn't crumble when you sit in it. But concrete cracks under tensile stress, when it's being pulled on. Think of lifting a grocery bag with a heavy bowling ball in it. The bag might tear apart when you lift it, right? And steel is just the opposite: it has tensile strength, but is not so great under compression. By joining these two, engineers created a material that resists both compression and tension, making it indispensable for constructing resilient structures like tall buildings. But how exactly do they work together? For one thing, concrete and steel expand and contract at nearly identical rates in response to temperature variations. All materials expand slightly when they get warmer and contract when they cool. If the rates at which two combined materials do so are different, cracks may develop over time. But here, we don't have this problem. Now, reinforced concrete isn't perfect. Environmental factors, particularly in regions with salty air, like coastal areas, can lead to steel corrosion, which affects its strength. Alternatives like stainless steel or fiberglass are being explored, but they come with higher costs.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段材料科学课的讲座。大城市摩天楼高得仿佛无视重力，对吧？它们靠一种叫钢筋混凝土的材料成为可能，真是现代工程的壮举。钢筋混凝土整合两种截然不同的材料：混凝土与钢。混凝土抗压强度极好，意思是可被用力挤压而不碎，就像椅子不会因你坐下而崩塌。但混凝土在拉应力下会裂，也就是被拉扯时。想象提起装着重保龄球的购物袋。一提袋子可能撕裂，对吧？钢恰恰相反：有抗拉强度，但抗压不那么强。把二者结合，工程师创造出既抗压又抗拉的材料，对建造摩天楼这类韧性结构不可或缺。它们究竟如何协同？其一，混凝土与钢随温度变化膨胀收缩速率几乎相同。所有材料变热时略胀、变冷时收缩。若两种结合材料速率不同，久之可能开裂。但这里没有这个问题。钢筋混凝土并非完美。环境因素，尤其在海岸等盐雾地区，可导致钢腐蚀，影响强度。不锈钢或玻璃纤维等替代材料正在探索，但成本更高。

transcriptSentences.textZh: 钢筋混凝土整合两种截然不同的材料：混凝土与钢。

transcriptSentences.text: Concrete has excellent compressive strength, meaning it can be squeezed hard without breaking, the same way that a chair doesn't crumble when you sit in it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 混凝土抗压强度极好，意思是可被用力挤压而不碎，就像椅子不会因你坐下而崩塌。

transcriptSentences.text: But concrete cracks under tensile stress, when it's being pulled on.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但混凝土在拉应力下会裂，也就是被拉扯时。

transcriptSentences.text: Think of lifting a grocery bag with a heavy bowling ball in it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 想象提起装着重保龄球的购物袋。

transcriptSentences.text: The bag might tear apart when you lift it, right?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 一提袋子可能撕裂，对吧？

transcriptSentences.text: And steel is just the opposite: it has tensile strength, but is not so great under compression.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 钢恰恰相反：有抗拉强度，但抗压不那么强。

transcriptSentences.text: By joining these two, engineers created a material that resists both compression and tension, making it indispensable for constructing resilient structures like tall buildings.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 把二者结合，工程师创造出既抗压又抗拉的材料，对建造摩天楼这类韧性结构不可或缺。

transcriptSentences.text: But how exactly do they work together?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们究竟如何协同？

transcriptSentences.text: For one thing, concrete and steel expand and contract at nearly identical rates in response to temperature variations.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 其一，混凝土与钢随温度变化膨胀收缩速率几乎相同。

transcriptSentences.text: All materials expand slightly when they get warmer and contract when they cool.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 所有材料变热时略胀、变冷时收缩。

transcriptSentences.text: If the rates at which two combined materials do so are different, cracks may develop over time.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 若两种结合材料速率不同，久之可能开裂。

transcriptSentences.text: But here, we don't have this problem.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但这里没有这个问题。

transcriptSentences.text: Now, reinforced concrete isn't perfect.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 钢筋混凝土并非完美。

transcriptSentences.text: Environmental factors, particularly in regions with salty air, like coastal areas, can lead to steel corrosion, which affects its strength.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 环境因素，尤其在海岸等盐雾地区，可导致钢腐蚀，影响强度。

transcriptSentences.text: Alternatives like stainless steel or fiberglass are being explored, but they come with higher costs.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 不锈钢或玻璃纤维等替代材料正在探索，但成本更高。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker mainly discuss?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者主要讨论了什么？

choices.label: The reasons that skyscrapers have been built taller over time
choices.labelZh: 摩天大楼随时间越建越高的原因
choices.explanationZh: skyscrapers 只是开头引出 reinforced concrete 的例子；讲座没有解释摩天楼为什么越来越高。

choices.label: The combination of two materials to build strong structures
choices.labelZh: 两种材料结合以建造坚固结构
choices.explanationZh: 正确：讲座主线是 concrete 和 steel 如何互补，合成 reinforced concrete 来同时抵抗 compression 和 tension。

choices.label: The processes used to make different building materials
choices.labelZh: 制造不同建筑材料的过程
choices.explanationZh: 讲座讲材料性能和配合方式，不讲不同建材的制造流程。

choices.label: The best and worst options for construction materials
choices.labelZh: 建筑材料的最佳与最差选择
choices.explanationZh: 结尾只提 reinforced concrete 的缺点和替代材料成本高，不是在比较最好和最差建材。

questions.promptText: Why does the speaker mention a grocery bag?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者为何提到一个杂货袋？

choices.label: To compare the weights of concrete and steel
choices.labelZh: 为了比较混凝土和钢材的重量
choices.explanationZh: grocery bag 的例子不是比较 concrete 和 steel 的重量，而是说明被拉扯时会撕裂。

choices.label: To explain why concrete can become squeezed
choices.labelZh: 为了解释为何混凝土会被挤压
choices.explanationZh: concrete 被挤压不碎是 compressive strength，speaker 用 chair 解释；grocery bag 讲的是 tensile stress。

choices.label: To illustrate what happens when tensile strength is absent
choices.labelZh: 为了说明没有抗拉强度时会发生什么
choices.explanationZh: 正确：装着重物的袋子被提起时可能撕裂，正好说明缺少 tensile strength 时材料承受不了拉力。

choices.label: To point out a difference between paper and plastic
choices.labelZh: 为了指出纸与塑料的区别
choices.explanationZh: 讲座没有比较纸袋和塑料袋；bag 只是用来解释拉力问题。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker say about temperature variations?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者对温度变化有何说法？

choices.label: They improve the strength of reinforced concrete.
choices.labelZh: 它们增强了钢筋混凝土的强度。
choices.explanationZh: temperature variations 没有被说成能增强 reinforced concrete；重点是两种材料热胀冷缩速率接近。

choices.label: They worsen the effect of salt on buildings.
choices.labelZh: 它们加剧了盐对建筑物的影响。
choices.explanationZh: salt corrosion 是另一个环境问题，和 temperature variations 不是同一个因果关系。

choices.label: Concrete and steel react to them in similar ways.
choices.labelZh: 混凝土和钢材对它们的反应相似。
choices.explanationZh: 正确：speaker 明确说 concrete and steel expand and contract at nearly identical rates，所以温度变化下反应相似。

choices.labelZh: 如果变化剧烈，建筑物裂缝会形成。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker imply about stainless steel and fiberglass?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者对不锈钢和玻璃纤维有何暗示？

choices.label: They may be better than reinforced concrete in coastal areas.
choices.labelZh: 它们在沿海地区可能优于钢筋混凝土。
choices.explanationZh: 正确：coastal areas 的 salty air 会导致 steel corrosion，speaker 随后说 stainless steel 和 fiberglass 正被探索，暗示它们可能更适合这种环境。

choices.label: They may work together to improve resistance to environmental factors.
choices.labelZh: 它们可能协同作用以提高抗环境因素能力。
choices.explanationZh: 原文说它们是 alternatives，没有说 stainless steel 和 fiberglass 要组合使用。

choices.label: They are simpler to produce than reinforced concrete.
choices.labelZh: 它们比钢筋混凝土更易于生产。
choices.explanationZh: 讲座只说这些替代材料成本更高，没有说生产更简单。

choices.labelZh: 它们与钢筋混凝土的腐蚀方式相似。
choices.explanationZh: 它们被提到是因为 salty air 会让 reinforced concrete 中的 steel 腐蚀；不是说这些替代材料也同样腐蚀。

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an architecture class. The Eastgate Centre in Harare, Zimbabwe, is a mixed-use complex combining retail spaces and offices. When the architect Mick Pearce was asked to design the building in the early 1990s, he faced a big challenge: how to keep all its shops and offices cool without traditional air conditioning, and do it during an economic crisis. Energy costs were high, and importing advanced air conditioners was impossible. To solve this dilemma, Pearce looked to termite mounds. Termites are insects that live in large colonies. They build big mounds on the ground throughout the African savanna. The mounds are amazing structures. Some rise three meters above ground and extend another one to three meters below the ground. The underground chambers connect to the above-ground chimneys through a maze of tunnels. And this entire system works as natural climate control. Warm air rises and escapes through the top, while cooler air flows in from below. The thick walls of soil and clay absorb heat during the day and release it at night. Termites fine-tune airflow by opening and closing vents, adding or removing soil to enlarge or seal passages. On hot days, they open more vents for cooling. At night, they close them to keep warmth in. Pearce borrowed these ideas. The Eastgate Centre's walls are made from thick materials like concrete and brick, and there's a system of ducts and adjustable louvers throughout the building to mimic those vents. The result? A building that uses far less energy than its conventional counterparts.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段建筑学课的讲座。津巴布韦哈拉雷的东门中心是集零售与办公于一体的综合体。建筑师 Mick Pearce 在一九九〇年代初受邀设计该建筑时面临大挑战：如何在不用传统空调的情况下让所有商铺与办公室保持凉爽，而且还是在经济危机期间。能源成本高，进口先进空调又不可能。为解此困，Pearce 求教于白蚁丘。白蚁是群居昆虫。它们在非洲稀树草原各地地面筑起大丘。蚁丘是惊人结构。有的高出地面三米，地下再延伸一到三米。地下腔室通过隧道迷宫与地面烟囱相连。整套系统起到自然气候控制作用。热空气上升从顶部逸出，较冷空气从下方流入。厚土与黏土墙白天吸热、夜间释放。白蚁通过开闭通风口、加减泥土扩大或封闭通道，微调气流。热天开更多通风口降温。夜间关闭以保暖。Pearce 借用了这些想法。东门中心的墙用混凝土与砖等厚材料，整栋楼有管道与可调百叶系统模仿那些通风口。结果？能耗远低于传统同类建筑的一座楼。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a psychology class.

Man: Positive reinforcement is a powerful concept in psychology and behavior training. It means giving a reward after someone performs an action you want them to do again. The basic idea is that when a behavior leads to a positive outcome, it's more likely to be repeated. In other words, we tend to repeat actions that bring us something positive. This principle applies to both humans and animals, but the way it works can differ. Animals need to receive rewards immediately after the desired behavior. For example, if a dog sits and gets a treat right away, it learns that sitting leads to something good. If the reward comes too late, the connection is lost. Humans, however, can understand delayed rewards. They might work hard today because they're aiming for a future goal, like earning a degree. Or they might feel motivated by praise even if the reward isn't tangible or instant. But rewards must be used carefully. If a parent gives a child candy to stop whining, the child may learn that whining gets rewarded. It's like watering weeds instead of flowers. You're encouraging the wrong behavior. And if rewards are given too frequently, they can reduce a person's internal motivation, making them rely more on external incentives to take action. So while positive reinforcement is effective, it works best when applied thoughtfully and with clear intent.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段心理学课的讲座。

男：正强化是心理学与行为训练中有力的概念。意思是在某人做出你希望他再做的动作之后给予奖励。基本想法是：行为带来积极结果时，更可能被重复。换句话说，我们倾向重复能带来积极事物的动作。这一原则适用于人类与动物，但作用方式可能不同。动物需要在目标行为后立刻得到奖励。例如狗坐下马上得到零食，就学会坐下带来好事。奖励太晚会失去联结。人类却能理解延迟奖励。他们可能今天努力是为了未来目标，比如拿学位。也可能被表扬激励，即便奖励不具体或不即时。但奖励必须谨慎使用。若父母给孩子糖果让其停止哭闹，孩子可能学会哭闹会得奖。就像给杂草浇水而不是花。你在鼓励错误行为。奖励给得太频繁，还会削弱内在动机，使人更依赖外部激励才行动。因此正强化虽有效，最好经深思熟虑、意图明确地使用。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a health podcast.

Woman: Today we're going to talk about the importance of sleep for cognitive function. Sleep is crucial for maintaining various aspects of brain health. One of the key benefits of sleep is the consolidation of memory. During sleep, particularly during the deep sleep stages, the brain processes and stores information acquired during the day, making it easier to recall later. During deep sleep, the brain also undergoes a process that flushes out neurotoxins like beta amyloid, which are linked to Alzheimer's disease. Sleep helps in learning new skills and knowledge by strengthening neural connections, and it allows the brain to enhance problem solving abilities by reorganizing information. Studies have shown that sleep deprivation affects cognitive functions like attention and decision making. Another crucial aspect of sleep is its role in emotional regulation. During sleep, the brain can process emotional experiences, which helps maintain emotional stability. REM sleep in particular plays a key role in recalibrating the brain's emotional circuits, helping people better manage fear and anxiety responses. By doing so, individuals can improve their cognitive function and overall well being.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a geography class.

Woman: Urbanization is frequently associated with negative outcomes: pollution, overcrowding, and especially traffic congestion. In many cities, poor planning has led to increased noise and emissions as well as reduced quality of life. However, urbanization doesn't have to be this way. If approached thoughtfully, an alternative to traffic jams and congested city streets is to foster sustainable transportation. Copenhagen in Denmark, for instance, has made bicycles a central part of its urban design. The city's extensive network of protected bike lanes and pro cycling policies have encouraged residents to choose bicycles over cars. In addition to lowering automobile emissions, this shift has also improved public health and reduced traffic related stress. Also, when kept in control and planned properly, urbanization, in this case compact urban living, minimizes land use and energy consumption. Compared to sprawling suburban development, suburban neighborhoods require large plots of land for individual homes, roads and parking. When housing, services and infrastructure are concentrated, this can actually preserve surrounding natural areas and agricultural lands. So, even though this may seem strange, urban growth is actually more compatible with environmental conservation. Urbanization also, by necessity, has led to some innovative thinking, especially concerning the efficient use of land and space. Many cities are incorporating such innovation in food production by creating rooftop farms and using vertical agriculture, which grows crops in stacked vertical layers. In particular, Singapore has invested in high tech urban farming systems that grow vegetables in controlled environments, helping increase local food supply and reduce dependence on imports.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class.

Man: The Renaissance was a pivotal period in European history. Spanning roughly the 14th to the 17th centuries, the Renaissance is characterized by a renewed interest in art, science and literature. It marked a significant departure from the Middle Ages and laid the groundwork for the modern era. One of the defining features of the Renaissance was the revival of classical learning. Scholars and artists looked back to the texts and artistic achievements of ancient Greece and Rome for inspiration. This led to a flourishing of ideas and creativity evident in the works of figures like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo and Galileo Galilei. The invention of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440 was a crucial development during this time. It allowed for the mass production of books, making literature and scholarly works more accessible to a broader audience. This contributed to increased literacy and the spread of Renaissance ideas. The Renaissance also saw major advancements in science, particularly in astronomy. Nicolaus Copernicus proposed a heliocentric model of the solar system, placing the sun, not the Earth, as the center. Galileo Galilei later used a telescope to observe celestial bodies, providing evidence that supported Copernicus theory. These discoveries challenged long held beliefs and laid the foundation for modern astronomy. Despite political instability in some regions, the Renaissance left a lasting legacy on European society. Its influence can still be seen today in art, science and education.

男：文艺复兴是欧洲历史上的关键时期。大约跨越十四至十七世纪，其特征是对艺术、科学与文学的重新兴趣。它标志着与中世纪的重大背离，并为现代奠定基础。文艺复兴的界定特征之一是古典学问的复兴。学者与艺术家回望古希腊罗马的文本与艺术成就寻求灵感。这带来观念与创造力的繁荣，可见于列奥纳多·达·芬奇、米开朗琪罗与伽利略·伽利莱等人的作品。约翰内斯·古腾堡约一四四〇年发明印刷机是这一时期的关键发展。它使书籍可大批量生产，让文学与学术著作更易被更广受众获取。这促进了识字率提高与文艺复兴思想传播。文艺复兴在科学尤其天文学上也有重大进展。尼古拉·哥白尼提出太阳系日心模型，把太阳而非地球置于中心。伽利略·伽利莱后来用望远镜观测天体，提供支持哥白尼理论的证据。这些发现挑战了长期信念，为现代天文学奠基。尽管某些地区政治不稳，文艺复兴仍给欧洲社会留下持久遗产。其影响今日仍可见于艺术、科学与教育。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Scholars and artists looked back to the texts and artistic achievements of ancient Greece and Rome for inspiration.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: This led to a flourishing of ideas and creativity evident in the works of figures like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo and Galileo Galilei.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: The invention of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440 was a crucial development during this time.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: It allowed for the mass production of books, making literature and scholarly works more accessible to a broader audience.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: This contributed to increased literacy and the spread of Renaissance ideas.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: The Renaissance also saw major advancements in science, particularly in astronomy.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 文艺复兴在科学尤其天文学上也有重大进展。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed a heliocentric model of the solar system, placing the sun, not the Earth, as the center.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Galileo Galilei later used a telescope to observe celestial bodies, providing evidence that supported Copernicus theory.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 伽利略·伽利莱后来用望远镜观测天体，提供支持哥白尼理论的证据。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: These discoveries challenged long held beliefs and laid the foundation for modern astronomy.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这些发现挑战了长期信念，为现代天文学奠基。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Despite political instability in some regions, the Renaissance left a lasting legacy on European society.

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Its influence can still be seen today in art, science and education.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 其影响今日仍可见于艺术、科学与教育。

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Expressionism is an influential modernist art movement that emerged in the early 20th century. This movement is characterized by its focus on representing emotional experience rather than physical reality. Expressionist artists aim to convey their inner feelings and perceptions through distorted and exaggerated forms, vivid colors, and bold brushstrokes. One of the most famous Expressionist artists is Edvard Munch. His painting The Scream shows an agonized person crying out. It eventually became an icon of the movement's focus on intense personal experience. Expressionism was not limited to visual arts, however. It also influenced literature, theater and cinematic arts. In literature, authors like Franz Kafka explored themes of alienation and existential angst. Expressionist theater often used dramatic lighting and intense performances to evoke emotional responses. Sets sometimes featured oversized symbolic objects. In Elmer Rice's 1923 play The Adding Machine, a giant adding machine represents the dehumanizing forces of technology. Similarly, German Expressionist film used innovative techniques. Despite its impact, Expressionism faced criticism for departure from traditional aesthetics and emphasis on the personal. Critics argued that its focus on subjective emotion robbed works of broader content or meaning. Nonetheless, Expressionism paved the way for later movements such as Surrealism.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段艺术史课的讲座。表现主义是二十世纪初兴起的有影响力的现代主义艺术运动。其特点是侧重表现情感体验而非物理现实。表现主义艺术家通过变形夸张的形态、鲜明色彩与大胆笔触，传达内心感受与知觉。最著名的表现主义艺术家之一是爱德华·蒙克。他的画作《呐喊》呈现一个痛苦呼号的人。它最终成为该运动强调强烈个人体验的标志。但表现主义不限于视觉艺术。它也影响文学、戏剧与电影。文学上，弗兰茨·卡夫卡等作家探索异化与存在焦虑主题。表现主义戏剧常用戏剧性灯光与强烈表演唤起情感反应。布景有时出现超大号象征物件。在埃尔默·赖斯一九二三年的剧作《加法机》中，一台巨大的加法机代表技术的非人化力量。同样，德国表现主义电影使用创新手法。尽管影响巨大，表现主义因偏离传统美学、强调个人而受批评。批评者认为它对主观情感的聚焦剥夺了作品更广的内容或意义。尽管如此，表现主义为超现实主义等后来运动铺了路。

versions.transcript: Expressionism is an influential modernist art movement that emerged in the early 20th century. This movement is characterized by its focus on representing emotional experience rather than physical reality. Expressionist artists aim to convey their inner feelings and perceptions through distorted and exaggerated forms, vivid colors, and bold brushstrokes. One of the most famous Expressionist artists is Edvard Munch. His painting The Scream shows an agonized person crying out. It eventually became an icon of the movement's focus on intense personal experience. Expressionism was not limited to visual arts, however. It also influenced literary theater and cinematic arts. In literature, authors like Franz Kafka explored themes of alienation and existential angst in his bizarre, dreamlike fiction. Expressionist theater often used dramatic lighting and intense performances to evoke emotional responses. Set sometimes featured oversized symbolic objects. In Elmer Rice's 1923 play The Adding Machine, a giant adding machine represents the dehumanizing forces of technology. Similarly, the German Expressionist film movement used innovative techniques, such as cutting between scenes with a shared sound to help create emotionally charged narratives. Despite its impact, Expressionism faced criticism for its departure from traditional aesthetics and its emphasis on the personal. Critics argued that its focus on subjective emotion robbed the works of broader content or meaning. And the bold brushwork in painting was sometimes viewed as lacking in skill and technique. Nonetheless, Expressionism paved the way for later movements such as Surrealism, leaving a lasting legacy in the art world.
versions.transcriptZh: 表现主义是一个出现于20世纪初且具有影响力的现代主义艺术运动。 这一运动的特点是专注于表现情感体验而非物理现实。 表现主义艺术家旨在通过扭曲和夸张的形式、鲜艳的色彩以及大胆的笔触来传达他们的内在感受和感知。 最著名的表现主义艺术家之一是爱德华·蒙克。 他的画作《呐喊》展示了一个极其痛苦的人在尖叫。 它最终成为了该运动关注强烈个人体验的象征。 然而，表现主义并不局限于视觉艺术。 它还影响了文学戏剧和电影艺术。 在文学方面，像弗兰茨·卡夫卡这样的作者在他离奇、梦幻的小说中探索了疏离感和存在焦虑的主题。 表现主义戏剧经常使用戏剧性的灯光和强烈的表演来激发情感反应。 布景有时会出现超大的象征性物品。 在埃尔默·赖斯1923年的戏剧《加法机》中，一台巨大的加法机代表了技术剥离人性的力量。 类似地，德国表现主义电影运动使用了创新技术，例如在共用音效的场景之间进行剪辑，以帮助创作充满情感色彩的叙事。 尽管具有影响力，表现主义因其背离传统美学和对个人体验的强调而面临批评。 批评者认为，它对主观情感的关注剥夺了作品更广泛的内容或意义。 绘画中粗犷的笔触有时被认为缺乏技巧和技术。 尽管如此，表现主义为后来的超现实主义等运动铺平了道路，在艺术界留下了持久的遗产。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a podcast about political science.
versions.transcript: Listen to a podcast about political science. Soft power refers to a country's ability to influence others through attraction, culture, and collaboration. The term was introduced by political scientist Joseph Nye in 1990. He noticed that some countries gain support not by using force or money, but by being admired and respected. What Nye contributed wasn't just a name. He offered a clear framework for understanding this kind of influence. He explained that power works in three ways: by forcing others, by paying them, or by attracting them. That third kind, attraction, is what he called soft power. A modern example is South Korea's cultural wave, which has sparked global interest in Korean pop music, language, and food. This kind of appeal fits directly into Nye's idea of attraction. Now, soft power takes time because it's built on trust, reputation, and emotional connection. It spreads through cultural events, learning opportunities, and other shared experiences, things that grow gradually but once established, it tends to last, often shaping how future generations view a country.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段关于政治学的播客。软实力指一国通过吸引力、文化与合作影响他国的能力。这一术语由政治学家约瑟夫·奈于一九九〇年提出。他注意到有些国家获得支持不是靠武力或金钱，而是靠被钦佩与尊重。奈的贡献不只是一个名称。他提供了理解这种影响力的清晰框架。他解释权力有三种作用方式：强迫、收买，或吸引。第三种——吸引——就是他所谓的软实力。当代例子是韩国文化浪潮，引发全球对韩国流行音乐、语言与饮食的兴趣。这种魅力直接契合奈的吸引概念。软实力需要时间，因为它建立在信任、声誉与情感联结之上。它通过文化活动、学习机会及其他共享体验传播，这些事物逐渐成长，一旦确立往往持久，并常塑造后代如何看待一个国家。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a literature class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in a literature class. A common theme in literature is isolation. Isolation can be a powerful motif, reflecting the psychological effects of being separated from society. One classic example is Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, where the creature experiences profound isolation due to his monstrous appearance and the fear he instills in people. This isolation leads to anger and a desire for revenge. Another example is The Catcher in the Rye, whose protagonist Holden Caulfield feels disconnected from the world. Another example that ends badly is Moby Dick. Captain Ahab's obsessive, vengeful quest for the white whale leads to his isolation and propels him and his ship toward a destructive end. However, isolation is not always negative. In Jane Eyre, Jane experiences isolation at various points, but she is resilient in the face of isolation, becoming strong and independent.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段文学课的讲座。文学中常见主题是孤立。孤立可以是有力母题，反映与社会隔绝的心理效应。经典例子之一是玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》，其中造物因丑陋外表与在人们心中引发的恐惧而经历深刻孤立。这种孤立导致愤怒与复仇欲望。另一例子是《麦田里的守望者》，主人公霍尔顿·考尔菲德感到与世界脱节。结局糟糕的另一例子是《白鲸》。亚哈船长对白鲸偏执复仇的追逐导致他孤立，并把他与船推向毁灭结局。然而孤立并不总是负面的。在《简·爱》中，简在多个时刻经历孤立，但她面对孤立坚韧，变得坚强独立。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a biology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Man: Trilobites were a group of ancient sea creatures. They are classified as arthropods. They are extinct now. Among modern animals, horseshoe crabs probably resemble trilobites the most. As arthropods, both trilobites and horseshoe crabs have segmented bodies, joints in their legs, and hard exoskeletons, kind of like shells. So we have known for years that trilobites had two compound eyes. There are different kinds of compound eyes, but for many trilobites, it meant that their eyes had thousands of tiny lenses. This is helpful for detecting motion, like noticing other creatures swimming around. Other types of compound eyes provided, say, sharper images. But having thousands of lenses was most common for trilobites. But in a recent study, researchers examined a trilobite fossil that was damaged. Part of its head was missing. This allowed them to notice, in the middle of the trilobite's forehead, three tiny dark spots. They said, hmm, these do not seem random. In fact, the tiny spots are evidence of a median eye, that is, a third eye. Most arthropods have median eyes, which are not really like compound eyes. They are simpler. But a median eye had never been found in trilobites before. Why? Well, researchers had believed it was only there during the larval stage, early in the development of a young trilobite, so researchers thought adult fossils would not have it. But it would have been hidden underneath a thin, dark layer of shell, which was missing in this fossil. So you would not see it in a fossil whose entire head was intact.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段生物学课的讲座。

男：三叶虫是一类古代海洋生物。归入节肢动物。现已灭绝。在现代动物中，鲎大概最像三叶虫。作为节肢动物，三叶虫与鲎都有分节身体、腿关节与硬外骨骼，有点像壳。我们多年已知三叶虫有两只复眼。复眼有不同类型，但对许多三叶虫而言，意味着眼睛有数千微小晶状体。这有助于探测运动，比如察觉周围游动的其他生物。其他类型复眼则提供更清晰的图像之类。但拥有数千晶状体对三叶虫最常见。最近一项研究中，研究者检查了一块受损的三叶虫化石。头部一部分缺失。这让他们注意到三叶虫前额中央有三个微小暗斑。他们说，嗯，这些似乎不是随机的。实际上，小斑点是中眼的证据，也就是第三只眼。多数节肢动物有中眼，与复眼并不相同，更简单。但三叶虫中此前从未发现中眼。为什么？研究者曾以为它只存在于幼体阶段，即幼年三叶虫发育早期，因此认为成体化石不会有。但它本会被藏在一层薄而暗的壳下，而这件化石缺失了那层壳。所以头部完整的化石上你看不到它。

transcriptSentences.textZh: 但在最近一项研究中，研究者检查了一块受损的三叶虫化石。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Part of its head was missing.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它的头部有一部分缺失。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: This allowed them to notice, in the middle of the trilobite's forehead, three tiny dark spots.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这让他们注意到，在三叶虫前额中央有三个微小暗斑。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: They said, hmm, these do not seem random.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 他们说，嗯，这些似乎不是随机的。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: In fact, the tiny spots are evidence of a median eye, that is, a third eye.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 实际上，这些小斑点是中眼的证据，也就是第三只眼。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Most arthropods have median eyes, which are not really like compound eyes.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 多数节肢动物都有中眼，它们并不真正像复眼。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: They are simpler.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 中眼更简单。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: But a median eye had never been found in trilobites before.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但三叶虫中此前从未发现过中眼。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Why?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 为什么？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Well, researchers had believed it was only there during the larval stage, early in the development of a young trilobite, so researchers thought adult fossils would not have it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 研究者曾以为它只存在于幼体阶段，也就是幼年三叶虫发育早期，因此认为成体化石不会有。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: But it would have been hidden underneath a thin, dark layer of shell, which was missing in this fossil.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但它本会被藏在一层薄而暗的壳下，而这件化石缺失了那层壳。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: So you would not see it in a fossil whose entire head was intact.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 所以头部完整的化石上你看不到它。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on an art podcast.

Woman: Humans have been expressing themselves through art for thousands of years. Consider ancient cave paintings that have been discovered throughout the world, some of them more than 40,000 years old. Caves in Sulawesi, Indonesia, that include figurative art are an example of this. Some forms of art, though, have much more recent origins. Take, for example, decalcomania, a really cool art technique that originated in the eighteenth century. So what is decalcomania? At its core, it is a simple process. You begin by spreading paint onto a surface, like a sheet of paper. Then you press another surface, let's say canvas, onto the paper. So you press the two surfaces together. At this point, you pull them apart while the paint is still wet. The resulting image is often rich with organic abstract patterns. Decalcomania was first used to decorate pottery in the eighteenth century, but it really took off in the twentieth century, especially with the Surrealist movement. Artists like Max Ernst loved this technique because it helped them tap into the subconscious and explore the unexpected. Ernst was enchanted by the process that allowed him to create shapes that the artist could not fully control. What's especially intriguing about decalcomania is the balance it strikes between control and chaos. Sure, the artist chooses the colors and the materials, but once the process is complete, the final result is mostly up to chance.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段艺术播客的讲座。

女：人类通过艺术表达自我已有数千年。想想世界各地发现的古代洞穴壁画，有些超过四万年。印度尼西亚苏拉威西含具象艺术的洞穴即是一例。不过有些艺术形式起源近得多。例如印花转印法，一种源于十八世纪的很酷技法。什么是印花转印法？核心上过程简单。先把颜料涂在一个表面，比如一张纸。再把另一表面——比如画布——压到纸上。两表面压合。此时趁颜料未干把它们拉开。所得图像常充满有机抽象图案。印花转印法十八世纪先用于装饰陶器，但真正兴起在二十世纪，尤其随超现实主义运动。马克斯·恩斯特等艺术家热爱此法，因它助他们触及潜意识、探索意外。恩斯特着迷于让他创造出艺术家无法完全控制的形状的过程。印花转印法特别引人入胜之处在于控制与混沌之间的平衡。当然，艺术家选择颜色与材料，但过程完成后，最终结果多半取决于偶然。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a science podcast.

Woman: The study of bioacoustics is a fascinating field that explores how living organisms produce and perceive sound. Bioacoustics encompasses a wide range of topics, from the songs of whales and birds to the communication methods of insects. Understanding these sounds can provide insights into animal behavior and even aid in conservation efforts. For example, researchers have utilized bioacoustics to monitor whale populations. By recording and analyzing whale songs, scientists can track their movements and estimate population sizes. This information is vital for creating effective conservation strategies. Similarly, studying bird songs helps ornithologists understand mating rituals and territorial behavior. These acoustic signals are often complex and specific to each species, providing a wealth of information about their social structures. Insects also use sounds for communication, particularly during mating. The chirping of crickets and buzzing of bees are examples of how bioacoustics plays a role in their life cycles. Despite its benefits, bioacoustics research faces challenges. The equipment needed for recording and analyzing sounds can be expensive and requires specialized knowledge to operate. Additionally, environmental noise such as traffic, machinery, or even wind can interfere with the clarity of recordings, making it difficult to study certain species. Nonetheless, advancements in technology continue to improve the capabilities of bioacoustics, making it an invaluable tool for studying and protecting wildlife.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段科学播客的讲座。

女：生物声学是探索生物如何产生与感知声音的迷人领域。生物声学涵盖广泛议题，从鲸与鸟的歌声到昆虫的交流方式。理解这些声音可洞察动物行为，甚至助力保护工作。例如，研究者已用生物声学监测鲸种群。通过录制分析鲸歌，科学家可追踪其移动并估计种群规模。这些信息对制定有效保护策略至关重要。同样，研究鸟鸣帮助鸟类学家理解求偶仪式与领地行为。这些声学信号往往复杂且物种特异，提供关于其社会结构的丰富信息。昆虫也用声音交流，尤其在交配时。蟋蟀鸣叫与蜜蜂嗡嗡是生物声学在其生命周期中起作用的例子。尽管有益，生物声学研究面临挑战。录音与分析所需设备可能昂贵，并需专门知识操作。此外，交通、机械甚至风等环境噪声会干扰录音清晰度，使某些物种难以研究。尽管如此，技术进步继续提升生物声学能力，使其成为研究与保护野生动物的宝贵工具。

versions.label: Koala 03-05
versions.transcript: The study of bioacoustics is a fascinating field that explores how living organisms produce and perceive sound. Bioacoustics encompasses a wide range of topics, from the songs of whales and birds to the communication methods of insects. Understanding these sounds can provide insights into animal behaviour and even aid in conservation efforts. For example, researchers have utilized bioacoustics to monitor whale populations. By recording and analyzing whale songs, scientists can track their movements and estimate population sizes. This information is vital for creating effective conservation strategies. Similarly, studying bird songs helps ornithologists understand mating rituals in territory establishment. These acoustic signals are often complex and specific to each species, providing a wealth of information about their social structures. Insects 2 use sounds for communication, particularly during mating. The chirping of crickets and buzzing of bees are examples of how bioacoustics plays a role in their life cycles. Despite its benefits, bioacoustics research faces challenges. The equipment needed for recording and analyzing sounds can be expensive and requires specialized knowledge to operate. Additionally, environmental noise such as traffic, machinery or even wind can interfere with the clarity of recordings, making it difficult to study certain species. Nonetheless, advancements in technology continue to improve the capabilities of bioacoustics, making it an invaluable tool for studying and protecting wildlife.
versions.transcriptZh: 生物声学研究是一个引人入胜的领域，它探索生物如何产生和感知声音。 生物声学涵盖了广泛的主题，从鲸鱼和鸟类的鸣叫到昆虫的交流方式。 了解这些声音可以让我们深入了解动物的行为，甚至有助于保护工作。 例如，研究人员已利用生物声学来监测鲸鱼种群。 通过记录和分析鲸鱼的歌声，科学家们可以追踪它们的活动并估算种群规模。 这些信息对于制定有效的保护策略至关重要。 同样，研究鸟鸣有助于鸟类学家了解领地建立中的求偶仪式。 这些声学信号通常非常复杂且具有物种特异性，提供了有关其社会结构的大量信息。 昆虫也利用声音进行交流，尤其是在交配期间。 蟋蟀的鸣叫和蜜蜂的嗡嗡声都是生物声学在其生命周期中发挥作用的例子。 尽管生物声学研究有很多益处，但它也面临着挑战。 录制和分析声音所需的设备可能非常昂贵，并且需要专门的操作知识。 此外，交通、机械甚至风等环境噪音可能会干扰录音的清晰度，使得研究某些物种变得困难。 尽管如此，技术的进步不断提高生物声学的能力，使其成为研究和保护野生动物的宝贵工具。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in a psychology class. Have you ever been so engrossed in a task that you completely missed something obvious? This is called inattentional blindness, a phenomenon where concentrating on one thing can make us overlook something happening right in front of us. A classic study illustrates this perfectly. Participants watched a video of people passing a basketball and were asked to count passes made by players in white shirts. Midway through the video, a person in a gorilla suit walked into the scene, thumped its chest and left. Astonishingly, about half the viewers never saw the gorilla. Their attention was locked on counting passes. In real world situations, inattentional blindness can have serious consequences. For example, while driving, focusing on finding a street sign might make you miss a pedestrian stepping into the road. Recognizing this tendency can help us stay safer and more aware. Interestingly, psychologists trace this phenomenon to a useful ability, selective attention. This is the brain's way of filtering sensory input to avoid overload, allowing us to concentrate on important tasks. Think about sitting in a noisy open plan office writing a report. Phones are ringing, people are talking, but you manage to tune it all out and focus on your work. That's selective attention at its best.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段心理学课的讲座。你是否曾如此专注于一项任务，以至于完全错过眼前明显的事物？这叫无意视盲：专注一件事会让我们忽略正发生在眼前的另一件事。一项经典研究完美说明了这一点。参与者观看人们传篮球的视频，并被要求数白衣球员的传球次数。视频中途，一个穿大猩猩服装的人走进画面，捶胸后离开。令人吃惊的是，约一半观众从未看见大猩猩。他们的注意力锁在数传球上。现实中，无意视盲可有严重后果。例如开车时，专注找路牌可能让你错过走上马路的行人。认识这种倾向有助于我们更安全、更警觉。有趣的是，心理学家把这一现象追溯到一种有用能力：选择性注意。这是大脑过滤感觉输入以免过载的方式，让我们能专注重要任务。想想坐在嘈杂开放式办公室写报告。电话响、有人说话，你却能全部屏蔽、专注工作。那就是选择性注意的最佳状态。

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an environmental science class. Some years ago, the government of Tanzania in Africa proposed building a 452 kilometer paved road in the north of the country, with the goal of boosting transportation and economic growth. The proposed route, though, would go through Serengeti National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and conservationists raised alarms. The road would bisect the annual migration corridor of wildebeests and other animals, potentially putting enormous pressure on their populations and disrupting the ecosystem in general. The models used by the conservationists showed that blocking the corridor with the road could reduce wildebeest populations by up to one third, disrupt predator prey dynamics and fragment an ecosystem that supports lions, cheetahs and countless other species. Increased traffic would also heighten poaching risks and introduce invasive species. The evidence wasn't conclusive, but because the risk was so serious and the consequences probably irreversible, the government decided to halt the project. That decision reflects what's known as the precautionary principle. When an action or policy poses a plausible risk of serious or irreversible harm, we shouldn't wait for absolute scientific certainty before deciding what to do. Why is this important? The consequences of indecision can be expensive or impossible to repair. Consider asbestos, once a widely used material for insulation and fire proofing, it was later linked to life threatening adverse effects on human health. But for decades, lack of consensus among researchers delayed government action, and by the time bans on asbestos were enacted, millions had been exposed, leading to costly litigation, clean up and preventable deaths.

versions.transcript: Listen to a lecture in a music class. If you're familiar with ancient Greece, you know how important music was in everyday life. You can probably imagine people sitting in a Greek amphitheater, completely absorbed by the sounds filling the air. But music wasn't only heard in theater performances. It played a role in all kinds of settings, including religious ceremonies and athletic competitions. One instrument that stands out is the aulos. This aulos is a double reeded wind instrument that was a big part of Greek musical life, and it has a distinctive design. It has two pipes, each with a reed, usually made from a plant, similar to what you'd find in a modern oboe. And because the pipes are cylindrical, not conical like some other wind instruments, it produces a sound that's rich and sharp. That unique sound helped bring out emotion in plays and public events, which brought depth to the drama unfolding on stage. To really master the aulos, the player had to be highly skilled. One technique they used was circular breathing. It means inhaling air through the nose while simultaneously pushing air out through the cheeks. This allowed them to play long, continuous passages without stopping for breath. Even though the aulos was hugely important in ancient times, it eventually faded from use as other instruments and musical styles took over. Still, its legacy lives on as it gives us a glimpse into the musical world of ancient Greece.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段音乐课的讲座。若你熟悉古希腊，就知道音乐在日常生活中有多重要。你大概能想象人们坐在希腊露天剧场，完全沉浸在弥漫的声音里。但音乐不只出现在戏剧演出。它在各种场合起作用，包括宗教仪式与体育竞赛。一种突出的乐器是双管箫 aulos。这种 aulos 是双簧管乐器，在希腊音乐生活中地位重要，设计独特。它有两根管子，各有一簧片，通常用植物制成，类似现代双簧管上的簧。因为管子是圆柱形，不像某些管乐器那样锥形，它发出浓郁而锐利的声音。那种独特音色帮助在戏剧与公共活动中带出情感，为舞台上展开的戏剧增添深度。要真正掌握 aulos，演奏者必须技艺高超。他们使用的一种技巧是循环呼吸：用鼻子吸气的同时用面颊把空气推出。这使他们能演奏长而连续的乐段而不停下来换气。尽管 aulos 在古代极为重要，随着其他乐器与音乐风格兴起，它最终淡出使用。但其遗产仍在，因为它让我们一窥古希腊的音乐世界。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a psychology podcast.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a psychology podcast. There are many different factors that influence human behaviour. One is related to social influence, or the idea that our behaviour can be shaped by group pressure. To test this idea, a psychologist named Solomon Asch conducted a famous study in the 1950s, which has become hugely influential in the field. In his experiment, Asch invited American University students to take part in a simple visual judgement task. Each participant was placed in a group of seven to nine people, all but one of whom were working with the researcher. The group members were shown a standard line on one card and three comparison lines on another card. One comparison line matched the standard, while the other two were clearly different lengths. Basically, the correct choice was totally obvious. Each person announced aloud which line matched the standard, and those who were in on the study deliberately gave the wrong answer first. The real participant answered last. Across 12 trials, 75% of participants conformed with the incorrect answers that people in the group had given before them at least once, so they chose the line that was clearly wrong. This indicates strong influence of group pressure. This study was replicated in 1980, roughly 30 years after Asch conducted his experiment. The subjects in this experiment were British university students. Interestingly, conformity was much lower with these participants. This suggests that conformity may be influenced by culture and the country people grow up in.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段心理学播客的讲座。影响人类行为的因素很多。其一与社会影响有关，即我们的行为可被群体压力塑造。为检验这一想法，心理学家所罗门·阿希在一九五〇年代做了一项著名研究，对该领域影响巨大。实验中，阿希邀请美国大学学生参加简单的视觉判断任务。每位参与者被放入七到九人的小组，除一人外其余都与研究者合作。小组成员看到一张卡片上的标准线与另一张上的三条比较线。一条比较线与标准线匹配，另两条长度明显不同。基本上正确选择完全显而易见。每人出声宣布哪条线匹配标准，知情者故意先给出错误答案。真正的参与者最后回答。在十二次试验中，百分之七十五的参与者至少一次从众于组内前人给出的错误答案，因此选了明显错误的线。这表明群体压力影响强烈。该研究在一九八〇年被复制，大约在阿希实验三十年后。受试是英国大学生。有趣的是，这些参与者的从众率低得多。这提示从众可能受文化与人们成长国家影响。

transcriptSentences.text: Listen to a talk on a psychology podcast.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 请听一段心理学播客的讲座。

transcriptSentences.text: There are many different factors that influence human behaviour.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 影响人类行为的因素很多。

transcriptSentences.text: One is related to social influence, or the idea that our behaviour can be shaped by group pressure.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 其一与社会影响有关，即我们的行为可被群体压力塑造。

transcriptSentences.text: To test this idea, a psychologist named Solomon Asch conducted a famous study in the 1950s, which has become hugely influential in the field.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 为检验这一想法，心理学家所罗门·阿希在一九五〇年代做了一项著名研究，对该领域影响巨大。

transcriptSentences.text: In his experiment, Asch invited American University students to take part in a simple visual judgement task.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 实验中，阿希邀请美国大学学生参加简单的视觉判断任务。

transcriptSentences.text: Each participant was placed in a group of seven to nine people, all but one of whom were working with the researcher.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 每位参与者被放入七到九人的小组，除一人外其余都与研究者合作。

transcriptSentences.text: The group members were shown a standard line on one card and three comparison lines on another card.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 小组成员看到一张卡片上的标准线与另一张上的三条比较线。

transcriptSentences.text: One comparison line matched the standard, while the other two were clearly different lengths.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 一条比较线与标准线匹配，另两条长度明显不同。

transcriptSentences.text: Basically, the correct choice was totally obvious.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 基本上正确选择完全显而易见。

transcriptSentences.text: Each person announced aloud which line matched the standard, and those who were in on the study deliberately gave the wrong answer first.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 每人出声宣布哪条线匹配标准，知情者故意先给出错误答案。

transcriptSentences.text: The real participant answered last.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 真正的参与者最后回答。

transcriptSentences.text: Across 12 trials, 75% of participants conformed with the incorrect answers that people in the group had given before them at least once, so they chose the line that was clearly wrong.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 在十二次试验中，百分之七十五的参与者至少一次从众于组内前人给出的错误答案，因此选了明显错误的线。

transcriptSentences.text: This indicates strong influence of group pressure.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这表明群体压力影响强烈。

transcriptSentences.text: This study was replicated in 1980, roughly 30 years after Asch conducted his experiment.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 该研究在一九八〇年被复制，大约在阿希实验三十年后。

transcriptSentences.text: The subjects in this experiment were British university students.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 受试是英国大学生。

transcriptSentences.text: Interestingly, conformity was much lower with these participants.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 有趣的是，这些参与者的从众率低得多。

transcriptSentences.text: This suggests that conformity may be influenced by culture and the country people grow up in.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这提示从众可能受文化与人们成长国家影响。

questions.promptText: What was the main purpose of Solomon Asch's experiment?
questions.promptTextZh: 所罗门·阿希实验的主要目的是什么？

choices.label: To measure memory skills of university students
choices.labelZh: 测量大学生的记忆能力
choices.explanationZh: 实验是 visual judgment + group pressure，不是 memory。

choices.label: To study the effect of social pressure on behavior
choices.labelZh: 研究社会压力对行为的影响
choices.explanationZh: 正确：speaker 明确说 To test this idea，即 group pressure shaping behaviour。

choices.label: To compare visual judgments across cultures
choices.labelZh: 比较不同文化背景下的视觉判断
choices.explanationZh: 跨文化比较来自后来的 1980 replication，不是 Asch 原实验主要目的。

choices.label: To determine study habits of university students
choices.labelZh: 确定大学生的学习习惯
choices.explanationZh: 没有 study habits。

questions.promptText: What were the participants in Asch's study asked to do?
questions.promptTextZh: 阿希研究中的参与者被要求做什么？

choices.label: Compare the lengths of different lines
choices.labelZh: 比较不同线条的长度
choices.explanationZh: 正确：participants completed a visual judgement task comparing a standard line with comparison lines。

choices.label: Draw lines on a card
choices.labelZh: 在卡片上画线
choices.explanationZh: 他们是判断线段，不是画线。

choices.label: Work with a group to solve a problem
choices.labelZh: 与团队合作解决问题
choices.explanationZh: 他们在 group 中回答，但不是合作解题。

choices.label: Match words from two different lists
choices.labelZh: 将两个不同列表中的单词进行匹配
choices.explanationZh: 没有 word lists。

questions.promptText: What was Asch's main finding about the majority of participants in his study?
questions.promptTextZh: 阿希关于其研究中大多数参与者的主要发现是什么？

choices.label: They could not solve complex problems without help from others.
choices.labelZh: 没有他人帮助，他们无法解决复杂问题。
choices.explanationZh: 任务很简单且答案 obvious，不是 complex problem。

choices.label: They thought for a long time before answering a simple question.
choices.labelZh: 回答简单问题前，他们会思考很长时间。
choices.explanationZh: 没有讨论思考时间。

choices.label: They used a variety of different strategies to solve a problem.
choices.labelZh: 他们使用多种不同的策略来解决问题。
choices.explanationZh: 没有说策略。

choices.label: They gave incorrect answers to match the answers of others at least once.
choices.labelZh: 他们至少有一次为了与他人的答案一致而给出了错误答案。
choices.explanationZh: 正确：75% conformed with incorrect answers at least once。

questions.promptText: What difference between the Asch study and the study conducted in 1980 does the speaker discuss?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者讨论了阿希研究与1980年进行的研究之间的哪个区别？

choices.label: The number of participants in each group
choices.labelZh: 每组参与者的数量
choices.explanationZh: 没有比较 group size。

choices.label: The number of times participants answered questions
choices.labelZh: 参与者回答问题的次数
choices.explanationZh: 没有比较 trials 数量。

choices.label: The cultural background of the participants
choices.labelZh: 参与者的文化背景
choices.explanationZh: 正确：Asch 是 American students，1980 是 British university students，并讨论 culture。

choices.label: The difficulty of the questions being answered
choices.labelZh: 所回答问题的难度
choices.explanationZh: 问题难度没有被比较。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a history class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class.

Man: Let's talk about how ideas and values are transmitted across national borders, leading to an increasingly interconnected world. This process, known as cultural globalization, has been going on for millennia, but it has been accelerated by advancements in communication technology and transportation. Certainly, one of the most visible aspects of cultural globalization is the spread of popular culture. Music, fashion, and food from one part of the world often become popular in other regions. American films, for instance, are watched worldwide, and American fast-food chains are found in numerous countries as well. This diffusion of culture can lead to greater cultural understanding and exchange, fostering a sense of global community. However, it also raises concerns about the erosion of local cultures and identities. The dominance of Western culture, in particular, can overshadow indigenous traditions and practices, leading to worldwide cultural homogenization. This can result in a loss of cultural diversity, as unique customs and languages may fade away. There's also the issue of cultural appropriation. Cultural appropriation occurs when elements of a culture are taken and used by another, often without understanding or respect. On the other hand, cultural globalization can empower local cultures by providing a platform for them to reach a global audience. Social media, for example, allows artists and creators from diverse backgrounds to share their work with a worldwide audience. Understanding cultural globalization involves recognizing both its benefits and its drawbacks, and finding ways to preserve cultural diversity while embracing global interconnectedness.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段历史课的讲座。

男：我们谈观念与价值如何跨越国界传播，导致日益互联的世界。这一过程称为文化全球化，已进行数千年，但因通信技术与交通进步而加速。当然，文化全球化最可见的方面之一是流行文化的传播。世界一地的音乐、时尚与食物常在其他地区流行。例如美国电影在全球被观看，美国快餐连锁也遍布众多国家。这种文化扩散可带来更大文化理解与交流，培育全球共同体感。但它也引发对本地文化与身份侵蚀的担忧。尤其西方文化的主导可遮蔽原住民传统与实践，导致全球文化同质化。这可造成文化多样性丧失，因独特习俗与语言可能消逝。还有文化挪用问题。文化挪用指一种文化的元素被另一文化拿来使用，常缺乏理解或尊重。另一方面，文化全球化也可赋能本地文化，为它们提供触及全球受众的平台。例如社交媒体让多元背景的艺术家与创作者与全世界观众分享作品。理解文化全球化既要认识其益处与弊端，也要找到在拥抱全球互联的同时保护文化多样性的方法。

questions.promptText: What is the main topic of the talk?
questions.promptTextZh: 讲座的主要主题是什么？

choices.label: The spreading of culture across international borders and its impact
choices.labelZh: 文化跨越国际边界的传播及其影响
choices.explanationZh: 正确。开头定义 cultural globalization 为 ideas and values across borders，后面讲 benefits and drawbacks。

choices.label: Reasons for the transmission of Western culture across the world
choices.labelZh: 西方文化在全球传播的原因
choices.explanationZh: Western culture dominance 是 concern 之一，不是主旨。

choices.label: The role played by modern technology in connecting different cultures
choices.labelZh: 现代技术在连接不同文化中所扮演的角色
choices.explanationZh: technology 是加速因素，不是整段主题。

choices.label: The potentially negative effects of cultural globalization
choices.labelZh: 文化全球化的潜在负面影响
choices.explanationZh: 负面影响只占一部分，原文也讲 greater understanding 和 global audience。

choices.label: They sometimes depict foreign cultures inaccurately.
choices.labelZh: 它们有时会不准确地描绘外国文化。
choices.explanationZh: 没有说美国电影描绘外国文化不准。

choices.label: They frequently include elements of cultures found outside the United States.
choices.labelZh: 它们经常包含美国以外的文化元素。
choices.explanationZh: 没有说美国电影常包含外国文化元素。

choices.label: They are an example of how a country's culture is spread across the world.
choices.labelZh: 它们是一个国家文化传播到世界各地的例子。
choices.explanationZh: 正确。American films are watched worldwide 是 popular culture spread 的例子。

choices.label: They are more popular outside the United States than within it.
choices.labelZh: 它们在美国以外比在美国国内更受欢迎。
choices.explanationZh: 没有比较国内外受欢迎程度。

questions.promptText: Why does the speaker talk about cultural appropriation?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者为什么谈到文化挪用？

choices.label: To highlight a common benefit of cultural exchange
choices.labelZh: 为了强调文化交流的一个常见好处
choices.explanationZh: cultural appropriation 是风险，不是好处。

choices.label: To present one of the concerns associated with cultural globalization
choices.labelZh: 为了提出与文化全球化相关的一个担忧
choices.explanationZh: 正确。原文把 appropriation 放在 raises concerns 后，说明全球化的担忧之一。

choices.label: To emphasize the importance of social media in spreading a country's culture
choices.labelZh: 为了强调社交媒体在传播一国文化方面的重要性
choices.explanationZh: social media 是赋能本地文化的例子，不是 appropriation 的目的。

choices.label: To explain how people from different cultures come to respect one another
choices.labelZh: 为了解释来自不同文化的人们如何学会相互尊重
choices.explanationZh: appropriation 常是 without understanding or respect，和互相尊重相反。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker suggest about social media?
questions.promptTextZh: 关于社交媒体，演讲者提出了什么看法？

choices.label: It is widely recognized as a primary driver of the dominance of Western culture.
choices.labelZh: 它被广泛认为是西方文化主导地位的主要驱动力。
choices.explanationZh: dominance of Western culture 是另一个 concern，未说 social media 是主因。

choices.label: It can lead to cultural homogenization if not regulated.
choices.labelZh: 如果不加以监管，它可能导致文化同质化。
choices.explanationZh: 没有说不监管就 homogenization。

choices.label: It provides a convenient platform for local cultures to gain global exposure.
choices.labelZh: 它为地方文化走向全球提供了一个便捷的平台。
choices.explanationZh: 正确。原文说 social media allows artists and creators from diverse backgrounds to share with a worldwide audience。

choices.label: It is the primary vehicle for spreading movies, music, and fashion from one country to another.
choices.labelZh: 它是将电影、音乐和时尚从一个国家传播到另一个国家的主要载体。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a science class.

Man: Today, I want to tell you about an unusual phenomenon that scientists noticed in the Pacific Ocean in the early 1990s. The scientists were recording sounds using hydrophones positioned on the ocean floor in the North Pacific. Hydrophones are specially designed microphones that allow scientists to collect acoustic data underwater. While most of the undersea noises picked up by the hydrophones came from whales, ships' engines, or earthquakes, the scientists monitoring the hydrophones detected a number of sounds that they could not identify. One was a regular series of rising infrasonic tones, that is, very low-frequency sounds below what humans can hear. The scientists labeled these very low-frequency noises "upsweep." At first, these sounds were thought to be the songs of whales migrating in the Pacific. However, scientists who study whale acoustics eventually ruled out this possibility, and the origin of the upsweep sounds remained unknown. So, what is the source of the rising tones detected by the hydrophones? The sounds were ultimately tracked to an area of inferred volcanic seismic activity in a chain of undersea mountains in the South Pacific. Some scientists believe that if these mountains contain an active volcano, the source for the mysterious sounds may be hot volcanic lava coming into contact with cold seawater.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a film class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a film class.

You're familiar with documentaries. Non-fiction films that use things like interviews and news footage to tell a true story. Of course, they're likely to show the filmmaker's perspective. If the filmmaker has an ax to grind, that's the version of the story you'll learn. So, it's important to use caution before being too credulous about what you see in one. Documentaries have become much more popular over the last several years. It seems like every streaming service is showing them, and all the streaming services seem to be creating their own. One from a few years back called My Octopus Teacher was recognized for its high production value. My Octopus Teacher had a team of camera operators, editors, plus a compelling story and great music. On the other hand, we have ethnographic films. These are also non-fiction, but unlike documentaries, ethnographic films don't have such elaborate production. They're non-fiction films about people, particular cultures around the world. Forest of Bliss is one. Um, Forest of Bliss is about daily life in a city in India. Now, researchers making ethnographic films might spend years living within a particular cultural group. This way, they learn about the everyday life of its people and integrate into the group. This enables them to make ethnographic films. They're more like research films than movies. They're not likely to have dramatic music or cinematography. Instead, they'll focus on everyday life and show the complexity of life while not trying to tell one particular story.

请听一段电影课的讲座。

你熟悉纪录片。用访谈与新闻素材等讲述真实故事的非虚构影片。当然，它们很可能展现电影人的视角。若电影人有一己之见要推销，你就会学到那个版本的故事。因此在对所看到的过于轻信之前保持谨慎很重要。纪录片在过去几年变得更受欢迎。似乎每个流媒体都在放，而且所有流媒体似乎都在制作自己的。几年前一部叫《我的章鱼老师》的因其高制作水准而获认可。《我的章鱼老师》有摄制、剪辑团队，加上引人入胜的故事与出色音乐。另一方面，我们有民族志电影。它们也是非虚构，但与纪录片不同，民族志电影没有如此精心的制作。它们是关于人、关于世界各地特定文化的非虚构影片。《极乐之林》就是一部。嗯，《极乐之林》关于印度一座城市的日常生活。制作民族志电影的研究者可能花数年生活在特定文化群体中。这样他们了解其人民的日常生活并融入该群体。这使他们能够制作民族志电影。它们更像研究片而非电影。它们不太可能有戏剧性音乐或摄影。相反，它们聚焦日常生活，展现生活的复杂性，同时不试图讲述某一个特定故事。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an economics class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an economics class. Imagine that you have a full-time job, but you want to take a year off to go back to school. What is it going to cost you? Of course, there's the cost of tuition for your classes plus living expenses, but what about the money you're no longer earning at your job because you're now a student? We call that the opportunity cost. Opportunity cost refers to the value of the next best alternative that must be given up when making a choice. It's a fundamental principle in economics that helps individuals and businesses understand the true cost of their decisions. My exercise in imagination illustrates a personal decision, but businesses also face opportunity costs in their operations. For instance, a company may choose to invest in new equipment rather than spend money to expand its product line. The opportunity cost of this decision is the potential revenue that could have been generated from the new products. Understanding opportunity cost helps individuals as well as businesses make informed decisions that maximize their benefits and minimize their losses. It's important to note that opportunity cost is not always measured in financial terms. It can also be related to factors like time, convenience, or personal satisfaction. For that reason, opportunity cost can be difficult to quantify, especially when dealing with non-monetary factors. Have you ever had to make a decision that included an opportunity cost? Take a few minutes now to think, and then I'll ask for volunteers to share.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段经济学课的讲座。想象你有一份全职工作，但想休一年假回学校。这会让你付出什么代价？当然有课程学费加生活开销，但你因现在是学生而不再从工作中挣到的钱呢？我们称之为机会成本。机会成本指做选择时必须放弃的次优备选方案的价值。它是经济学的基本原则，帮助个人与企业理解其决策的真实成本。我的想象练习说明的是个人决策，但企业运营中也面临机会成本。例如，公司可能选择投资新设备，而不是花钱扩展产品线。这一决策的机会成本是本可从新产品产生的潜在收入。理解机会成本帮助个人与企业做出知情决策，以最大化收益、最小化损失。重要的是，机会成本并不总以金钱衡量。它也可与时间、便利或个人满足等因素相关。因此，机会成本可能难以量化，尤其涉及非货币因素时。你是否曾做包含机会成本的决策？现在花几分钟想想，然后我会请志愿者分享。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a lecture in an art history class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a lecture in an art history class. Let's talk about a classic example of land art: Spiral Jetty by Robert Smithson. Picture yourself at the edge of the Great Salt Lake in the state of Utah in the United States. Stretching out into the water is a massive spiral made of dark basalt rocks, about 1,500 feet long. The title tells you a lot. A jetty is a structure that sticks out into a body of water, usually to protect a shoreline or dock. Smithson took that idea and twisted it, literally, into a spiral. Land art is an art movement that wanted to break free from museums and galleries and put art directly into nature. Smithson was fascinated by big concepts like geological time and change. He never intended Spiral Jetty to be permanent. The lake rises and falls, salt crystals form on the rocks, and the spiral slowly transforms. He wanted people to experience that reality firsthand, to make the journey and see the work in its natural setting. Here's the irony though: relatively few people have actually seen Spiral Jetty firsthand. Most people know it only through photographs and films that have been made about it. All this undermines Smithson's idea because the work is supposedly about being there, about sensing its scale and its shifting relationship with the Great Salt Lake. When we only see pictures, it becomes a static image, raising questions about whether land art, or at least this particular example of land art, can actually ever fulfill its intent.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段艺术史课的讲座。我们来谈大地艺术的经典例子：罗伯特·史密森的《螺旋防波堤》。想象自己站在美国犹他州大盐湖边。伸入水中的是由深色玄武岩堆成的巨大螺旋，约一千五百英尺长。标题本身信息很多。防波堤是伸入水体的结构，通常用来保护岸线或码头。史密森把这个概念拿来，字面意义上扭成了螺旋。大地艺术是一场想摆脱博物馆与画廊、把艺术直接放进自然的艺术运动。史密森着迷于地质时间与变化这类大概念。他从未打算让《螺旋防波堤》永恒不变。湖水涨落，盐晶在岩石上形成，螺旋缓慢变形。他希望人们亲身体验这种现实，专程前往，在自然环境中看作品。讽刺的是：真正亲眼见过《螺旋防波堤》的人相对很少。多数人只通过相关照片与影片认识它。这一切削弱了史密森的理念，因为作品本应关乎身临其境，关乎感受其尺度以及与大盐湖不断变化的关系。我们若只看图片，它就变成静止图像，从而提出疑问：大地艺术，至少这个具体例子，是否真能实现其意图。
