transcriptSentences.textZh: 我们来谈大地艺术的经典例子：罗伯特·史密森的《螺旋防波堤》。

transcriptSentences.text: Picture yourself at the edge of the Great Salt Lake in the state of Utah in the United States.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 想象自己站在美国犹他州大盐湖边。

transcriptSentences.text: Stretching out into the water is a massive spiral made of dark basalt rocks, about 1,500 feet long.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 伸入水中的是由深色玄武岩堆成的巨大螺旋，约一千五百英尺长。

transcriptSentences.text: The title tells you a lot.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 标题本身信息很多。

transcriptSentences.text: A jetty is a structure that sticks out into a body of water, usually to protect a shoreline or dock.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 防波堤是伸入水体的结构，通常用来保护岸线或码头。

transcriptSentences.text: Smithson took that idea and twisted it, literally, into a spiral.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 史密森把这个概念拿来，字面意义上扭成了螺旋。

transcriptSentences.text: Land art is an art movement that wanted to break free from museums and galleries and put art directly into nature.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 大地艺术是一场想摆脱博物馆与画廊、把艺术直接放进自然的艺术运动。

transcriptSentences.text: Smithson was fascinated by big concepts like geological time and change.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 史密森着迷于地质时间与变化这类大概念。

transcriptSentences.text: He never intended Spiral Jetty to be permanent.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 他从未打算让《螺旋防波堤》永恒不变。

transcriptSentences.text: The lake rises and falls, salt crystals form on the rocks, and the spiral slowly transforms.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 湖水涨落，盐晶在岩石上形成，螺旋缓慢变形。

transcriptSentences.text: He wanted people to experience that reality firsthand, to make the journey and see the work in its natural setting.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 他希望人们亲身体验这种现实，专程前往，在自然环境中看作品。

transcriptSentences.text: Here's the irony though: relatively few people have actually seen Spiral Jetty firsthand.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 讽刺的是：真正亲眼见过《螺旋防波堤》的人相对很少。

transcriptSentences.text: Most people know it only through photographs and films that have been made about it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 多数人只通过相关照片与影片认识它。

transcriptSentences.text: All this undermines Smithson's idea because the work is supposedly about being there, about sensing its scale and its shifting relationship with the Great Salt Lake.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这一切削弱了史密森的理念，因为作品本应关乎身临其境，关乎感受其尺度以及与大盐湖不断变化的关系。

transcriptSentences.text: When we only see pictures, it becomes a static image, raising questions about whether land art, or at least this particular example of land art, can actually ever fulfill its intent.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 我们若只看图片，它就变成静止图像，从而提出疑问：大地艺术，至少这个具体例子，是否真能实现其意图。

questions.promptText: What is the location of the artwork by Robert Smithson that the speaker discusses?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者讨论的罗伯特·史密森的艺术品位于何处？

choices.label: A forest
choices.labelZh: 一片森林
choices.explanationZh: 作品在 Great Salt Lake 的水边，不是在森林。

choices.label: A lake
choices.labelZh: 一个湖泊
choices.explanationZh: 正确：speaker 明确说 Spiral Jetty 位于 Great Salt Lake 边，并伸入水中。

choices.label: A mountaintop
choices.labelZh: 一座山顶
choices.explanationZh: 讲座没有说作品在山顶；位置证据是 Great Salt Lake。

choices.label: A desert
choices.labelZh: 一片沙漠
choices.explanationZh: Utah 是地理背景，但具体位置是 lake，不是 desert。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker emphasize about the physical nature of Spiral Jetty?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者强调《螺旋形防波堤》在物理性质上的什么特点？

choices.label: It was constructed using materials meant to resist weathering.
choices.labelZh: 它使用了旨在抵抗风化的材料建造。
choices.explanationZh: 原文说 Smithson never intended it to be permanent，不是用抗风化材料保持不变。

choices.label: It was designed without consideration of its surrounding environment.
choices.labelZh: 它在设计时没有考虑其周围环境。
choices.explanationZh: 作品正是放在自然环境中，与 Great Salt Lake 的变化发生关系，不是忽略环境。

choices.label: It requires frequent human maintenance to preserve its form.
choices.labelZh: 它需要频繁的人工维护以保持其形状。
choices.explanationZh: 讲座没有提人工维护；它的变化来自 lake rises and falls、salt crystals 等自然过程。

choices.label: It is shaped by its ongoing interaction with its natural environment.
choices.labelZh: 它的形状是由其与自然环境持续的相互作用塑造的。
choices.explanationZh: 正确：speaker 说湖水涨落、盐晶形成、spiral slowly transforms，强调作品和自然环境持续互动。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker imply was Smithson's attitude toward art museums?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者暗示史密森对艺术博物馆持何种态度？

choices.label: He believed that they were the only way to give large numbers of people access to great art.
choices.labelZh: 他认为博物馆是让大量人群接触伟大艺术的唯一途径。
choices.explanationZh: Smithson 的 land art 想 break free from museums and galleries，和“只有博物馆能让大众接触艺术”相反。

choices.label: He felt that they were necessary to preserve artworks from the effects of time.
choices.labelZh: 他认为博物馆对于保存艺术品免受时间影响是必要的。
choices.explanationZh: 他没有追求保存作品不受时间影响；原文说他不想让 Spiral Jetty permanent。

choices.label: He felt that they limited people's experience of art.
choices.labelZh: 他认为博物馆限制了人们对艺术的体验。
choices.explanationZh: 正确：land art wanted to break free from museums and galleries and put art directly into nature，说明他认为博物馆限制了艺术体验。

choices.label: He believed that they should be located far from big cities.
choices.labelZh: 他认为博物馆应该建在远离大城市的地方。
choices.explanationZh: 讲座讨论的是艺术走出 museums and galleries，不是博物馆应该建在哪里。

questions.promptText: Why does the speaker mention that Spiral Jetty is mainly known through photographs and movies?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者为何提到《螺旋形防波堤》主要是通过照片和电影为人所知？

choices.label: To point out that Smithson was an artist of wide-ranging talents
choices.labelZh: 为了指出史密森是一位才华横溢的艺术家
choices.explanationZh: 照片和电影不是为了说明 Smithson 多才多艺，而是说明多数人没有现场体验作品。

choices.label: To emphasize the enormous fame that the work enjoys
choices.labelZh: 为了强调该作品享有的巨大声誉
choices.explanationZh: speaker 的重点不是名气大，而是这种传播方式 undermines Smithson’s idea。

choices.label: To introduce a criticism that is made of the work
choices.labelZh: 为了引入针对该作品的一种批评
choices.explanationZh: 正确：speaker 说这件事 undermines Smithson’s idea，并质疑 land art 是否能 fulfill its intent，是对作品实现方式的批评。

choices.label: To suggest that Smithson's views about Land Art changed since he created the work
choices.labelZh: 为了表明史密森自创作该作品以来对地景艺术的看法发生了变化
choices.explanationZh: 讲座没有说 Smithson 后来改变观点；问题在于观众通过静态图像认识作品。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on an economics podcast.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on an economics podcast.

Man: Today we are discussing behavioral economics, a fascinating field that explores how psychological factors influence economic decision making. Traditionally, economists assumed that individuals made rational choices. However, behavioral economics challenges this notion by demonstrating that people often behave irrationally because of cognitive biases and emotions. One classic example is the concept of loss aversion. Studies show that individuals tend to prefer avoiding losses rather than acquiring equivalent gains. For instance, losing 100 euros feels worse than gaining 100 euros feels good. This bias can lead to risk-averse behavior impacting consumer decisions. The risk of loss seems intolerable even when there is an equal or greater opportunity for gain. Another factor is present bias, where individuals disproportionately value immediate rewards over future benefits. This can make it hard to save for retirement and can lead people to overspend. Another behavior that economists examine is confirmation bias, where individuals favor information that confirms their pre-existing beliefs while disregarding contradictory data. Imagine a consumer who strongly believes that brand X makes the best smartphones. Because of confirmation bias, they might only seek out favorable reviews about brand X while ignoring negative ones. Even when presented with objective comparisons showing that another brand has better features or is more reliable, they will downplay that information.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段经济学播客的讲座。

男：今天我们讨论行为经济学，这门迷人领域探究心理因素如何影响经济决策。传统上，经济学家假定个体做出理性选择。但行为经济学挑战这一观念，证明人常因认知偏见与情绪而不理性行事。经典例子之一是损失厌恶概念。研究表明，个体往往更倾向避免损失，而非获得等量收益。例如，损失一百欧元的难受程度，超过获得一百欧元的愉悦。这种偏见可导致风险规避行为，影响消费决策。即便有同等或更大的获利机会，损失风险也显得难以忍受。另一因素是当下偏见：个体不成比例地看重即时回报而非未来收益。这会让为退休储蓄变难，并导致超支。经济学家还考察确认偏误：个体偏爱印证既有信念的信息，忽视矛盾数据。想象一个坚信 X 品牌手机最好的消费者。因确认偏误，他可能只找 X 品牌的好评而忽略差评。即便客观比较显示另一品牌功能更好或更可靠，他也会淡化那些信息。

questions.promptText: What is the main topic of the lecture?
questions.promptTextZh: 讲座的主要主题是什么？

choices.label: The history of classical economics
choices.labelZh: 古典经济学的历史
choices.explanationZh: classical economics 只是传统假设的对照，主讲不是经济学历史。

choices.label: The importance of retirement planning
choices.labelZh: 退休规划的重要性
choices.explanationZh: retirement planning 只是 present bias 的例子。

choices.label: Key concepts in behavioral economics
choices.labelZh: 行为经济学的核心概念
choices.explanationZh: 正确。全文介绍 behavioral economics，并讲 loss aversion、present bias、confirmation bias 三个概念。

choices.label: The benefits of online shopping
choices.labelZh: 网购的好处

questions.promptText: What behavior is associated with loss aversion?
questions.promptTextZh: 与损失厌恶相关的行为是什么？

choices.label: A willingness to try unfamiliar products
choices.labelZh: 愿意尝试不熟悉的产品
choices.explanationZh: 尝试不熟悉产品不是 loss aversion。

choices.label: A tendency to avoid risks
choices.labelZh: 倾向于规避风险

choices.label: An interest in saving money for retirement

choices.label: A focus on information that supports existing beliefs

questions.promptText: Why does the professor mention retirement?
questions.promptTextZh: 教授为何提到退休？

choices.label: To show how behavioral economics has changed over time
choices.labelZh: 为了展示行为经济学如何随时间演变
choices.explanationZh: retirement 不是用来说明 behavioral economics 的历史变化。

choices.label: To explain why some people dislike economic theory
choices.labelZh: 为了解释为什么有些人不喜欢经济理论
choices.explanationZh: 原文没有说人们不喜欢 economic theory。

choices.label: To give an example of present bias
choices.labelZh: 为了举例说明现在偏差
choices.explanationZh: 正确。人们重视眼前奖励而忽视未来收益，所以可能不为退休储蓄，这是 present bias。

choices.label: To describe a recent policy change
choices.labelZh: 为了描述最近的政策变化
choices.explanationZh: 原文没有提政策变化。

questions.promptText: Which behavior best illustrates confirmation bias?
questions.promptTextZh: 哪种行为最能说明确认偏差？

choices.label: Saving money regularly for retirement
choices.labelZh: 定期为退休存钱
choices.explanationZh: 定期为退休存钱不是 confirmation bias。

choices.label: Comparing two brands without a preference
choices.labelZh: 无偏见地比较两个品牌
choices.explanationZh: 没有既有偏好地比较两个品牌，不体现 confirmation bias。

choices.label: Looking for positive reviews of a favored brand
choices.labelZh: 寻找对偏爱品牌的好评
choices.explanationZh: 正确。只找自己喜欢品牌的正面评价，正是 favor information that confirms pre-existing beliefs。

choices.label: Avoiding an expensive product because of its price
choices.labelZh: 因价格而回避昂贵产品
choices.explanationZh: 因价格高而回避产品更像损失/风险规避，不是 confirmation bias。

versions.transcript: Today we're discussing behavioral economics, a fascinating field that explores how psychological factors influence economic decision making. Traditionally, economists assumed that individuals made rational choices. However, behavioral economics challenges this notion by demonstrating that people often behave irrationally because of cognitive biases and emotions. One classic example is the concept of loss aversion. Studies show that individuals tend to prefer avoiding losses rather than acquiring equivalent gains. For instance, losing EUR100 feels worse than gaining EUR100 feels good. This bias can lead to risk averse behavior impacting consumer decisions. The risk of loss seems intolerable even when there is an equal or greater opportunity for gain. Another factor is present bias where individuals disproportionately value immediate rewards over future benefits. This can make it hard to save for retirement and can lead people to overspend. Another behavior that economists examine is confirmation bias where individuals favor information that confirms their pre existing beliefs while disregarding contradictory data. Imagine a consumer who strongly believes that brand X makes the best smartphones. Because of confirmation bias, they might only seek out favorable reviews about brand X while ignoring negative ones. Even when presented with objective comparisons showing that another brand has better features or is more reliable, they will downplay that information.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天我们要讨论行为经济学，这是一个探索心理因素如何影响经济决策的迷人领域。 传统上，经济学家假设个人会做出理性的选择。 然而，行为经济学通过证明人们往往因为认知偏差和情感而表现得不理性，从而挑战了这一观点。 一个经典的例子是损失厌恶的概念。 研究表明，个人往往更倾向于避免损失，而不是获得等额的收益。 例如，损失100欧元的痛苦感要超过获得100欧元的愉悦感。 这种偏见会导致规避风险的行为，从而影响消费者的决策。 即使面对同等或更大的获利机会，损失的风险似乎也是无法忍受的。 另一个因素是现状偏差，即个人过度看重眼前奖励而忽视未来利益。 这可能使人们难以通过储蓄来筹备退休，并可能导致过度消费。 经济学家研究的另一种行为是确认偏差，即个人倾向于支持证实其现有信念的信息，而忽视矛盾的数据。 想象一下，如果一个消费者坚信品牌 X 生产最好的智能手机。 由于确认偏差，他们可能只会寻找有关品牌 X 的正面评价，而忽视负面评价。 即使面对显示另一个品牌具有更好功能或更可靠的客观比较，他们也会轻视这些信息。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a personal health podcast.

Woman: Let's talk about biohacking. Biohacking is an increasingly popular, self-directed approach to enhancing physical and mental performance, often through methods that lack full scientific support. One widely practiced biohacking technique is intermittent fasting, where people restrict eating to only specific windows of time. Practitioners believe it helps regulate energy levels and supports metabolic efficiency. Although research is ongoing, results so far do show some metabolic benefits. Certain types of substances that are considered cognitive enhancers are another cornerstone of biohacking. Green tea, for example. Taking green tea extract is supposed to improve memory, attention, and focus. Users often keep track of their productivity, mood, and memory to refine their intake. However, long-term data about the effects of green tea extract and other cognitive enhancers are often lacking. Researchers emphasize the need for more rigorous, large-scale studies to determine their safety and effectiveness. Tracking sleep patterns is also central to biohacking. Wearable devices can monitor sleep stages, heart rate, and movement. This could help users identify patterns and make changes to improve sleep quality, like by adjusting room temperature and evening routines. Some people use soundscapes, for example ocean waves or forest sounds, to influence brainwave activity and deepen their sleep. Light plays a role in sleep too. Less nighttime light from digital screens and more bright light in the morning help improve one's sleep and wake cycle. This is the biohacking method that seems most strongly supported by research, since manipulating light exposure does appear to significantly affect sleep quality.

请听一段个人健康播客的讲座。

女：我们来谈生物黑客。生物黑客是一种日益流行、自我主导的身心表现提升方法，所用手段往往缺乏充分科学支持。广泛实践的一种技术是间歇性禁食：只在特定时间窗进食。实践者相信它有助调节能量水平、支持代谢效率。尽管研究仍在进行，目前结果确实显示一些代谢益处。被视为认知增强剂的某些物质是生物黑客的另一基石。例如绿茶。服用绿茶提取物据称可改善记忆、注意与专注。用户常追踪生产力、情绪与记忆以调整摄入。然而绿茶提取物及其他认知增强剂的长期数据往往缺失。研究者强调需要更严格的大规模研究来判定其安全性与有效性。追踪睡眠模式也是生物黑客的核心。可穿戴设备可监测睡眠阶段、心率与活动。这有助用户识别规律并做出改变以改善睡眠质量，例如调节室温与晚间习惯。有人用声景，如海浪或森林声，影响脑波活动、加深睡眠。光对睡眠也有作用。夜间减少数字屏幕光、早晨增加明亮光线，有助改善睡醒周期。这似乎是研究支持最强的生物黑客方法，因为调控光照暴露确实显著影响睡眠质量。

versions.transcript: Let's talk about biohacking. Biohacking is an increasingly popular self directed approach to enhancing physical and mental performance, often through methods that lack full scientific support. One widely practiced biohacking technique is intermittent fasting, where people restrict eating to only specific windows of time. Biohacking is a very popular self directed approach to enhancing physical and mental performance. Practitioners believe it helps regulate energy levels and supports metabolic efficiency. Although research is ongoing, results so far do show some metabolic benefits. Certain types of substances that are considered cognitive enhancers are another cornerstone of biohacking. Green tea, for example. Taking green tea extract is supposed to improve memory, attention and focus. Users often keep track of how much they are consuming. It can help improve their productivity, mood and memory to refine their intake. However, long term data about the effects of green tea extract and other cognitive enhancers are often lacking. Researchers emphasize the need for more rigorous large scale studies to determine their safety and effectiveness. Tracking sleep patterns is also central to biohacking. Wearable devices can monitor sleep stages, heart rate and movement. This could help users identify patterns and make changes to improve sleep quality, like by adjusting room temperature and evening routines. Some people use soundscapes, for example, ocean waves or forest sounds, to influence brainwave activity and deepen their sleep. Light plays a role in sleep, too. Less nighttime light from digital screens and more bright light in the morning help improve one's sleep and wake cycle. This is the biohacking method that seems most strongly supported by research, since manipulating light exposure does appear to significantly affect sleep quality.
versions.transcriptZh: 让我们来聊聊生物黑客（biohacking）。 生物黑客是一种日益流行的、旨在增强身体和心理表现的自我管理方法，通常采用缺乏充分科学支持的方法。 一种广泛应用的生物黑客技术是间歇性禁食，即人们将进食限制在特定的时间窗口内。 生物黑客是一种非常流行的、旨在提高身心潜能的自我导向型方法。 从业者认为这有助于调节能量水平并支持代谢效率。 尽管研究仍在进行中，但目前的结果确实显示出了一些代谢方面的益处。 被视为认知增强剂的某些物质是生物黑客的另一个基石。 例如绿茶。 服用绿茶提取物被认为可以改善记忆力、注意力和专注力。 用户通常会记录自己的摄入量。 这可以帮助他们通过优化摄入量来提高工作效率、改善情绪和记忆力。 然而，通常缺乏关于绿茶提取物和其他认知增强剂效果的长期数据。 研究人员强调，需要进行更严谨的大规模研究来确定其安全性和有效性。 追踪睡眠模式也是生物黑客的核心内容。 可穿戴设备可以监测睡眠阶段、心率和运动。 这可以帮助用户识别模式并做出改变以提高睡眠质量，例如通过调节室温和晚间常规活动。 有些人使用声景（例如海浪声或森林声）来影响脑波活动并加深睡眠。 光线对睡眠也起着重要作用。 减少来自数字屏幕的夜间光线，并在早晨增加明亮的自然光，有助于改善一个人的睡眠-觉醒周期。 这是似乎得到研究支持最科学的生物黑客方法，因为调节光照暴露确实显着地影响睡眠质量。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a marine biology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a marine biology class.

Woman: One growing concern in marine biology is ocean acidification. This refers to the decrease in the pH of Earth's oceans, mainly due to the absorption of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. When carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater, it forms carbonic acid, which lowers the pH and alters the ocean's chemical balance. This change has serious consequences for marine organisms, especially those that use calcium carbonate to build shells and skeletons, such as staghorn corals, Pacific oysters, and certain types of plankton. As acidity increases, these organisms struggle to maintain their structures, resulting in weaker shells and unhealthy corals. Coral reefs, such as the Great Barrier Reef in the Coral Sea, are particularly vulnerable. Their decline can lead to reduced biodiversity and disrupted ecosystems. Ocean acidification also affects fish. A 2023 study conducted by marine biologists at James Cook University found that clown fish exposed to lower pH levels in reef environments had difficulty detecting the sounds of predators and navigating their surroundings. This sensory impairment may also interfere with reproduction, threatening population stability. To address this issue, efforts focus on reducing carbon dioxide emissions. This includes shifting to renewable energy, improving energy efficiency, and adopting sustainable practices. Additionally, protecting ecosystems like seagrass beds and mangroves can help absorb carbon dioxide and buffer acidification. Mangroves, in particular, can store up to ten times more carbon per hectare than terrestrial forests. Understanding and mitigating ocean acidification is essential for preserving marine biodiversity and maintaining healthy oceans. It requires global cooperation and long-term commitment.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段海洋生物学课的讲座。

女：海洋生物学中日益令人关切的问题之一是海洋酸化。这指地球海洋 pH 下降，主要因吸收大气中的二氧化碳。二氧化碳溶入海水形成碳酸，降低 pH 并改变海洋化学平衡。这一变化对海洋生物有严重后果，尤其对用碳酸钙建造壳与骨骼的生物，如鹿角珊瑚、太平洋牡蛎与某些浮游生物。酸度上升时，这些生物难以维持结构，导致壳变弱、珊瑚不健康。珊瑚礁如珊瑚海的大堡礁特别脆弱。其衰退可导致生物多样性下降与生态系统紊乱。海洋酸化也影响鱼类。詹姆斯·库克大学海洋生物学家二零二三年的研究发现，在珊瑚礁环境中暴露于较低 pH 的小丑鱼难以察觉捕食者声音并导航周围环境。这种感觉损害也可能干扰繁殖，威胁种群稳定。为应对此问题，努力聚焦减少二氧化碳排放。包括转向可再生能源、提高能效与采用可持续做法。此外，保护海草床与红树林等生态系统有助吸收二氧化碳并缓冲酸化。尤其红树林每公顷可储存比陆地森林多达十倍的碳。理解并缓解海洋酸化对保护海洋生物多样性与维持健康海洋至关重要。它需要全球合作与长期承诺。

versions.transcript: One growing concern in marine biology is ocean acidification. This refers to the decrease in the pH of Earth's oceans, mainly due to the absorption of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. When carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater, it forms carbonic acid, which lowers the pH and alters the ocean's chemical balance. This change has serious consequences for marine organisms, especially those that use calcium carbonate to build shells and skeletons, such as staghorn corals, Pacific oysters, and certain types of plankton. As acidity increases, these organisms struggle to maintain their structures, resulting in weaker shells and unhealthy corals. Coral reefs, such as the Great Barrier Reef in the Coral Sea, are particularly vulnerable. Their decline can lead to reduced biodiversity and disrupted ecosystems. Ocean acidification also affects fish. A 2023 study conducted by marine biologists at James Cook University found that clownfish exposed to lower pH levels in reef environments had difficulty detecting the sounds of predators and navigating their surroundings. This sensory impairment may also interfere with reproduction, threatening population stability. To address this issue, efforts focus on reducing carbon dioxide emissions. This includes shifting to renewable energy, improving energy efficiency, and adopting sustainable practices. Additionally, protecting ecosystems like seagrass beds and mangroves can help absorb carbon dioxide and buffer acidification. Mangroves, in particular, can store up to 10 times more carbon per hectare than terrestrial forests. Understanding and mitigating ocean acidification is essential for preserving marine biodiversity and maintaining healthy oceans. It requires global cooperation and long term commitment.
versions.transcriptZh: 海洋生物学中一个日益增长的担忧是海洋酸化。 这指的是地球海洋pH值的下降，主要是由于吸收了大气中的二氧化碳。 当二氧化碳溶解在海水中时，会形成碳酸，从而降低pH值并改变海洋的化学平衡。 这种变化对海洋生物有严重后果，特别是那些利用碳酸钙构建贝壳和骨骼的生物，如鹿角珊瑚、太平洋牡蛎和某些类型的浮游生物。 随着酸度的增加，这些生物难以维持其结构，导致贝壳变弱和珊瑚不健康。 珊瑚礁，例如珊瑚海中的大堡礁，尤其脆弱。 它们的衰退可能导致生物多样性减少和生态系统紊乱。 海洋酸化也影响鱼类。 詹姆斯库克大学海洋生物学家在2023年进行的一项研究发现，暴露于珊瑚礁环境中较低pH值的小丑鱼难以探测捕食者的声音并导航周围环境。 这种感觉障碍还可能干扰繁殖，威胁种群稳定。 为解决这个问题，努力的重点是减少二氧化碳排放。 这包括转向可再生能源、提高能源效率和采用可持续做法。 此外，保护海草床和红树林等生态系统有助于吸收二氧化碳和缓冲酸化。 特别是红树林，每公顷储存的碳量是陆地森林的10倍。 理解和减缓海洋酸化对于保护海洋生物多样性和维持健康的海洋至关重要。 这需要全球合作和长期承诺。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a literature class.

Woman: So today we are looking at the hero's journey, a storytelling pattern that shows up in myths, literature, and narratives from all over the world. This structure was brought into the spotlight by Joseph Campbell, an American mythologist, in his book The Hero with a Thousand Faces. Campbell studied myths across cultures and noticed they shared a common structure. Campbell called it the monomyth, and he believed it reflected something universal about the human experience. The journey usually kicks off with a call to adventure, some kind of invitation or challenge that pulls the hero out of their everyday life. They might resist at first, but eventually they accept, often with a mentor's help. Then come the trials, tests that push the hero to grow. At the center of it all is the abyss, the toughest part, where the hero faces their greatest fear or enemy. If they make it through, they are transformed. And here's the key part. They return with a gift, some kind of insight, wisdom, or ability that can help others. That gift is what makes the journey meaningful, not just for the hero, but for their community. Now, some critics argue this model oversimplifies storytelling. It can flatten out cultural differences and force diverse stories into a single mold. Still, I would argue it is influential because it taps into something deeply human, the idea that struggle leads to growth and that we come back changed.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段文学课的讲座。

女：今天我们看英雄之旅，一种出现在世界各地神话、文学与叙事中的故事模式。这一结构因美国神话学家约瑟夫·坎贝尔的著作《千面英雄》而备受瞩目。坎贝尔研究跨文化神话，发现它们共享共同结构。他称之为单一神话，并相信它反映人类经验中某种普遍之物。旅程通常以冒险召唤开始：某种邀请或挑战把英雄拉出日常生活。起初他们可能抗拒，但最终接受，常在导师帮助下。接着是试炼，推动英雄成长的考验。核心是深渊，最艰难的部分，英雄面对最大恐惧或敌人。若挺过，他们被转化。关键在这里：他们带着礼物归来，某种可助他人的洞见、智慧或能力。正是这份礼物使旅程有意义，不仅对英雄，也对其共同体。有批评者认为这一模型过度简化叙事。它可能抹平文化差异，把多样故事塞进单一模具。尽管如此，我认为它有影响力，因为它触及极深的人性：斗争带来成长，我们归来时已改变。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a sociology podcast.

Woman: Picture a bustling town square. What makes it lively? Is it the buildings? The people? The signage? Sociologists argue that public spaces hold a mirror to a society's values. This concept, known as public sphere theory, suggests that the way we design and use our public spaces reveals much about our cultural identity. According to this theory, a city's parks, plazas, and streetscapes serve not just as physical locations, but also as stages for social interaction and cultural exchange. The theory also examines how accessible these spaces are to the people who live near them. A public space that is inclusive, one that welcomes people from all walks of life, is reflective of a progressive society. On the flip side, spaces that are restrictive or that exclude certain people are often indicative of societal divisions and inequalities. Another aspect of public sphere theory is the struggle faced by cities to balance the need for open, accessible areas with issues like overcrowding and other safety concerns. In addition, city planners often face the dilemma of preserving cultural heritage while adapting to the modern needs of a community. I should note that technology is also reshaping public spaces. Social media platforms offer new arenas for interaction, and these virtual public spaces are fundamentally altering the traditional public sphere. However, just as traditional public spaces face challenges, so too do these digital spaces. Most prominent are privacy concerns and the digital divide between those who have computer access and those who do not.

女：想象一座热闹的城镇广场。什么让它有生气？是建筑？人？标识？社会学家认为公共空间映照社会价值观。这一概念称为公共领域理论，主张我们设计与使用公共空间的方式揭示许多文化身份。按此理论，城市的公园、广场与街景不仅是物理地点，也是社会互动与文化交流的舞台。理论还考察这些空间对附近居民的可达性。包容的公共空间——欢迎各阶层的人——反映进步社会。反之，限制性或排斥某些人的空间往往标示社会分裂与不平等。公共领域理论的另一方面是城市在开放可达区域需求与过度拥挤及其他安全问题之间的挣扎。此外，规划者常面临保护文化遗产与适应社区现代需求的两难。还须指出，技术也在重塑公共空间。社交媒体平台提供新的互动场域，这些虚拟公共空间从根本上改变传统公共领域。但正如传统公共空间面临挑战，数字空间亦然。最突出的是隐私担忧，以及有电脑接入者与无接入者之间的数字鸿沟。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Man: Earlier, we talked about the horseshoe crab and how compounds from the horseshoe crab's blood have been critical for detecting bacterial contamination in medical products and in the manufacture of pharmaceuticals. Today, let's look at the blue-ringed octopus. This small creature, a little bigger than a ping-pong ball, carries one of the most potent venoms in the ocean, tetrodotoxin. Tetrodotoxin works by blocking sodium channels in nerve cells. Think of sodium channels as gates that allow electrical signals to travel along nerves. When tetrodotoxin shuts those gates, nerve impulses stop, muscles cannot contract, and the prey becomes completely paralyzed. For the octopus, it is an elegant hunting strategy. It injects the venom into small crustaceans or fish, and within moments, they are immobilized. Now, someone always asks when I talk about this subject, what happens if the octopus injects itself with its own venom by accident, you know, with those eight arms? Well, the answer is they are unaffected by it. And by the way, octopuses are not alone in this respect. For example, spiders are also protected from the toxins they produce. As it happens, both the blue-ringed octopus and spiders have evolved sodium channels with structural differences that prevent the toxin from working. They can carry their deadly compounds without risk to themselves. Getting back to the octopus and its venom, tetrodotoxin's ability to block nerve signals has huge medical potential. Researchers are exploring it for applications like pain management and also for treating certain neurological conditions.

请听一段生物学课的讲座。

男：此前我们谈过鲎，以及鲎血中的化合物如何对检测医疗产品细菌污染与制药至关重要。今天看蓝环章鱼。这种小生物比乒乓球稍大一点，携带海洋中最强剧毒之一——河豚毒素。河豚毒素通过阻断神经细胞中的钠通道起作用。把钠通道想成允许电信号沿神经传递的门。河豚毒素关掉那些门时，神经冲动停止，肌肉无法收缩，猎物完全瘫痪。对章鱼而言，这是优雅的狩猎策略。它把毒注入小甲壳类或鱼，片刻间它们就动弹不得。谈这个话题时总有人问：章鱼若意外用自己的八条臂给自己注射会怎样？答案是它们不受影响。顺便说，章鱼在这点上并不孤单。例如蜘蛛也免受自己产生的毒素伤害。碰巧，蓝环章鱼与蜘蛛都进化出结构不同的钠通道，使毒素不起作用。它们可携带致命化合物而无自身风险。回到章鱼及其毒液：河豚毒素阻断神经信号的能力有巨大医学潜力。研究者正探索其用于疼痛管理以及治疗某些神经系统疾病等应用。

versions.transcript:
Listen to part of a psychology podcast.

Man: My brother Alex has always wanted to get a cat. He likes cats better than dogs. One day he sent me an online article titled Which Pet Is Right for You and said, see, even experts agree cats are better. But when I read the article, nowhere did it say that. The article presents balanced facts. Dogs are loyal and trainable, while cats are independent and low maintenance. My brother was not being dishonest. He simply focused only on the parts that praised cats and skimmed over or dismissed the parts that highlighted dogs' advantages. This is called confirmation bias. Our brains are lazy. They like consistency. Information that aligns with what we already know is easier to understand and less mentally taxing. So our brains seek it out and filter out the rest. versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an anthropology class.

Man: Previously, we discussed the significance of pottery to ancient cultures, including pottery as an art form and pottery's crucial role in trade. Today, we will focus on the development of pottery over time. One breakthrough was the invention of the potter's wheel around 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia. Before this, pottery was shaped mostly by hand, which was slow and produced less uniform results. The potter's wheel allowed artisans to spin and shape the clay more quickly and evenly, making it possible to create symmetrical vessels with greater precision and speed. Firing technology also advanced. Early pots were fired in open pits, which limited temperature control, resulting in uneven or fragile pots. So kilns were developed, enclosed ovens that could reach higher and more consistent temperatures. These allowed for stronger, more durable pottery. Another advance was the updraft kiln, which directed heat upward through the chamber. By adjusting the airflow, potters could control how much oxygen reached the fire. This helped them produce pottery with specific colors, like red or black, depending on how the clay reacted to the firing atmosphere. Then, in ancient China, potters developed kilns that could reach very high temperatures. This allowed them to create stoneware and eventually porcelain. Porcelain is made from a special mix of fine clay and minerals and must be fired at temperatures above 1200 degrees Celsius. The result is a smooth white ceramic that is strong, lightweight, and slightly translucent. Porcelain was a major breakthrough because it was more durable and versatile than earlier pottery.

男：此前我们讨论了陶器对古代文化的意义，包括陶器作为艺术形式及其在贸易中的关键作用。今天聚焦陶器随时间的发展。一项突破是约公元前三五〇〇年在美索不达米亚发明的陶轮。此前陶器多靠手塑，慢且不够均匀。陶轮让工匠更快、更均匀地旋转塑形黏土，从而能以更高精度与速度制作对称器皿。烧制技术也进步了。早期陶器在露天坑中烧，温度控制有限，结果不均或易碎。于是发展出窑——能达到更高且更稳定温度的封闭炉。这使陶器更强、更耐用。另一进展是升焰窑，把热向上导过窑室。通过调节气流，陶工可控制到达火的氧气量。这帮助他们按黏土对烧成气氛的反应，做出特定颜色的陶器，如红或黑。随后在古代中国，陶工发展出可达极高温的窑。这使他们能做炻器，最终做出瓷器。瓷器由细黏土与矿物的特殊混合制成，须在摄氏一千二百度以上烧成。结果是光滑的白色陶瓷，强韧、轻、略透光。瓷器是重大突破，因其比早期陶器更耐用、用途更广。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Narrator
transcriptSentences.text: Listen to a talk in an anthropology class.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 请听一段人类学课的讲座。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Previously, we discussed the significance of pottery to ancient cultures, including pottery as an art form and pottery's crucial role in trade.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 此前我们讨论了陶器对古代文化的意义，包括陶器作为艺术形式及其在贸易中的关键作用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Today, we will focus on the development of pottery over time.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 今天聚焦陶器随时间的发展。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: One breakthrough was the invention of the potter's wheel around 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 一项突破是约公元前三五〇〇年在美索不达米亚发明的陶轮。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Before this, pottery was shaped mostly by hand, which was slow and produced less uniform results.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 此前陶器多靠手塑，慢且不够均匀。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: The potter's wheel allowed artisans to spin and shape the clay more quickly and evenly, making it possible to create symmetrical vessels with greater precision and speed.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 陶轮让工匠更快、更均匀地旋转塑形黏土，从而能以更高精度与速度制作对称器皿。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Firing technology also advanced.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 烧制技术也进步了。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Early pots were fired in open pits, which limited temperature control, resulting in uneven or fragile pots.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 早期陶器在露天坑中烧，温度控制有限，结果不均或易碎。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: So kilns were developed, enclosed ovens that could reach higher and more consistent temperatures.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 于是发展出窑——能达到更高且更稳定温度的封闭炉。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: These allowed for stronger, more durable pottery.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这使陶器更强、更耐用。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Another advance was the updraft kiln, which directed heat upward through the chamber.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 另一进展是升焰窑，把热向上导过窑室。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: By adjusting the airflow, potters could control how much oxygen reached the fire.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 通过调节气流，陶工可控制到达火的氧气量。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: This helped them produce pottery with specific colors, like red or black, depending on how the clay reacted to the firing atmosphere.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这帮助他们按黏土对烧成气氛的反应，做出特定颜色的陶器，如红或黑。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Then, in ancient China, potters developed kilns that could reach very high temperatures.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 随后在古代中国，陶工发展出可达极高温的窑。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: This allowed them to create stoneware and eventually porcelain.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这使他们能做炻器，最终做出瓷器。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Porcelain is made from a special mix of fine clay and minerals and must be fired at temperatures above 1200 degrees Celsius.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 瓷器由细黏土与矿物的特殊混合制成，须在摄氏一千二百度以上烧成。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: The result is a smooth white ceramic that is strong, lightweight, and slightly translucent.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 结果是光滑的白色陶瓷，强韧、轻、略透光。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Porcelain was a major breakthrough because it was more durable and versatile than earlier pottery.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 瓷器是重大突破，因其比早期陶器更耐用、用途更广。

questions.promptText: What is the main purpose of the talk?
questions.promptTextZh: 讲座的主要目的是什么？

choices.label: To describe the events that led to pottery being invented
choices.labelZh: 描述导致陶器发明的事件
choices.explanationZh: 讲座从 pottery 已存在之后的发展说起，不是讲陶器如何被发明。

choices.label: To highlight technological advancements in pottery
choices.labelZh: 强调陶器制作的技术进步
choices.explanationZh: 正确。全文按 potter’s wheel、kilns、updraft kiln、porcelain 介绍陶器技术进步。

choices.label: To highlight the cultural significance of pottery
choices.labelZh: 强调陶器的文化意义
choices.explanationZh: cultural significance 是 previous discussion，不是 today 的重点。

choices.label: To compare pottery styles from different ancient regions
choices.labelZh: 比较不同古代地区的陶器风格
choices.explanationZh: 原文没有比较不同地区的 pottery styles。

questions.promptText: What benefit of the potter's wheel is mentioned?
questions.promptTextZh: 讲座中提到了陶轮的哪个好处？

choices.label: It allowed potters to decorate pots more easily.
choices.labelZh: 它使陶工更容易装饰陶罐
choices.explanationZh: 原文没有说 potter’s wheel 让装饰更容易。

choices.label: It made pottery lighter and more portable.
choices.labelZh: 它使陶器更轻便、更易于携带
choices.explanationZh: 原文没有说它让陶器更轻或更便携。

choices.label: It helped potters to control the shape of the pots better.
choices.labelZh: 它帮助陶工更好地控制陶罐的形状
choices.explanationZh: 正确。potter’s wheel 让陶工更快、更均匀地塑形，create symmetrical vessels with greater precision。

choices.label: It reduced the need for firing pottery.
choices.labelZh: 它减少了烧制陶器的需求
choices.explanationZh: firing technology 是后面另一个话题，potter’s wheel 没有减少烧制需求。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker imply about the updraft kiln?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者暗示了关于上风窑的什么信息？

choices.label: It was easier to build than other types of kilns.
choices.labelZh: 它比其他类型的窑更容易建造
choices.explanationZh: 原文没有说 updraft kiln 更容易建造。

choices.label: It allowed potters to control the final appearance of pottery.
choices.labelZh: 它允许陶工控制陶器的最终外观
choices.explanationZh: 正确。通过调节 airflow/oxygen，potters could produce specific colors，所以能控制最终外观。

choices.label: It was primarily used for making porcelain.
choices.labelZh: 它主要用于制作瓷器
choices.explanationZh: porcelain 关联的是中国后来的高温窑，不是 updraft kiln 的主要用途。

choices.label: It was difficult to maintain consistent temperatures when using it.
choices.labelZh: 使用它时难以保持稳定的温度
choices.explanationZh: 窑的发展提升了 temperature control，不是更难保持稳定温度。

questions.promptText: How is making porcelain different from making other types of pottery?
questions.promptTextZh: 制作瓷器与制作其他类型陶器有何不同？

choices.label: The clay is painted before being placed in a kiln.
choices.labelZh: 黏土在放入窑前就被上釉
choices.explanationZh: 原文没有说烧制前要先给 clay 上色。

choices.label: It requires very high temperatures.
choices.labelZh: 它需要非常高的温度
choices.explanationZh: 正确。porcelain must be fired at temperatures above 1200 degrees Celsius。

choices.label: The clay is shaped without using a potter’s wheel.
choices.labelZh: 黏土塑形时不使用陶轮
choices.explanationZh: 原文没有说 porcelain 不用 potter’s wheel 塑形。

choices.label: It has to be handled with care as it is very fragile.
choices.labelZh: 因为它非常易碎，所以必须小心处理
choices.explanationZh: 原文说 porcelain strong，不是 fragile。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a psychology class.

Woman: Have you ever wondered why certain songs evoke strong emotions or memories? This phenomenon is rooted in the field of music psychology, which examines how music impacts our feelings, thoughts, and behaviors. Research indicates that music can trigger a range of emotional responses through its rhythm, melody, and lyrics. For example, upbeat songs often make us feel happy and energetic. On the other hand, slow, melancholic tunes can evoke sadness or nostalgia. But why does this happen? One theory suggests that music stimulates the brain's reward system. That is, it releases a chemical called dopamine. Dopamine is a neurotransmitter associated with pleasure and motivation. In addition, music is often intertwined with personal experiences. Hearing a song that played during a significant life event can bring back vivid memories and the emotions associated with them. I should point out, though, that individual responses to music can vary greatly. Idiosyncratic factors that play a role in how we perceive and react to different types of music include cultural background, personality, and the context in which we hear the song. Now, this effect that music has on emotional well-being is the basis for music therapy, which has been useful in treating a variety of psychological conditions like stress or anxiety. By leveraging music's emotional power, music therapists can help patients reduce stress and improve their overall well-being. More research is needed, but our growing understanding of music psychology points to its even greater benefits for mental health and emotional regulation in the future.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段心理学课的讲座。

女：你是否想过为何某些歌曲会唤起强烈情绪或记忆？这一现象植根于音乐心理学领域，研究音乐如何影响我们的感受、思想与行为。研究表明，音乐可通过节奏、旋律与歌词触发一系列情绪反应。例如，欢快歌曲常让我们感到快乐、充满活力。另一方面，缓慢忧郁的曲调可唤起悲伤或怀旧。但为何如此？一种理论认为音乐刺激脑的奖赏系统。也就是说，它释放一种叫多巴胺的化学物质。多巴胺是与愉悦和动机相关的神经递质。此外，音乐常与个人经历交织。听到在重大人生事件中播放过的歌，可带回鲜明记忆及与之相连的情绪。不过我应指出，个体对音乐的反应可差异很大。影响我们如何感知与回应不同类型音乐的特异因素包括文化背景、个性以及听歌的情境。音乐对情绪福祉的这种效应是音乐治疗的基础，已用于治疗压力或焦虑等多种心理状况。通过借助音乐的情绪力量，音乐治疗师可帮助患者减压并改善整体福祉。仍需更多研究，但我们对音乐心理学日益加深的理解指向它未来对心理健康与情绪调节的更大益处。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a business class.

Woman: Let's discuss the role of startup incubators in supporting new businesses. These are programs designed to help startups navigate the early stages of development and increase their chances of success by providing resources, mentorship, and networking. What resources might a new business lack? Incubators often provide office space and equipment to help startups get off the ground, and they also steer new businesses toward funding opportunities. Many new entrepreneurs will lack the financial means to invest in basic necessities themselves, and this support can be invaluable. Another important element of incubators is mentorship. Experienced professionals and industry experts offer guidance and advice to startup founders. Starting a business is full of pitfalls, and a good mentor can help you avoid some of the more common ones, not to mention refine your business strategies. Networking opportunities are another significant benefit of incubators. What does a new enterprise need more than anything else? Investors. Being part of an incubator program allows you to connect with potential investors, other entrepreneurs, and future business partners. Now, participating in an incubator is not without its challenges. There is a lot of competition to get into some of these programs, so not all startups are accepted. Once you have been accepted, the pressure to perform and meet milestones can be intense, and failure to do so can lose you the support of the incubator. That said, the benefits can be substantial. Incubators provide a supportive environment that fosters innovation and helps startups overcome the hurdles of early-stage development.

transcriptSentences.textZh: 让我们讨论一下创业孵化器在支持新业务中的作用。

transcriptSentences.text: These are programs designed to help startups navigate the early stages of development and increase their chances of success by providing resources, mentorship, and networking.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这些计划旨在通过提供资源、指导和人际网络，帮助初创企业度过早期发展阶段并增加成功的机会。

transcriptSentences.text: What resources might a new business lack?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 新企业可能缺乏哪些资源？

transcriptSentences.text: Incubators often provide office space and equipment to help startups get off the ground, and they also steer new businesses toward funding opportunities.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 孵化器通常提供办公空间和设备以帮助初创企业起步，并且还会引导新企业寻找融资机会。

transcriptSentences.text: Many new entrepreneurs will lack the financial means to invest in basic necessities themselves, and this support can be invaluable.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 许多新创业者会缺乏投资基本必需品的财力，而这种支持可能是无价的。

transcriptSentences.text: Another important element of incubators is mentorship.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 孵化器的另一个重要元素是导师制度。

transcriptSentences.text: Experienced professionals and industry experts offer guidance and advice to startup founders.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 经验丰富的专业人士和行业专家为初创企业创始人提供指导和建议。

transcriptSentences.text: Starting a business is full of pitfalls, and a good mentor can help you avoid some of the more common ones, not to mention refine your business strategies.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 创业充满了陷阱，一位好的导师可以帮助你避开一些常见的陷阱，更不用说优化你的商业策略了。

transcriptSentences.text: Networking opportunities are another significant benefit of incubators.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 社交机会是孵化器的另一个显著优势。

transcriptSentences.text: What does a new enterprise need more than anything else?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 新企业最需要的是什么？

transcriptSentences.text: Investors.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 投资者。

transcriptSentences.text: Being part of an incubator program allows you to connect with potential investors, other entrepreneurs, and future business partners.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 加入孵化器计划可以让你与潜在的投资者、其他企业家和未来的业务合作伙伴建立联系。

transcriptSentences.text: Now participating in an incubator is not without its challenges.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 现在，参加孵化器也不是没有挑战的。

transcriptSentences.text: There's a lot of competition to get into some of these programs, so not all startups are accepted.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 进入其中一些计划的竞争非常激烈，因此并非所有初创企业都会被录取。

transcriptSentences.text: Once you've been accepted, the pressure to perform and meet milestones can be intense, and failure to do so can lose you the support of the incubator.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 一旦你被录取，表现和达成里程碑的压力可能会很大，如果做不到这一点，你可能会失去孵化器的支持。

transcriptSentences.text: That said, the benefits can be substantial.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 尽管如此，带来的好处还是巨大的。

transcriptSentences.text: Incubators provide a supportive environment that fosters innovation and helps startups overcome the hurdles of early stage development.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 孵化器提供了一个支持性的环境，促进创新并帮助初创企业克服早期发展的障碍。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an archaeology class.

Man: For decades, archaeologists believed that complex societies and monumental architecture only emerged after agriculture, and that farming was essential for societal development. Before agriculture developed, people tended not to settle in a single place, but moved from place to place in search of food. We call such people nomadic hunter-gatherers. They were continuously on the move to hunt and collect food. And for people who are not settled, it was more practical to live in small mobile groups rather than in complex societies. Or so it was believed. But the excavation of the ancient site of Gobekli Tepe threw a wrench in this whole story. Gobekli Tepe, dating back about 11,000 years, consists of multiple massive pillars arranged in circles and is considered the world's oldest known temple. Remarkably, it predates the earliest evidence of agriculture in the area by several thousand years. This suggests spiritual practices, not agriculture, may have caused early communities to form. Many scholars interpret the site as a ceremonial center, a periodic gathering place for nomadic hunter-gatherers. More recently, archaeologists there did find traces of things like food processing areas, stone tools for grinding grains, as well as actual plant residues. Yet these residues come from local wild grains, not domesticated crops, and the structures may not indicate year-round habitation. So while Gobekli Tepe might have hosted temporary gatherings, the evidence still supports the idea that spiritual practices played a central role in early societal development.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段考古学课的讲座。

男：数十年来，考古学家相信复杂社会与纪念性建筑只在农业之后出现，耕作对社会发展必不可少。农业发展之前，人们往往不在一处定居，而是为觅食四处迁徙。我们称其为游动的狩猎采集者。他们不断移动以狩猎采集。对未定居者而言，住在小型流动群体比复杂社会更实际。或者说人们曾如此相信。但哥贝克力石阵古代遗址的发掘打乱了整个叙事。哥贝克力石阵约有一万一千年历史，由多根巨型石柱围成圆圈，被认为是已知世界最古老的神庙。惊人的是，它比该地区最早农业证据还早数千年。这暗示可能是精神实践而非农业促成早期共同体形成。许多学者把该遗址解读为礼仪中心，游动狩猎采集者的周期性聚集地。更近些时候，考古学家确实发现了食物加工区、磨谷石器以及植物残体等痕迹。但这些残体来自本地野生谷物而非驯化作物，建筑也可能不表示常年居住。因此，尽管哥贝克力石阵可能举办过临时聚集，证据仍支持精神实践在早期社会发展中起核心作用。

transcriptSentences.text: We call such people nomadic hunter gatherers.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 我们称这些人是游牧的狩猎采集者。

transcriptSentences.text: They were continuously on the move to hunt and collect food.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 他们不断地迁徙以狩猎和采集食物。

transcriptSentences.text: And for people who aren't settled, it was more practical to live in small mobile groups rather than in complex societies.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 对于不安定居的人来说，生活在小型流动群体中比生活在复杂社会中更实际。

transcriptSentences.text: Or so it was believed.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 至少之前是这样认为的。

transcriptSentences.text: But the excavation of the ancient site of Göbekli Tepe threw a wrench in this whole story.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但是格贝克利石阵古遗址的挖掘却给这个故事带来了意想不到的转折。

transcriptSentences.text: Göbekli Tepe, dating back about 11,000 years, consists of multiple massive pillars arranged in circles and is considered the world's oldest known temple.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 格贝克利石阵可追溯到大约11,000年前，由多个圆形排列的巨大石柱组成，被认为是世界上已知最古老的寺庙。

transcriptSentences.text: Remarkably, it predates the earliest evidence of agriculture in the area by several thousand years.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 值得注意的是，它比该地区最早的农业证据早了几千年。

transcriptSentences.text: This suggests spiritual practices, not agriculture, may have caused early communities to form.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这表明是精神实践而非农业，可能导致了早期社区的形成。

transcriptSentences.text: Many scholars interpret the site as a ceremonial center, a periodic gathering place for nomadic hunter gatherers.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 许多学者将该遗址解释为一个仪式中心，一个游牧狩猎采集者定期聚集的场所。

transcriptSentences.text: More recently, archaeologists there did find traces of things like food processing areas, stone tools for grinding grains, as well as actual plant residues.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 最近，那里的考古学家确实发现了食物加工区、研磨谷物的石器以及实际植物残骸的痕迹。

transcriptSentences.text: Yet these residues come from local wild grains, not domesticated crops.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 然而，这些残骸来自当地的野生谷物，而非驯化作物。

transcriptSentences.text: And the structures may not indicate year round habitation.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 而且这些结构可能并不表明是全年居住地。

transcriptSentences.text: So while Göbekli Tepe might have hosted temporary gatherings, the evidence still supports the idea that spiritual practices played a central role in early societal development.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 因此，尽管格贝克利石阵可能举办过临时集会，但证据仍然支持精神实践在早期社会发展中扮演核心角色的观点。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Woman: The phenomenon of animal migration is a fascinating subject in biology. Migration involves the regular, often seasonal movement of animals from one region to another, typically in search of food, breeding grounds, or better climates. This behavior is observed in a wide variety of species, including birds, mammals, fish, and insects. One of the most well known examples is the migration of monarch butterflies. These butterflies travel thousands of miles from North America to central Mexico to escape the cold winter. This journey involves multiple generations, as no single butterfly makes the round trip. Another remarkable example is the migration of humpback whales. These massive creatures travel from their feeding grounds in polar waters to warmer tropical regions where they breed and give birth. Birds like the Arctic tern undertake one of the longest migrations, traveling from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back each year. Despite their differences in size, species, and reasons for migrating, they all migrate vast distances with precision. They navigate like seasoned human pilots flying transcontinental routes, only without aircraft, instruments, or GPS. Of course, migration is not without its challenges. Animals must navigate vast distances, often facing predators, adverse weather, and human-made obstacles like buildings and roads. Protecting habitats and reducing human interference can help maintain the delicate balance that allows migration to occur. Understanding animal migration provides insight into the complex behaviors and survival strategies of various species.

请听一段生物学课的讲座。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an anthropology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an anthropology class.

Kinship refers to the relationships formed through blood ties, marriage or adoption. When you think about siblings or parent and child, you're thinking about consanguineal relationships — those based on shared blood. In contrast, relationships formed through marriage, such as the bond between spouses, or between a person and their in-laws, are known as affinal relationships. Both types of relationships play important roles.

Kinship systems vary widely across cultures. Some societies practice patrilineal descent, where lineage and inheritance are traced through the father's side of the family. Others follow matrilineal descent, where these aspects are traced through the mother's side.

How do anthropologists study kinship? They often live within a community for extended periods to conduct interviews, attend family events, and make observations. An anthropologist studying a matrilineal society might observe the role of maternal uncles, who may play key roles in child-rearing. Anthropologists map out relationships in kinship charts to visualize how people are related and to identify patterns in descent, marriage and inheritance.

Do kinship charts sound like family trees to you? Well, they both illustrate relationships among people. Family trees are commonly used in genealogy to trace biological ancestry and family history, while kinship charts highlight cultural categories of kin as well as biological ties. For example, in some cultures, a mother's sister may be treated as a second mother, and this relationship would be represented accordingly in a kinship chart.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段人类学课的讲座。

亲属关系指通过血缘、婚姻或收养形成的关系。想到兄弟姐妹或父母子女时，你想的是血亲关系——基于共同血缘。相比之下，通过婚姻形成的关系，如配偶之间，或个人与姻亲之间，称为姻亲关系。两类关系都起重要作用。

亲属制度跨文化差异很大。一些社会实行父系继嗣，谱系与继承沿父亲一方追溯。另一些遵循母系继嗣，这些方面沿母亲一方追溯。

人类学家如何研究亲属关系？他们常在社群中长期生活，进行访谈、参加家庭活动并观察。研究母系社会的人类学家可能观察舅父的角色——舅父可能在育儿中起关键作用。人类学家用亲属图绘制关系，以可视化人们如何关联，并识别继嗣、婚姻与继承的模式。

亲属图听起来像家谱吗？两者都说明人与人之间的关系。家谱常用于谱系学以追溯生物祖先与家族史，而亲属图既突出亲属的文化类别，也突出生物纽带。例如，在某些文化中，母亲的姐妹可能被当作第二母亲，这一关系会在亲属图中相应呈现。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a history podcast.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a history podcast.

Man: When you think of nineteenth-century inventors, what comes to mind? Maybe, like me, you think of an inventor alone in his laboratory, tinkering with devices that no one else had ever dreamed of. Well, actually, there were often multiple people working on similar inventions at once. They would improve on each other's work, compete, or collaborate. Have you heard of Lewis Latimer, who invented one kind of early air conditioner and improved the toilet systems in trains? Probably not. Latimer, as a Black man, was excluded from many opportunities that his white peers enjoyed in the United States. He never even got to attend high school. But he taught himself and practiced on his own to be a drafter, someone who makes technical drawings. Latimer's drawings were so skillful they were practically works of art. He wrote poetry, and you can see his poetic sensibility even in his drafting work. After practicing to learn drafting, Latimer worked with several famous inventors over the span of his career. One was Hiram Maxim. Working with Hiram Maxim, Latimer developed and patented a major innovation in carbon filaments. A carbon filament is a thin wire inside a light bulb that glows with electricity to produce light. Latimer made these filaments stronger, longer-lasting, and easier to make. This was a major step in making lighting feasible and affordable for the general public.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段历史播客的讲座。

男：想到十九世纪发明家，你会想到什么？也许像我一样，想到发明家独自在实验室里捣鼓别人从未梦想过的装置。其实，往往有多人同时在做相似发明。他们会改进彼此的工作、竞争或合作。你听说过刘易斯·拉蒂默吗？他发明过一种早期空调，并改进了火车上的厕所系统。大概没有。作为黑人，拉蒂默在美国被排除在许多白人同辈享有的机会之外。他甚至没能上高中。但他自学自练成为制图员——绘制技术图纸的人。拉蒂默的图纸如此精巧，几乎是艺术品。他写诗，你甚至能在制图作品中看到诗意。学会制图后，拉蒂默职业生涯中与多位著名发明家合作。一位是海勒姆·马克西姆。与马克西姆合作时，拉蒂默开发并专利了一项碳灯丝重大创新。碳灯丝是灯泡内通电发光的细丝。拉蒂默使这些灯丝更强、更耐用、更易制造。这是让照明对大众可行且负担得起的重要一步。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music class.

Woman: Hip-hop is one of the world's most popular musical genres. I want to discuss a characteristic feature of this art form: sampling. Sampling refers to the reuse of part of an existing song in a new composition. Hip-hop artists might write a song that uses part of a vocal track, a drumbeat, or some other sound from an existing song. For example, the singer Beyonce's 2003 hit "Crazy in Love" uses a melody from a 1970 release by the band the Chi-Lites. Sampling was especially common in the early days of hip-hop, before the landmark 1991 U.S. District Court case Grand Upright Music, Ltd. v. Warner Bros. Records, Inc. The ruling in that case required artists to obtain permission to use samples in their recordings. Before that legal decision, sampling had been a relatively cheap and easy practice. It continued afterward, down to today, but in a more limited way. Critics often argue that sampling is a less creative approach than traditional music making, but I would respond that all art, including music, is referential. In creating a new work, all artists borrow, in one manner or another, from existing works of art. Hip-hop creativity comes in finding unusual sources or putting recognizable material into new contexts. But now I would like to know what you think. Let's examine the sonic collage that is Paul's Boutique, the 1989 album from the Beastie Boys, which utilizes a remarkable number of samples.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a science podcast.

Woman: When you think of Siberia, you picture a cold place. But in 2014, Siberia had an unusually warm summer. The temps exceeded 30 degrees Celsius a couple times. And also in 2014, a helicopter pilot flying over a particular area of Siberia spotted a strange crater, a cylindrical hole in the ground that was massive, 20 meters wide and 50 meters deep. Really huge. Following the report, scientists investigated and found more such craters in the same area. It looked like stuff had just exploded from the ground, with material flying out and landing hundreds of meters away. These explosions occurred in an area where oil and gas extraction take place, so they're a real concern. What if an explosion happens near an oil or gas pipeline? What's happening is connected to the warmer temperatures. Let's back up. The region's soil is permanently frozen. It's called permafrost, with pockets of ice in it. This permafrost is on top of an extensive field of underground natural gas. The ice and permafrost help hold the gas under the surface. But warming temperatures cause melting at the surface, so it can't seal the gas underground as effectively. Also, when the ice in the permafrost melts, it leaves behind empty cavities where the ice used to be. What's probably happening is that gas from below rises up and fills these cavities, building up the pressure. Eventually, the gas bursts through, and boom, a crater-causing explosion. These craters are called gas emission craters.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an architecture class.

Construction materials have changed significantly over the centuries. The desire to employ more sustainable, more environmentally friendly building methods in recent years has led to advances in what we use for construction. For example, there's actually a new building in Amsterdam in the Netherlands whose structure is made with concrete that captures carbon from the atmosphere. And as you know, capturing atmospheric carbon helps mitigate global warming.

However, a building technique doesn't need to be newly invented to be environmentally friendly. In fact, an ancient building technique involving the use of adobe bricks is making a comeback. So what's good about it?

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an art history class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an art history class.

Today, we delve into the enigmatic world of outsider art, which refers to pieces created outside the boundaries of the traditional art world by self-taught artists. These artists typically work outside the mainstream, producing pieces that are raw, authentic and deeply personal. Many creators of outsider art have faced personal challenges, which in turn have influenced their work. This gives their art a profound depth, often resonating deeply with audiences.

An intriguing case is the work of James Castle, an artist who was born deaf and never learned to read, write or speak. In his drawings, James Castle used soot from his wood stove and saliva as his primary materials, creating works that now hang in renowned galleries worldwide.

What makes outsider art so compelling is its raw authenticity. But that same authenticity can be a barrier. Without formal training or gallery representation, outsider artists often struggle to gain visibility. Their work doesn't always fit into the neat categories curators and collectors expect, which means fewer exhibitions, less funding and limited access to networks that could elevate their careers. The art world can be insular, favoring artists with art degrees, connections or institutional backing. For outsiders, even getting a foot in the door can feel impossible.

But here's the twist. Outsider art is often the most innovative and most emotionally resonant. It's art that doesn't ask for permission. It just is, and that's exactly why it deserves more space, more support and more recognition.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段艺术史课的讲座。

今天我们深入局外人艺术的神秘世界：指自学艺术家在传统艺术界边界之外创作的作品。这些艺术家通常在主流之外工作，作品原始、真实、极具个人性。许多局外人艺术创作者曾面对个人挑战，这些挑战反过来影响其作品。这使其艺术有深刻厚度，常与观众强烈共鸣。

一个引人入胜的例子是詹姆斯·卡斯尔的作品：他天生失聪，从未学会读、写或说话。在绘画中，詹姆斯·卡斯尔以木炉烟灰与唾液为主要材料，创作出如今挂在世界知名画廊的作品。

局外人艺术如此有吸引力，在于其原始真实性。但同样的真实性也可成障碍。没有正规训练或画廊代理，局外人艺术家常难以获得可见度。其作品并不总符合策展人与收藏家期待的整齐类别，意味着展览更少、资金更少、可提升其事业的人脉有限。艺术界可能封闭，偏爱有艺术学位、关系或机构支持的艺术家。对外人而言，连踏进门槛都可能觉得不可能。

但转折在此。局外人艺术往往最创新、情感共鸣最强。它是不求许可的艺术。它就是它，而这正是它值得更多空间、更多支持与更多认可的原因。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an environmental science class.

Today, we're going to talk about the importance of wetlands and their role in ecosystems. Wetlands are areas where water covers the soil, either permanently or seasonally, and include marshes, swamps and bogs. These are incredibly productive ecosystems that provide numerous benefits to the environment and human society. They serve as critical habitats for a wide variety of wildlife, including birds, fish and amphibians. And they provide breeding grounds and food sources that are essential for the survival of many species.

But wetlands aren't just waterlogged habitats; they're biochemical powerhouses. One of their primary functions is to act as natural water filters, breaking down or neutralizing toxic substances like heavy metals and pesticides through the action of specialized microbes. These microbial communities form complex relationships with plants and sediments, creating a natural filtration system that can detoxify pollutants before they reach rivers, lakes or groundwater.

Another significant role of wetlands is their ability to manage floodwaters. During periods of heavy rain, wetlands can absorb and store excess water, reducing the risk of floods in surrounding areas. Furthermore, wetlands are important for carbon sequestration, capturing and storing large amounts of carbon dioxide, which helps mitigate climate change.

However, wetlands face numerous threats, including drainage from agriculture, urban development and pollution. Protecting and restoring wetlands is crucial for maintaining their ecological functions and the benefits they provide. In the next part of our class, we will examine specific efforts to conserve and restore wetlands around the world.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段环境科学课的讲座。

今天谈湿地的重要性及其在生态系统中的角色。湿地是水永久或季节性覆盖土壤的区域，包括沼泽、沼地与泥炭沼泽。这些是极其高产的生态系统，给环境与人类社会提供众多益处。它们是多种野生动物——包括鸟、鱼与两栖动物——的关键栖息地。它们也提供对许多物种存活至关重要的繁殖地与食物源。

但湿地不只是积水栖息地；它们是生化动力站。其主要功能之一是充当天然水过滤器，通过特化微生物的作用分解或中和重金属与杀虫剂等有毒物质。这些微生物群落与植物、沉积物形成复杂关系，创建可在污染物到达河流、湖泊或地下水之前解毒的天然过滤系统。

湿地的另一重要角色是管理洪水。暴雨期间，湿地可吸收并储存过量水，降低周边地区洪水风险。此外，湿地对碳封存很重要，捕获并储存大量二氧化碳，有助缓解气候变化。

然而湿地面临众多威胁，包括农业排水、城市开发与污染。保护并恢复湿地对维持其生态功能与所提供益处至关重要。下一部分课我们将考察世界各地保护与恢复湿地的具体努力。

transcriptSentences.textZh: 湿地是指土壤被水永久或季节性覆盖的区域，包括沼泽、沼泽林和泥炭地。

transcriptSentences.text: These are incredibly productive ecosystems that provide numerous benefits to the environment and human society.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这些生态系统的生产力极高，能为环境和人类社会带来诸多益处。

transcriptSentences.text: They serve as critical habitats for a wide variety of wildlife, including birds, fish, and amphibians, and they provide breeding grounds and food sources that are essential for the survival of many species.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们是鸟类、鱼类和两栖动物等多种野生动物的重要栖息地，并为许多物种的生存提供必不可少的繁殖场所和食物来源。

transcriptSentences.text: But wetlands aren't just waterlogged habitat.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但湿地不仅仅是充满水的栖息地。

transcriptSentences.text: They're biochemical powerhouses.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们还是生物化学的发电机。

transcriptSentences.text: One of their primary functions is to act as natural water filters, breaking down or neutralizing toxic substances like heavy metals and pesticides through the action of specialized microbes.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们的主要功能之一是充当天然净水器，通过专门微生物的作用分解或中和重金属和农药等有毒物质。

transcriptSentences.text: These activities form complex relationships with plants and sediments, creating a natural filtration system that can detoxify pollutants before they reach rivers, lakes, or groundwater.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这些活动与植物和沉积物形成复杂的关系，建立起一套天然过滤系统，可以在污染物进入河流、湖泊或地下水之前对其进行解毒。

transcriptSentences.text: Another significant role of wetlands is their ability to manage floodwaters.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 湿地的另一个重要作用是管理洪水的能力。

transcriptSentences.text: During periods of heavy rain, wetlands can absorb water from the soil and store excess water, reducing the risk of floods in surrounding areas.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 在强降雨期间，湿地可以从土壤中吸收水分并储存多余的水，从而降低周边地区发生洪水的风险。

transcriptSentences.text: Furthermore, wetlands are important for carbon sequestration, capturing and storing large amounts of carbon dioxide, which helps mitigate climate change.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 此外，湿地对碳汇也很重要，它们能捕捉并储存大量的二氧化碳，有助于减缓气候变化。

transcriptSentences.text: However, wetlands face numerous threats, including drainage from agriculture, urban development, and pollution.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 然而，湿地面临着众多威胁，包括农业排水、城市开发和污染。

transcriptSentences.text: Protecting and restoring wetlands is crucial for maintaining biodiversity and preserving their ecological functions and the benefits they provide.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 保护和恢复湿地对于维持生物多样性、保护其生态功能及其带来的益处至关重要。

transcriptSentences.text: In the next part of our class, we will examine specific efforts to conserve and restore wetlands around the world.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 在接下来的课程中，我们将探讨全球范围内保护和修复湿地的具体努力。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an art history class.

Woman: When we think of the Renaissance, we often picture grand paintings and sculptures. But a lesser-known art form also flourished during this period: tapestry weaving. Tapestries were not only decorative pieces but also served practical purposes, such as insulating the cold stone walls of castles. Artists of the era used tapestries to depict intricate scenes from mythology, religion, and daily life, often incorporating vibrant colors and rich textures. An advantage of tapestries was their portability. Unlike frescoes, which were fixed to walls, tapestries could be rolled up and transported from one location to another, allowing their owners to display their wealth wherever they went. This portability also had a downside, however. Tapestries were susceptible to damage during transit. Even today, museums face challenges preserving these unique artworks due to their fragile nature. The creation of a tapestry was a labor-intensive process, requiring collaboration between designers, weavers, and dyers. Unlike paintings, which could be completed by a single artist, tapestries were team efforts, and it was common for a designer's sketches to be translated by skilled weavers into woven masterpieces. The intricate craftsmanship required to produce these artworks offers a glimpse into the collaborative spirit of the Renaissance era.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段艺术史课的讲座。

女：想到文艺复兴，我们常会想象宏伟的绘画与雕塑。但这一时期也繁荣了一种较不为人知的艺术形式：挂毯编织。挂毯不仅是装饰品，也有实用用途，例如给城堡冰冷石墙保温。该时代的艺术家用挂毯描绘神话、宗教与日常生活中的复杂场景，常融入鲜艳色彩与丰富质感。挂毯的一个优势是可携带性。与固定在墙上的湿壁画不同，挂毯可卷起并从一个地点运到另一个，让主人无论去哪都能展示财富。然而这种可携带性也有缺点。挂毯在运输中易受损。即便今天，博物馆因其脆弱性而在保存这些独特艺术品时面临挑战。创作挂毯是劳动密集型过程，需要设计者、织工与染工协作。与可由单一艺术家完成的绘画不同，挂毯是团队成果，设计者的草图由熟练织工译成编织杰作很常见。生产这些艺术品所需的精巧工艺，让我们一窥文艺复兴时代的协作精神。

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Jacob Lawrence was an African American painter, born in 1917. His paintings celebrated African American culture and history. Lawrence painted well-known Black figures like Harriet Tubman. Harriet Tubman had been an important African American social activist before the painter's time. Lawrence also painted everyday people and their struggles. For example, the Migration Series. Lawrence frequently made series of paintings. The Migration Series is 60 panels with captions that chronicle the Great Migration, when many African American families made the difficult move from the rural United States South up to northern cities in the early 1900s. In the painting, Lawrence used bold colors and strong diagonal shapes to create a sense of motion, which is representative of many of his paintings. He was only in his mid-20s when he completed the 60 panels. Quite an accomplishment for such a young artist. Lawrence purposely used a style that appeared somewhat simple. Unfortunately, this led to some critics saying his work, such as the Migration Series, was childlike or even crude. However, you can see a very polished style in his even earlier works, which showed he was perfectly capable of a painting style that would satisfy snooty critics. He chose to paint the way he did because he found this style more powerful and convincing.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段艺术史课的讲座。雅各布·劳伦斯是非裔美国画家，生于一九一七年。他的画作颂扬非裔美国文化与历史。劳伦斯画过哈丽雅特·塔布曼等知名黑人人物。哈丽雅特·塔布曼在画家时代之前已是重要的非裔美国社会活动家。劳伦斯也画普通人及其挣扎。例如《迁徙系列》。劳伦斯常画系列作品。《迁徙系列》有六十幅带说明的画面，记述大迁徙——二十世纪初许多非裔美国家庭从美国南部农村艰难迁往北方城市。在画中，劳伦斯用大胆色彩与强烈对角线形状制造动感，这代表了他许多作品的特点。完成六十幅时他才二十多岁。对如此年轻的艺术家而言相当成就。劳伦斯有意使用显得有些简单的风格。不幸的是，这导致一些批评者说他的作品如《迁徙系列》幼稚甚至粗糙。然而，你可在他更早的作品中看到非常精致的风格，表明他完全有能力画出让势利批评者满意的画风。他选择这样画，是因为他觉得这种风格更有力、更令人信服。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology podcast.

Have you ever heard of tardigrades? These are animals about half a millimeter in size, just about large enough to be visible to the naked eye. Tardigrades are renowned for their ability to survive a variety of extreme conditions — an ability that is unique among animals. They are found in diverse environments, ranging from the deep sea to high mountaintops. They can also withstand temperatures from just above absolute zero to over 150 degrees Celsius. They even survive intense radiation in the vacuum of space.

The secret to tardigrades' survival is a process called cryptobiosis. During cryptobiosis, tardigrades lose almost all their water content and produce unique proteins that protect their cells from damage. But remember, no metabolic activity — meaning no bodily process — can happen without water, so all metabolism essentially shuts down. When favorable conditions return, tardigrades rehydrate and resume normal functions.

Scientists are fascinated by tardigrades because understanding their survival mechanisms could have important implications. Take health care, for example. If we can figure out how tardigrades protect their cells from radiation, it might lead to breakthroughs in radiation therapy for cancer patients.

Astronomers are intrigued by tardigrades because of their ability to endure the vacuum of space. In a research study in 2007, tardigrades were sent to the harsh realms of space. Some not only survived, but they successfully reproduced upon their return to Earth. If tardigrades can survive in space, it suggests life might exist in the extreme environments of other planets.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段生物学播客的讲座。

你听说过缓步动物吗？这些动物体长约半毫米，刚好大到肉眼可见。缓步动物以能在多种极端条件下存活而闻名——这一能力在动物中独一无二。它们见于多样环境，从深海到高山之巅。它们也能承受从略高于绝对零度到超过摄氏一百五十度的温度。它们甚至能在太空真空中的强辐射下存活。

缓步动物存活的秘诀是一种叫隐生的过程。隐生期间，缓步动物几乎失去全部水分，并产生保护细胞免受损伤的独特蛋白质。但请记住，没有水就没有任何代谢活动——意思是没有任何身体过程——因此一切代谢基本上关闭。当有利条件恢复时，缓步动物重新吸水并恢复正常功能。

科学家着迷于缓步动物，因为理解其存活机制可能有重要意义。以医疗为例。若我们能弄清缓步动物如何保护细胞免受辐射，或许会带来癌症患者放射治疗的突破。

天文学家因缓步动物能承受太空真空而对其感兴趣。在二零〇七年的一项研究中，缓步动物被送入严酷的太空。一些不仅存活，返回地球后还成功繁殖。若缓步动物能在太空存活，这提示生命或许存在于其他行星的极端环境中。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a music history podcast.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a music history podcast. The Aeolian harp is a stringed instrument that became popular in the 18th and 19th centuries. It's basically a shallow wooden box with strings stretched across it and sound holes in the middle. Kind of like you'd see on an acoustic guitar or violin. Rather than being plucked or strummed though, it's placed near a window or outside and creates otherworldly sounds when the wind blows. It's named after the Greek god of wind, Aeolus. It was popular for a couple hundred years, though not so much today. Judging by the sound the Aeolian harp makes, you'd think that all of its strings are tuned to play different notes. In fact, they're all tuned to the same note. See, each string is a different diameter or width. So when the wind blows, they all vibrate at different frequencies. This might also remind you of, say, wind chimes. You can just hang wind chimes up outside and kind of forget about them. But for Aeolian harps, they needed to be cleaned and oiled. Some parts needed to be replaced every couple of years, so the instrument itself required regular maintenance. Contrary to what might seem logical, the Aeolian harp also wasn't made to withstand the elements, like changes in temperature or humidity. And since it was most popular in England, where the seasons change and, well, it's England, so there's a lot of damp weather. You'd either have to put it away for months at a time or keep it inside near an open window, especially in winter.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段音乐史播客的讲座。风鸣琴是十八、十九世纪流行起来的弦乐器。它基本是一个浅木盒，弦绷在上面，中间有音孔。有点像木吉他或小提琴上你会看到的那样。不过它不是拨奏或扫弦，而是放在窗边或户外，风吹时发出超凡脱俗的声音。它以希腊风神埃俄罗斯命名。流行了几百年，如今不那么流行了。从风鸣琴的声音判断，你会以为所有弦调成不同音。其实它们都调成同一音。你看，每根弦直径或粗细不同。所以风吹时它们以不同频率振动。这也许会让你想到风铃之类。风铃可以挂在外面就差不多忘了。但风鸣琴需要清洁上油。有些部件每隔几年要更换，所以乐器本身需要定期维护。与看似合乎逻辑的相反，风鸣琴也不是为经受风雨而造的，比如温度或湿度变化。而且它最流行于英格兰，那里季节更替，而且——嗯，是英格兰——所以潮湿天气很多。你要么一次收起数月，要么放在室内靠开着的窗户，尤其是冬天。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a marketing class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a marketing class. 
One of the most effective strategies in modern marketing is the use of storytelling. Storytelling involves crafting a narrative around a brand or product that engages consumers on an emotional level. Instead of simply listing features and benefits, marketers use stories to create a connection with their audience, making the brand memorable and relatable. This method has been especially powerful in the age of social media, where personal stories and viral content can significantly boost brand awareness and loyalty. Successful storytelling in marketing often includes elements like a compelling character, a relatable conflict, and a satisfying resolution. For example, a company selling eco-friendly products might tell the story of a family striving to reduce their environmental footprint. This narrative not only highlights the product's benefits but also resonates with consumers who share similar values. Another key aspect of storytelling in marketing is authenticity. Consumers are more likely to trust and engage with brands that appear genuine and transparent. This means that the story should reflect the brand's real values and mission, avoiding exaggeration or false claims. Visuals also play a crucial role in storytelling. High-quality images and videos can bring the narrative to life, making it more impactful and easier to share. Of course, measuring the success of storytelling campaigns can be difficult, as traditional metrics like sales figures don't always capture the full impact of a well-told story.

请听一段市场营销课的讲座。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music appreciation class.

Most wind instruments, which are played by blowing into them, went through lots of modifications before becoming the standardized instruments we see and hear today. Now, most brass instruments, like the trumpet and trombone, underwent many centuries of refinement before being standardized. But the tuba only took about 180 years to reach its current form. That's because through centuries, composers and inventors wanted an ideal bass instrument to play those really low notes. Rather than tinker with an instrument they didn't love, they would discard it and start again. So the tuba doesn't really have a clear ancestor — more a series of unrelated precursors trying to do what it now does.

An early example was the serpent. The serpent was made of a wooden tube bent into the shape of, well, a serpent — or the letter S. The problem was, it didn't sound great. The wooden tube was too wide, which caused problems with intonation, meaning it was hard to hit the right notes. Imagine a choir of voices accompanied by a serpent booming along out of tune. Ouch.

Well, so long, serpent. And hello, ophicleide. The ophicleide's main advantage was that it was made of brass. The brass construction made its intonation much better. The ophicleide became much more popular than the serpent. The composer Berlioz used it in some famous pieces, but still the ophicleide wasn't the answer. Its pitch range was pretty narrow, and composers wanted something that could play lower notes.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段音乐欣赏课的讲座。

多数管乐器——靠吹奏演奏——在成为我们今天所见所听的标准化乐器前经历了大量改动。多数铜管乐器，如小号与长号，标准化前经历了数世纪的改进。但大号只花了大约一百八十年就达到现今形态。那是因为数世纪里，作曲家与发明家想要一种理想的低音乐器来演奏那些很低的音。与其修补他们不喜欢的乐器，他们会弃之重来。所以大号其实没有清晰祖先——更多是一系列无关前身，试图做它现在做的事。

早期例子是蛇形号。蛇形号由弯成——嗯——蛇形或字母 S 形的木管制成。问题是声音不好。木管太粗，造成音准问题，意思是很难奏准音。想象一群人声合唱，配上蛇形号走调地轰鸣。哎哟。

好，再见蛇形号。你好，奥菲克莱德号。奥菲克莱德号的主要优势是用铜制成。铜制结构使其音准好得多。奥菲克莱德号比蛇形号流行得多。作曲家柏辽兹在一些名曲中用过它，但奥菲克莱德号仍不是答案。其音域相当窄，作曲家想要能奏更低音的东西。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an architecture class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an architecture class.

Man: Have you ever thought about how ancient concrete structures like Roman amphitheaters and aqueducts have managed to last for thousands of years, while modern concrete buildings seem to fall apart and need replacing after just a few decades? For a long time, researchers thought the secret to Roman concrete's durability was volcanic ash. That makes sense, since volcanic ash was a major ingredient, and it was described as such by architects and historians who were writing at the time. But it turns out the real secret was actually tiny chunks of calcium carbonate. These formed because the Romans used dry quicklime in their mix, instead of the way we make concrete today, called Portland cement, where lime gets mixed with water first and then blended with everything else. When cracks show up in Roman concrete and water enters, those calcium carbonate bits react with the water and seal up the cracks. So the concrete basically heals itself, fixes the cracks, and gets stronger over time. The funny thing is, researchers have noticed these chunks in Roman concrete for ages, but they just figured they were a production flaw, like someone didn't mix the ingredients well enough. Anyway, considering how short-lived modern concrete is, and the fact that making it is bad for the environment, it's pretty exciting to think we might use some of these ancient Roman tricks in future construction.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段建筑学课的讲座。

男：你是否想过，罗马圆形剧场与高架渠等古代混凝土结构如何能存续数千年，而现代混凝土建筑似乎几十年就开裂、需要更换？长期来研究者以为罗马混凝土耐久的秘密是火山灰。这说得通，因为火山灰是主要成分，当时建筑师与历史学家也如此描述。但事实证明真正秘密其实是碳酸钙小块。它们形成是因为罗马人在混合料中使用干生石灰，而不是我们今天做混凝土的方式——波特兰水泥，即先把石灰与水混合再与其他成分拌合。当罗马混凝土出现裂缝、水进入时，那些碳酸钙颗粒与水反应并封闭裂缝。于是混凝土基本上自我愈合、修复裂缝，并随时间变强。有趣的是，研究者很久就注意到罗马混凝土中的这些小块，却以为只是生产瑕疵，像有人没把配料拌匀。无论如何，考虑到现代混凝土寿命短，以及生产对环境有害，想到我们或许在未来建筑中使用这些古罗马技巧，相当令人兴奋。
