transcriptSentences.text: Have you ever thought about how ancient concrete structures like Roman amphitheaters and aqueducts have managed to last for thousands of years, while modern concrete buildings seem to fall apart and need replacing after just a few decades?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 你是否想过，罗马圆形剧场与高架渠等古代混凝土结构如何能存续数千年，而现代混凝土建筑似乎几十年就开裂、需要更换？

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: For a long time, researchers thought the secret to Roman concrete's durability was volcanic ash.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 长期来研究者以为罗马混凝土耐久的秘密是火山灰。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: That makes sense, since volcanic ash was a major ingredient, and it was described as such by architects and historians who were writing at the time.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这说得通，因为火山灰是主要成分，当时建筑师与历史学家也如此描述。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: But it turns out the real secret was actually tiny chunks of calcium carbonate.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但事实证明真正秘密其实是碳酸钙小块。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: These formed because the Romans used dry quicklime in their mix, instead of the way we make concrete today, called Portland cement, where lime gets mixed with water first and then blended with everything else.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们形成是因为罗马人在混合料中使用干生石灰，而不是我们今天做混凝土的方式——波特兰水泥，即先把石灰与水混合再与其他成分拌合。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: When cracks show up in Roman concrete and water enters, those calcium carbonate bits react with the water and seal up the cracks.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 当罗马混凝土出现裂缝、水进入时，那些碳酸钙颗粒与水反应并封闭裂缝。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: So the concrete basically heals itself, fixes the cracks, and gets stronger over time.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 于是混凝土基本上自我愈合、修复裂缝，并随时间变强。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: The funny thing is, researchers have noticed these chunks in Roman concrete for ages, but they just figured they were a production flaw, like someone didn't mix the ingredients well enough.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 有趣的是，研究者很久就注意到罗马混凝土中的这些小块，却以为只是生产瑕疵，像有人没把配料拌匀。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Man
transcriptSentences.text: Anyway, considering how short-lived modern concrete is, and the fact that making it is bad for the environment, it's pretty exciting to think we might use some of these ancient Roman tricks in future construction.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 无论如何，考虑到现代混凝土寿命短，以及生产对环境有害，想到我们或许在未来建筑中使用这些古罗马技巧，相当令人兴奋。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Human activities produce large amounts of organic waste like fruit scraps, yard waste and paper products. This waste can build up as trash. We can put it in landfills, but there it decomposes anaerobically — meaning without oxygen. Anaerobic decomposition results in the release of methane, a gas that significantly contributes to undesirable global warming.

But we have an alternative to landfills: composting. In composting, organic waste is broken down in special conditions by microorganisms, fungi, and sometimes insects. These organisms break down organic material into a dark, crumbly, earthy-smelling substance called humus. Unlike decomposition in landfills, composting occurs aerobically — or with oxygen — and therefore doesn't produce methane gas.

To compost effectively, you need the right balance of four things. One is nitrogen-rich materials, also known as greens — things like fruit and vegetable scraps. The second one is carbon-rich materials, or browns, like dry leaves, wood chips and paper waste. And you also need water and air, so the process does require proper management.

Humus, the primary product of composting, is full of essential nutrients. Adding it to soil enhances plant growth and increases agricultural yields. This reduces the need for chemical fertilizers. Humus-enriched soil also provides a habitat for microorganisms, insects and worms that in turn help decompose organic material and maintain soil health. This creates a virtuous circle of sorts.

In contrast, while chemical fertilizers can boost agricultural productivity in the short term, they are harmful to these beneficial organisms. They can actually damage the soil in the long run by killing the helpful organisms living in it.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段生物学课的讲座。

人类活动产生大量有机废物，如果皮、庭院废弃物与纸制品。这些废物可堆积成垃圾。我们可以放进填埋场，但在那里它厌氧分解——意思是无氧。厌氧分解释放甲烷，这种气体显著助长不良的全球变暖。

但我们有填埋场的替代：堆肥。堆肥中，有机废物在特殊条件下由微生物、真菌，有时还有昆虫分解。这些生物把有机物分解成深色、易碎、有泥土气味的物质，称为腐殖质。与填埋场分解不同，堆肥在有氧条件下发生——因此不产生甲烷。

要有效堆肥，需要四样东西的正确平衡。一是富氮材料，也称绿色物——如蔬果边角料。二是富碳材料，或称棕色物，如干叶、木屑与纸废。还需要水与空气，因此过程确实需要妥善管理。

腐殖质——堆肥的主要产物——充满必需养分。加入土壤可增强植物生长、提高农业产量。这减少对化肥的需要。富含腐殖质的土壤也为微生物、昆虫与蠕虫提供栖息地，它们反过来帮助分解有机物并维持土壤健康。这形成某种良性循环。

相比之下，化肥虽可短期提高农业生产力，却对这些有益生物有害。长远看，它们实际上会通过杀死土中有益生物而损害土壤。

versions.label: Koala 03-17
versions.transcript: Human activities produce large amounts of organic waste, like food scraps, yard waste, and paper products. This waste can build up as trash. We can put it in landfills, but there it decomposes anaerobically, meaning without oxygen. Anaerobic decomposition results in the release of methane, a gas that significantly contributes to undesirable global warming. But we have an alternative to landfills. Composting. In composting, organic waste is broken down in special conditions by microorganisms, fungi, and sometimes insects. These organisms break down organic material into a dark, crumbly, earthy smelling substance called humus. Unlike decomposition in landfills, composting occurs aerobically, or with oxygen, and therefore doesn't produce methane gas. To compost effectively, you need the right balance of four things. One is nitrogen rich materials, also known as greens, things like fruit and vegetable scraps. The second one is carbon rich materials, or browns, like dry leaves, wood chips, and paper waste. And you also need water and air. So the process does require proper management. Humus, the primary product of composting, is full of essential nutrients. Adding it to soil enhances plant growth and increases agricultural yields. This reduces the need for chemical fertilizers. Humus enriched soil also provides a habitat for microorganisms, insects, and worms that in turn help decompose organic material and maintain soil health. This creates a virtuous circle of sorts. In contrast, while chemical fertilizers can boost agricultural productivity in the short term, they are harmful to these beneficial organisms. They can actually damage the soil in the long run by killing the helpful organisms living in it.
versions.transcriptZh: 人类活动产生大量的有机垃圾，如食物残渣、庭院垃圾和纸制品。 这些垃圾会堆积成废弃物。 我们可以把它们放在垃圾填埋场，但在那里它们会进行厌氧分解，即在无氧环境下分解。 厌氧分解会导致甲烷的释放，这种气体是导致全球变暖的重要原因。 但除了填埋，我们还有另一种选择。 堆肥。 在堆肥过程中，有机垃圾在特殊条件下由微生物、真菌，有时还有昆虫进行分解。 这些生物将有机材料分解成一种深色的、易碎的、闻起来有泥土气息的物质，叫做腐殖质。 与填埋场中的分解不同，堆肥是好氧进行的，即有氧分解，因此不会产生甲烷气体。 为了有效地进行堆肥，你需要平衡好四种要素。 一是富氮材料，也被称为“绿色材料”，比如水果和蔬菜残渣。 二是富碳材料，或称“棕色材料”，比如枯叶、木屑和废纸。 你还需要水分和空气。 所以这个过程确实需要恰当的管理。 腐殖质作为堆肥的主要产物，富含基本营养成分。 将其加入土壤可以促进植物生长并提高农作物产量。 这减少了对化学肥料的需求。 富含腐殖质的土壤还为微生物、昆虫和蚯蚓提供了栖息地，它们反过来又帮助分解有机物质并维持土壤健康。 这创造了一种良性循环。 相比之下，虽然化肥可以在短期内提高农业生产力，但它们对这些有益生物是有害的。 从长远来看，它们实际上会因为杀死了土壤中生活的有益生物而破坏土壤。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a biology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Man: You've probably heard that ants can carry 50 times their own body weight. Amazing, right? Ants also have, on the front of their heads, strong mandibles. Mandibles are like jaws, though ants use them like pincers or grippers, similar to how humans use our thumb and index finger to pick things up. Now, ants' mandibles, their inner surfaces, are covered in tiny hairs. And researchers working on biomimicry, which means imitating nature in human inventions, recently wondered if they could use this idea in a robot gripper. A robot gripper is a device with flat plates that come together to pick things up. But it's difficult to pick up packaging with curved edges, so manufacturers often use grippers with three plates for stability. Three plates are bulky and harder to operate, making them awkward. So, the researchers built a robot gripper with two plates, adding tiny artificial hairs and copying ants' mandibles, and another gripper with just two smooth plates. They conducted over 2,000 tests, an astonishing number, I think, comparing how well the grippers picked up items like a cereal box and a shampoo bottle. The hairy gripper was at least 29 percent better at grabbing and holding onto items. Its grip was more gentle and more secure.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段生物学课的讲座。

男：你大概听说过蚂蚁能搬动自身体重五十倍的东西。神奇，对吧？蚂蚁头部前方还有强壮的大颚。大颚像颌，不过蚂蚁像钳子或夹具那样用它们，类似人类用拇指与食指抓东西。蚂蚁大颚的内表面覆盖着细毛。从事仿生学——意思是在人类发明中模仿自然——的研究者最近想知道能否把这一想法用于机器人夹爪。机器人夹爪是用平板合拢抓取物体的装置。但抓取带曲面边缘的包装很难，所以制造商常为稳定性使用三板夹爪。三板笨重、更难操作，显得别扭。于是研究者做了带两板并加微小人造毛、模仿蚂蚁大颚的机器人夹爪，以及只有两块光滑板的另一夹爪。他们做了超过两千次测试——我认为数量惊人——比较夹爪抓取麦片盒与洗发水瓶等物品的表现。带毛夹爪在抓取与持物上至少好百分之二十九。其抓握更轻柔也更稳固。

versions.transcript: You've probably heard that ants can carry 50 times their own body weight. Amazing, right? Ants also, out on the front of their heads, they have strong mandibles. Mandibles are like jaws, though ants use them like pincers, grippers, like how humans use our thumb and index finger to pick things up. Now, ants' mandibles, their inner surfaces, are covered in tiny hairs. And researchers working on biomimicry: biomimicry means imitating nature in human inventions. A group of researchers studying ant mandibles and their hairs recently wondered if they could use biomimicry with a robot gripper. So, a robot gripper is a device with flat plates that come together to pick things up. But it's difficult to pick up packaging with curved edges, so manufacturers often use grippers with three plates for stability. But three plates are bulky and harder to operate. You know, awkward. So, the researchers built a robot gripper with two plates with tiny artificial hairs copying ants' mandibles. And another gripper, with just the two smooth plates. They did an experiment with over 2,000 tests, an astonishing number, I think, comparing how well the grippers picked up items like a cereal box and a shampoo bottle. Well, the hairy gripper was at least 29% better at grabbing and holding onto items. Its grip was more gentle and more secure.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a history class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class.

Man: Before we say any more about textiles, let's talk about the historical indigo trade. Indigo is a natural blue dye that comes from the leaves of Indigofera plants. Today, you see it most often in blue jeans. Indigo was a staple export for hundreds of years. There was a time when only rice was more valuable. The English began importing it during the early 1600s from India, and British colonists started growing it in North America about a century later. Natural indigo nearly vanished from industrial use by the early 20th century after German chemists invented a synthetic alternative. This was cheaper and more efficient for large-scale production. For decades, natural indigo survived only in niche applications and local traditions. Today, indigo is back as a viable commercial crop in places like Bangladesh and the United States. This is partly thanks to the fashion industry's efforts to be more environmentally sustainable, and many now see natural indigo as a symbol of ethical consumption. Its value as a commodity also lies in its versatility. It is also used in cosmetics and food coloring. Farmers find it to be low maintenance with high returns. One hectare can yield thousands of kilograms of leaves. The economic incentive is clear: minimal input, high output, and growing international interest. That said, the traditional fermentation techniques for extracting the dye are extremely labor-intensive, which makes natural indigo expensive. And some producers claiming natural methods still rely on harsh chemicals, which undermines the dye's eco-friendly reputation.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段历史课的讲座。

男：在继续谈纺织品之前，我们先谈历史上的靛蓝贸易。靛蓝是来自木蓝属植物叶子的天然蓝色染料。今天你最常见于蓝色牛仔裤。靛蓝数百年都是大宗出口。曾有一段时间只有大米比它更值钱。英国人在十七世纪初开始从印度进口，英国殖民者约一个世纪后在北美开始种植。二十世纪初德国化学家发明合成替代品后，天然靛蓝几乎从工业用途中消失。合成品对大规模生产更便宜、更高效。数十年间，天然靛蓝只存活于小众应用与地方传统。今天，靛蓝在孟加拉与美国等地重新成为可行的经济作物。这部分得益于时装业更环保可持续的努力，许多人现把天然靛蓝视为伦理消费的象征。其作为商品的价值也在于多用途。它还用于化妆品与食用色素。农民觉得它维护成本低、回报高。一公顷可产数千公斤叶子。经济激励明确：投入少、产出高、国际兴趣增长。尽管如此，提取染料的传统发酵技术极费劳力，使天然靛蓝昂贵。而且一些声称用天然方法的生产商仍依赖苛刻化学品，这削弱了该染料的环保声誉。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music class.

Man: Have you ever listened to a piece of music and suddenly felt like you were somewhere else? Maybe walking through a Brazilian street market or climbing a misty mountain trail in China? That's the magic of musical borrowing, a practice where artists blend elements from different global traditions to create something fresh and emotionally resonant. Take bossa nova, for example. It's a genre that merges the laid-back swing of United States jazz music with the rhythmic pulse of Brazilian samba. When you listen to bossa nova, it feels both familiar and new at the same time. But successful musical borrowing isn't just about mixing sounds. It's about respect. When artists draw from other cultures, they need to understand the traditions behind the music. Composer Tan Dun nails this in his score for the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon. He blends Chinese instruments like the erhu and pipa with Western orchestration, but not just for effect. The erhu's haunting tones and the pipa's intricate rhythms reflect centuries of Chinese musical storytelling. Tan Dun doesn't just borrow; he honors the culture, letting its emotional depth shine through. Of course, fusion isn't always seamless. Sometimes the mix feels forced or the original meaning gets lost. But when it works, when the traditions truly speak to each other, it's proof that music can be a universal language, capable of bridging worlds and telling stories that transcend borders.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段音乐课的讲座。

男：你是否曾听一段音乐突然感觉自己身在别处？也许走在巴西街市，或攀爬中国雾蒙蒙的山径？那是音乐借用的魔力——艺术家融合不同全球传统的元素，创造出新鲜且情感共鸣的东西。以波萨诺瓦为例。这一类型把美国爵士的慵懒摇摆与巴西桑巴的节奏脉动融合。听波萨诺瓦时，既熟悉又新颖。但成功的音乐借用不只是混音。它关乎尊重。当艺术家从其他文化汲取时，需要理解音乐背后的传统。作曲家谭盾在电影《卧虎藏龙》配乐中做到了这一点。他将二胡、琵琶等中国乐器与西方管弦乐融合，但不只为效果。二胡萦绕的音色与琵琶复杂的节奏反映数世纪中国音乐叙事。谭盾不只借用；他尊重文化，让其情感深度透出。当然，融合并非总是无缝。有时混合显得生硬，或原意丢失。但当它奏效、当传统真正彼此对话时，证明音乐可以是通用语言，能够连接世界、讲述跨越边界的故事。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a business class.

Woman: Today we're discussing the concept of dark stores, which are retail centers that resemble warehouses and are usually located near city centers. Unlike traditional storefronts, they are not designed for walk-in customers, but function as fulfillment hubs optimized for rapid online delivery. The rise of dark stores has been fueled by the growing demand for online shopping, especially in urban areas where space is limited and rent is high. The main appeal of dark stores lies in their efficiency. By eliminating the traditional storefront, businesses can reduce overhead and pass savings on to consumers through lower prices. Their proximity to dense urban areas also allows for faster delivery times, meeting the expectations of customers who value speed and convenience. For instance, a company might deliver groceries in under an hour, giving it a major competitive advantage over traditional supermarkets. However, dark stores are not without drawbacks. Their expansion can contribute to the decline of traditional retail spaces, creating economic challenges for local businesses. Employment is another concern. While these centers generate jobs in logistics and delivery, they may reduce the number of customer-facing roles available in physical stores. Looking ahead, many experts predict that dark stores will continue to reshape the retail landscape. Some may adopt advanced automation, further reducing the need for human labor and potentially redefining the shopping experience itself. As with other technological shifts, the key challenge will be balancing efficiency with the broader social and economic implications of these changes.

请听一段商业课的讲座。

女：今天我们讨论暗店概念：形似仓库、通常位于市中心附近的零售中心。与传统店面不同，它们不为进店顾客设计，而是作为为快速线上配送优化的履约枢纽。暗店兴起受线上购物需求增长推动，尤其在空间有限、租金高的城市地区。暗店主要吸引力在于效率。通过取消传统店面，企业可降低开销，并以更低价格把节省转给消费者。靠近人口密集城区也使配送更快，满足看重速度与便利的顾客期望。例如，公司可在一小时内送达杂货，相对传统超市形成重大竞争优势。但暗店并非没有缺点。其扩张可加剧传统零售空间衰退，给本地企业带来经济挑战。就业是另一关切。这些中心在物流与配送中创造岗位，但可能减少实体店中面向顾客的角色数量。展望未来，许多专家预测暗店将继续重塑零售格局。有些可能采用先进自动化，进一步减少人力需求，并潜在重新定义购物体验本身。与其他技术变革一样，关键挑战将是在效率与这些变化更广的社会与经济影响之间取得平衡。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Narrator
transcriptSentences.text: Listen to a talk in a business class.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 请听一段商业课的讲座。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: Today we're discussing the concept of dark stores, which are retail centers that resemble warehouses and are usually located near city centers.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 今天我们讨论暗店概念：形似仓库、通常位于市中心附近的零售中心。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: Unlike traditional storefronts, they are not designed for walk-in customers, but function as fulfillment hubs optimized for rapid online delivery.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 与传统店面不同，它们不为进店顾客设计，而是作为为快速线上配送优化的履约枢纽。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: The rise of dark stores has been fueled by the growing demand for online shopping, especially in urban areas where space is limited and rent is high.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 暗店兴起受线上购物需求增长推动，尤其在空间有限、租金高的城市地区。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: The main appeal of dark stores lies in their efficiency.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 暗店主要吸引力在于效率。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: By eliminating the traditional storefront, businesses can reduce overhead and pass savings on to consumers through lower prices.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 通过取消传统店面，企业可降低开销，并以更低价格把节省转给消费者。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: Their proximity to dense urban areas also allows for faster delivery times, meeting the expectations of customers who value speed and convenience.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 靠近人口密集城区也使配送更快，满足看重速度与便利的顾客期望。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: For instance, a company might deliver groceries in under an hour, giving it a major competitive advantage over traditional supermarkets.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 例如，公司可在一小时内送达杂货，相对传统超市形成重大竞争优势。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: However, dark stores are not without drawbacks.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但暗店并非没有缺点。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: Their expansion can contribute to the decline of traditional retail spaces, creating economic challenges for local businesses.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 其扩张可加剧传统零售空间衰退，给本地企业带来经济挑战。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: Employment is another concern.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 就业是另一关切。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: While these centers generate jobs in logistics and delivery, they may reduce the number of customer-facing roles available in physical stores.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这些中心在物流与配送中创造岗位，但可能减少实体店中面向顾客的角色数量。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: Looking ahead, many experts predict that dark stores will continue to reshape the retail landscape.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 展望未来，许多专家预测暗店将继续重塑零售格局。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: Some may adopt advanced automation, further reducing the need for human labor and potentially redefining the shopping experience itself.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 有些可能采用先进自动化，进一步减少人力需求，并潜在重新定义购物体验本身。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Woman
transcriptSentences.text: As with other technological shifts, the key challenge will be balancing efficiency with the broader social and economic implications of these changes.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 与其他技术变革一样，关键挑战将是在效率与这些变化更广的社会与经济影响之间取得平衡。

questions.promptText: What aspect of dark stores does the speaker mainly discuss?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者主要讨论了暗店的哪个方面？

choices.label: Their influence on the retail market and society.
choices.labelZh: 它们对零售市场和社会的影响。
choices.explanationZh: 正确。讲座从效率和低价讲到传统零售空间、就业和 automation，核心是 dark stores 对零售和社会的影响。

choices.label: Their architectural design and layout.
choices.labelZh: 它们的建筑设计和布局。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。warehouse-like 只是定义，没展开建筑设计。

choices.label: Their similarities to traditional storefronts.
choices.labelZh: 它们与传统店面的相似之处。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。原文强调 Unlike traditional storefronts，不是相似。

choices.label: Their role in the history of warehouse development.
choices.labelZh: 它们在仓库发展史中的作用。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。没有讲仓库发展史。

questions.promptText: According to the talk, why can dark stores offer lower prices?
questions.promptTextZh: 根据讲座，暗店为何能提供更低的价格？

choices.label: Because they sell large quantities of goods.
choices.labelZh: 因为它们销售大量商品。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。原文没有说靠销量大降价。

choices.label: Because they are not focused on making a profit.
choices.labelZh: 因为它们不以盈利为主要目标。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。没有说它们不追求利润。

choices.label: Because they obtain less expensive products.
choices.labelZh: 因为它们能获得更便宜的产品。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。没有提进货更便宜。

choices.label: Because they have lower overhead expenses.
choices.labelZh: 因为它们的运营开销更低。
choices.explanationZh: 正确。原文说 by eliminating the traditional storefront, businesses can reduce overhead and pass savings on to consumers。

questions.promptText: Why does the speaker mention grocery delivery?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者为何提到食品杂货配送？

choices.label: To illustrate how dark stores compete with traditional supermarkets.
choices.labelZh: 为了说明暗店如何与传统超市竞争。
choices.explanationZh: 正确。原文用 groceries in under an hour 说明 dark stores 比 traditional supermarkets 有 competitive advantage。

choices.label: To compare delivery speeds in urban and nonurban environments.
choices.labelZh: 为了比较城市与非城市的配送速度。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。没有比较城市和非城市。

choices.label: To suggest that dark stores mainly sell perishable items.
choices.labelZh: 为了暗示暗店主要销售易腐商品。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。groceries 是例子，不代表主要只卖生鲜。

choices.label: To explain why consumers are willing to pay higher fees.
choices.labelZh: 为了解释为何消费者愿意支付更高费用。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。原文强调 lower prices 和 speed，不是 higher fees。

questions.promptText: What point does the speaker make about dark stores and employment?

choices.label: Employees in dark stores need to be comfortable with technology.
choices.labelZh: 暗店员工需要熟悉科技操作。
choices.explanationZh: 不选。automation 是未来趋势，但没有说员工必须熟悉技术。

choices.label: Dark stores do not need many in-store workers.
choices.labelZh: 暗店不需要很多店内员工。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a biology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.

Man: Frogs aren't just known for their croaks and leaps; they're key players in ecosystems, acting as both predators and prey. But scientists have been sounding the alarm: frog populations are shrinking fast across the globe. One major reason is chemical pollution. Pesticides and other pollutants often end up in the water where frogs live and breed. These chemicals interfere with their reproductive systems, leading to fewer eggs and developmental issues in tadpoles. Over time, this can cause entire populations to collapse. Another serious threat is disease, especially a fungus called chytrid. This fungus attacks the skin of frogs, which is vital for absorbing water and regulating electrolytes. Infected frogs often become lethargic, lose coordination, and eventually die. Chytrid has spread rapidly and is responsible for declines and extinctions in hundreds of frog species worldwide. It's one of the most devastating wildlife diseases ever recorded. Why is this problematic? Frogs also serve as indicators of environmental health because they're so sensitive to changes in water quality and temperature. Their decline often signals deeper ecological problems. Bees play a similar role. When bee populations drop, it can point to issues like pesticide overuse or habitat stress. When frogs and bees are struggling, it's a warning sign that the environment needs attention.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段生物学课的讲座。

男：青蛙不只以呱呱叫和跳跃闻名；它们是生态系统中的关键角色，既是捕食者也是猎物。但科学家一直在敲警钟：全球青蛙种群正在快速萎缩。一个主要原因是化学污染。杀虫剂与其他污染物常进入青蛙生活繁殖的水域。这些化学物质干扰其生殖系统，导致卵减少、蝌蚪发育问题。久而久之，可导致整个种群崩溃。另一严重威胁是疾病，尤其是一种叫壶菌的真菌。这种真菌攻击青蛙皮肤，而皮肤对吸水与调节电解质至关重要。受感染青蛙常变得嗜睡、失去协调，最终死亡。壶菌传播迅速，对全球数百种青蛙的衰退与灭绝负有责任。它是有记录以来最具毁灭性的野生动物疾病之一。为何成问题？青蛙也是环境健康的指示者，因为它们对水质与温度变化极敏感。其衰退常预示更深的生态问题。蜜蜂起类似作用。蜜蜂种群下降时，可指向杀虫剂过度使用或栖息地压力等问题。当青蛙与蜜蜂都在挣扎时，是环境需要关注的警告信号。

versions.transcript: Frogs aren't just their croaks and leaps. They're key players in ecosystems, acting as both predators and prey. But scientists have been sounding the alarm. Frog populations are shrinking fast across the globe. One major reason is chemical pollution. Pesticides and other pollutants often end up in the water where frogs live and breed. These chemicals interfere with their reproductive systems, leading to fewer eggs and developmental issues in tadpoles. Over time, this can cause entire populations to collapse. Another serious threat is disease, especially a fungus called chytrid. This fungus attacks the skin of frogs, which is vital for absorbing water and regulating electrolytes. Infected frogs often become lethargic, lose coordination, and eventually die. Chytrid has spread rapidly and is responsible for declines and extinctions in hundreds of frog species worldwide. It's one of the most devastating wildlife diseases ever recorded. Why is this problematic? Frogs also serve as indicators of environmental health. Because they're so sensitive to changes in water quality and temperature, their decline often signals deeper ecological problems. Bees play a similar role. When bee populations drop, it can point to issues like pesticide overuse or habitat stress. So when frogs and bees are struggling, it's a warning sign that the environment needs attention.
versions.transcriptZh: 青蛙不仅仅只会呱呱叫和跳跃。 它们是生态系统中的关键角色，既是捕食者也是猎物。 但是科学家们一直在敲响警钟。 全球范围内的青蛙数量正在迅速减少。 一个主要原因是化学污染。 杀虫剂和其他污染物经常最终流入青蛙生活和繁殖的水域。 这些化学物质会干扰它们的生殖系统，导致产卵数量减少以及蝌蚪的发育问题。 随着时间的推移，这会导致整个种群的崩溃。 另一个严重的威胁是疾病，特别是一种叫做壶菌的真菌。 这种真菌会攻击青蛙的皮肤，而皮肤对于青蛙吸收水分和调节电解质至关重要。 受感染的青蛙通常会变得昏昏欲睡，失去协调能力，最终死亡。 壶菌传播迅速，并导致了全球数百种青蛙的减少和灭绝。 这是有史以来记录在案的破坏性最强的野生动物疾病之一。 为什么这会成为一个严重的问题？ 青蛙也是环境健康的指示器。 因为它们对水质和温度的变化非常敏感，它们的减少通常预示着更深层次的生态问题。 蜜蜂也扮演着类似的角色。 当蜜蜂数量下降时，它可以指示出诸如杀虫剂过度使用或栖息地压力等问题。 因此，当青蛙和蜜蜂艰难生存时，这是一个警告信号，表明环境需要关注。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a physics class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a physics class.

Man: Today we're going to explore a phenomenon called thin film interference. This is an optical effect that occurs when light interacts with very thin surfaces. Imagine a soap bubble floating in the air. Although it's made of clear liquid, it shines with shifting rainbow colors. Thin film interference explains how this shimmering display occurs when light strikes a bubble. Some light reflects off the outer surface, and some reflects off the inner surface. As these waves meet, they can either reinforce one another or cancel each other out. If the waves reinforce one another, the color looks brighter. This is called constructive interference because the waves are building the light. If the waves cancel each other out, the color fades. This is called destructive interference because the waves are negating each other's effect. Which color appears depends on factors that constantly change, such as the thickness of the film and the angle of the incoming light. As these factors shift, some wavelengths are reinforced while others are canceled, producing the bubble's rainbow shimmer. The thin film that creates these dazzling colors also makes the bubble fragile, because the layer is so delicate. The bubble can burst with the slightest touch or breeze. Scientists are interested in applying thin-film interference to technology. Possible uses include paints that shine with bright colors without pigments, and anti-reflective coatings for lenses. However, achieving a reproducible natural balance of simplicity and efficiency remains a significant challenge.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段物理课的讲座。

男：今天我们探索一种叫薄膜干涉的现象。这是光与极薄表面相互作用时发生的光学效应。想象空中漂浮的肥皂泡。虽然由透明液体构成，它却闪耀着变幻的彩虹色。薄膜干涉解释了光打在泡上时这种闪烁如何发生。一些光从外表面反射，一些从内表面反射。这些波相遇时，要么相互加强，要么相互抵消。若波相互加强，颜色显得更亮。这叫相长干涉，因为波在叠加光。若波相互抵消，颜色变淡。这叫相消干涉，因为波在抵消彼此的效果。出现哪种颜色取决于不断变化的因素，如薄膜厚度与入射光角度。这些因素变化时，某些波长被加强而另一些被抵消，产生泡的彩虹闪烁。制造这些炫目色彩的薄膜也使泡脆弱，因为那一层极细。最轻微的触碰或微风就能使泡破裂。科学家有兴趣把薄膜干涉应用于技术。可能用途包括无需颜料即可闪耀亮色的涂料，以及镜头的抗反射涂层。然而，实现可复现的自然简洁与效率平衡仍是重大挑战。

versions.transcript: Today we're going to explore a phenomenon called thin film interference. This is an optical effect that occurs when light interacts with very thin surfaces. Imagine a soap bubble floating in the air. Although it's made of clear liquid, it shines with shifting rainbow colors. Thin film interference explains how this shimmering display occurs. When light strikes a bubble, some reflects off the outer surface, and some reflects off the inner surface. As these waves meet, they can either work together or work against each other. If they reinforce one another, the color looks brighter. This is called constructive interference because the waves are building the light. If the waves hit each other and cancel each other out, the color fades. This is destructive interference. Which color appears depends on changing factors like the thickness of the film and the angle of the light. As these factors shift, some wavelengths are reinforced while others are canceled, and that constant change is what produces the bubble's rainbow shimmer. The thin film that creates these dazzling colors also makes the bubble fragile. Because the layer is so delicate, the bubble can burst with the slightest touch or breeze. Scientists are interested in applying thin film interference to technology. Possible uses include paints that shine with bright colors without pigments and anti reflective coatings for lenses. Yet reproducing the bubble's natural balance of simplicity and efficiency remains a significant challenge.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天我们要探讨一种被称为“薄膜干涉”的现象。 这是一种在光与极薄表面相互作用时发生的各种光学效应。 想象一下悬浮在空中的肥皂泡。 虽然它是由透明液体组成的，但却闪烁着变幻的彩虹光泽。 薄膜干涉解释了这种绚丽色彩是如何产生的。 当光线照射到气泡上时，一部分光从外表面反射，另一部分则从内表面反射。 当这些波相遇时，它们会相互增强或相互抵消。 如果它们相互增强，颜色看起来就会更亮。 这被称为相长干涉，因为这些波正在增强光线。 如果波相互碰撞并抵消，颜色就会褪去。 这就是“相消干涉”。 出现哪种颜色取决于薄膜厚度和光线角度等不断变化的因素。 随着这些因素的偏移，一些波长被增强而另一些被抵消，这种持续的变化产生了气泡的彩虹光泽。 产生这些耀眼色彩的薄膜也使气泡变得脆弱。 由于薄层非常微妙，气泡稍有触碰或微风吹过就会破裂。 科学家们对将薄膜干涉应用于技术领域很感兴趣。 可能的用途包括不含颜料即可闪烁亮丽色彩的油漆，以及镜片的增透膜（抗反射涂层）。 然而，复制气泡那种简单与高效的自然平衡仍然是一个重大的挑战。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a history class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class. 
The Age of Exploration extended from the 15th century to the 17th century, but long before this, seafarers were venturing into unfamiliar waters using remarkably sophisticated techniques. One notable example is Pytheas of Massalia, a Greek explorer from the 4th century BCE. He sailed from the Mediterranean to the northern reaches of Europe, possibly reaching Britain and even Iceland. Without modern instruments, Pytheas relied on coastal landmarks, the position of the sun and stars, and careful observation of ocean tides and daylight patterns. His journey demonstrated that long-distance navigation was possible through keen environmental awareness and methodical planning. Centuries later, European explorers expanded on these early achievements with the help of new technologies. Among the most transformative was the magnetic compass, which used a magnetized needle to indicate direction. Originally developed in China and later adopted in Europe, the compass allowed sailors to maintain a heading even when celestial bodies were obscured by clouds or fog. This innovation enabled mariners to venture into open seas with greater confidence and precision. Historians note that the compass didn't just improve navigation; it transformed it. It allowed explorers like Vasco da Gama and Ferdinand Magellan to chart new maritime routes across vast oceans, connecting continents and reshaping global trade. Combined with other tools like the astrolabe and improved ship designs, the compass helped usher in the Age of Exploration.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段历史课的讲座。
大航海时代从十五世纪延伸到十七世纪，但在此之前很久，航海者就用极为精密的技术驶入陌生水域。一个显著例子是马萨利亚的皮西亚斯，公元前四世纪的希腊探险家。他从地中海航行到欧洲北部，可能到达不列颠甚至冰岛。没有现代仪器，皮西亚斯依靠海岸地标、日月星辰位置，以及对海潮与日照模式的仔细观察。他的旅程证明，通过敏锐的环境意识与有条不紊的计划，长距离导航是可能的。数世纪后，欧洲探险家借助新技术扩展了这些早期成就。最具变革性的之一是磁罗盘，用磁化指针指示方向。罗盘原产中国、后被欧洲采用，使水手即使在云雾遮蔽天体时也能保持航向。这一创新使航海者能更自信、更精确地驶入公海。历史学家指出，罗盘不只改进了导航；它改变了导航。它使瓦斯科·达·伽马与费迪南德·麦哲伦等探险家能在浩瀚大洋上开辟新航线，连接大陆并重塑全球贸易。结合星盘等其他工具与改进的船舶设计，罗盘帮助开启了大航海时代。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a social science podcast.

Man: Today, we're exploring a fascinating concept in social psychology known as pluralistic ignorance. Pluralistic ignorance describes a situation where the majority of members in a group privately reject a norm or standard, but incorrectly assume that most others accept it. This often results in everyone conforming to a norm they don't truly agree with. A classic example occurs in workplace overtime culture. Many employees might prefer to leave work on time, but they stay late because everyone else is committed to working extra hours. In reality, most colleagues also wish to leave on time, but fear appearing less dedicated. Research highlights this dynamic when employees are asked privately about their preferences. Many express a desire for better work-life balance, despite their public behavior suggesting enthusiasm for long hours. Pluralistic ignorance has broad implications beyond the workplace. Notably, it can perpetuate social stereotypes and hinder societal change, as individuals might hesitate to voice dissenting opinions, thinking they are in the minority. However, overcoming pluralistic ignorance has powerful benefits. When even one person speaks up, it can embolden others to express their true beliefs, potentially leading to a shift in group norms and to more honest, authentic communities. There is a challenge, and it's a big one. Being the first to speak out often requires courage, as it can put one's social standing among peers at risk.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段社会科学播客的讲座。

男：今天我们探讨社会心理学中一个迷人概念：多元无知。多元无知描述这样一种情形：群体中多数成员私下拒绝某规范或标准，却错误地假定多数他人接受它。这常导致人人从众于自己并不真正认同的规范。经典例子出现在职场加班文化中。许多员工可能更想准时下班，却因别人都坚持加班而留下。实际上多数同事也想准时走，但怕显得不够敬业。研究在私下询问员工偏好时凸显了这一动态。许多人表达希望更好的工作生活平衡，尽管公开行为暗示对长时间工作的热情。多元无知的影响远超职场。尤其它可延续社会刻板印象、阻碍社会变革，因为个人可能犹豫表达异议，以为自己是少数。但克服多元无知有强大益处。哪怕一人发声，也可鼓舞他人表达真实信念，潜在导致群体规范转变与更诚实真实的共同体。挑战很大。第一个发声常需要勇气，因为可能危及自己在同辈中的社会地位。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class.

Woman: Today, let's talk about the effects of the Industrial Revolution on urban life in Europe. Last week, we talked about how between the 16th and the 19th centuries, industrial capitalism utterly changed the European economy. As manufacturing became the most profitable activity, cities naturally grew larger and took on new character. By 1850, the physical layout of an industrial city was completely different from that of its predecessors. How do we picture a medieval city? It's surrounded by walls to protect it from invasion from the neighboring city. The emergence of nation-states did away with this need for protection from invasion, at least on the city scale. And so, over the centuries, the walls were removed and city boundaries pushed out dramatically. Industrial workplaces had been small craft shops, but now they were huge factories located in large factory districts with separate housing for workers constructed nearby. Medieval street layouts that had developed haphazardly were built over, replaced by a gridiron street pattern. Each lot was uniform and predictable, which made it easier to buy and sell property. Many cities kept their central marketplaces, but commercial structures became more prominent in city centers, often more so than cathedrals. Manchester, England, is a good example of this. It grew rapidly during the Industrial Revolution, and commercial buildings dominated the city center. Its layout reflected the new priorities of industrial capitalism.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段历史课的讲座。

女：今天我们谈工业革命对欧洲城市生活的影响。上周我们谈过十六至十九世纪间，工业资本主义如何彻底改变欧洲经济。随着制造业成为最赚钱的活动，城市自然变大并呈现新面貌。到一八五〇年，工业城市的物理布局与前代完全不同。我们如何想象中世纪城市？它被城墙环绕，以防邻城入侵。民族国家的出现消除了这种防入侵需要，至少在城市尺度上。于是数世纪间城墙拆除，城市边界大幅外推。工业工作场所曾是小作坊，如今是位于大厂区的巨型工厂，附近另建工人住房。中世纪杂乱发展的街道布局被覆盖，代之以棋盘格街网。每块地块统一可预期，更易买卖房产。许多城市保留中央市场，但商业建筑在市中心更突出，往往超过大教堂。英格兰曼彻斯特是好例子。工业革命期间它迅速扩张，商业建筑主导市中心。其布局反映了工业资本主义的新优先事项。

versions.transcript: Today, let's talk about the effects of the Industrial Revolution on urban life in Europe. Last week, we talked about how between the 16th and the 19th centuries, industrial capitalism utterly changed the European economy. As manufacturing became the most profitable activity, cities naturally grew larger and took on a new character. By 1850, the physical layout of an industrial city was completely different from that of its predecessors. How do we picture a medieval city? It's surrounded by walls to protect it from invasion from the neighboring city. The emergence of nation states did away with this need for protection from invasion, at least on the city scale. And so, over the centuries, the walls were removed and city boundaries pushed out dramatically. Industrial workplaces had been small craft shops, but now they were huge factories located in large factory districts, with separate housing for workers constructed nearby. Medieval street layouts that had developed haphazardly were built over, replaced by a gridiron street pattern. Each lot was uniform and predictable, which made it easier to buy and sell property. Many cities kept their central marketplaces, but commercial structures became more and more common. Commercial buildings became more prominent in city centers, often more so than cathedrals. Manchester, England, is a good example of this. It grew rapidly during the Industrial Revolution, and commercial buildings dominated the city center. Its layout reflected the new priorities of industrial capitalism.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a marine biology podcast.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a marine biology podcast.

Woman: There are many species out there that we wouldn't expect to see flying. Mammals, reptiles... one fascinating creature is the flying squid. Now, squid have fins, arms, tentacles, and gills for breathing. Their main body, the mantle, is basically a tube of muscle that water goes inside of while they swim. When this mantle clamps shut, it pumps the water out, which propels the squid through water quite quickly. It's like a little jetpack. And flying squid are able to propel themselves right up through the ocean's surface and into the air above. Another unexpected flying creature is the flying squirrel, which can simply glide, sometimes quickly and for long distances, between tree branches. However, unlike the flying squirrel, flying squid not only glide but can actually propel themselves upward. And, well, flying squid can accelerate as fast as a car, getting up to 100 kilometers per hour in about a second. Then the squid extends its tentacles and arms, and it has membranes between them that spread out and help the squid glide for several seconds, a bit like temporary wings. A squid in flight is likely to be fleeing from an underwater predator or a boat. There are some alternative theories, though. One is that it's a migration strategy, since moving through the air takes less energy and time than moving through water.

请听一段海洋生物学播客的讲座。

女：有许多我们想不到会飞的物种。哺乳动物、爬行动物……一种迷人的生物是飞鱿。鱿鱼有鳍、腕、触手以及呼吸用的鳃。其主体——外套膜——基本是一段肌肉管，游泳时水进入其中。外套膜夹紧时把水泵出，从而相当快地推动鱿鱼在水中前进。就像一个小喷气背包。飞鱿能把自己一直推出海面进入空中。另一种意外的飞行生物是飞鼠，它只是在树枝间滑翔，有时很快、距离很长。但与飞鼠不同，飞鱿不仅滑翔，还能实际上向上推进。而且飞鱿加速可像汽车一样快，约一秒内达到每小时一百公里。然后鱿鱼伸展触手与腕，其间有膜张开，帮助鱿鱼滑翔数秒，有点像临时翅膀。飞行中的鱿鱼很可能是在逃离水下捕食者或船只。不过也有其他理论。一种是这是迁徙策略，因为在空中移动比在水中更省能量与时间。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on an art podcast.

Woman: Today I'd like to talk about the color blue in art. Now, we might take blue for granted, but for centuries, it was one of the most elusive and expensive pigments an artist could use. In ancient Egypt, artisans crafted blue from lapis lazuli, a brilliant stone mined in what is now Afghanistan. This mineral was so rare and so valuable that it was literally worth its weight in gold. Because of its scarcity, blue was reserved for the most honored subjects in art. In medieval European paintings, important holy figures were often cloaked in deep blue robes. This wasn't just symbolic; it was also a financial statement. During the Renaissance, oil paints made the mixing and layering of colors easier, including the mixing of lapis lazuli powder with oil. Still, blue remained costly due to its natural sources. Then came a turning point in the 18th century: synthetic dyes. Prussian blue, which was originally created in Germany quite by accident, was affordable, vibrant, and widely accessible. Suddenly, artists from all walks of life could use blue freely. This democratization of color transformed artistic expression and opened doors for artistic movements like Impressionism, where blue was used freely to evoke mood, atmosphere, and emotion. Even today, blue carries echoes of its luxurious past. It's often linked to ideas of calm, depth, and aspiration. Yet some traditionalists still argue that no synthetic pigment can match the richness and depth of lapis lazuli. The story of blue continues to reflect the evolving relationship between art, innovation, and culture.

请听一段艺术播客的讲座。

女：今天想谈艺术中的蓝色。我们或许把蓝色视为理所当然，但数世纪里它曾是艺术家可用的最难求、最昂贵颜料之一。在古埃及，工匠用青金石制蓝，这种亮丽宝石开采于今阿富汗一带。该矿物稀少珍贵，简直与同等重量的黄金等值。因稀缺，蓝色专用于艺术中最尊贵的题材。中世纪欧洲绘画中，重要圣像常披深蓝袍。这不只是象征；也是财力声明。文艺复兴时期，油画使混色与叠色更容易，包括把青金石粉与油混合。但因天然来源，蓝色仍昂贵。转折出现在十八世纪：合成染料。普鲁士蓝最初在德国偶然制成，价格亲民、色彩鲜艳、获取广泛。突然间，各阶层艺术家都能自由用蓝。这种颜色民主化改变了艺术表达，并为印象派等运动打开大门——印象派中蓝色被自由用来唤起情绪、氛围与情感。即便今日，蓝色仍带着其奢华过往的回响。它常与平静、深度与志向相连。但一些传统派仍认为没有合成颜料能匹敌青金石的丰富与深度。蓝色的故事继续反映艺术、创新与文化之间不断演变的关系。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a lecture in an astrobiology class.

Woman: In 1967, astronomer Carl Sagan and biologist Harold Morowitz published a provocative paper in the journal Nature. At the time, most scientists assumed extraterrestrial life could only exist on planets with Earth-like surfaces, moderate temperatures, liquid water, and a solid ground to stand on. Sagan and Morowitz challenged that assumption. They argued that while Venus's surface is far too hot for life, hot enough to melt lead, the planet's upper cloud layers were a different story. About 50 kilometers above the surface, temperatures and pressures resemble those on Earth's surface. They speculated that microbial life could survive in those clouds, floating in droplets of sulfuric acid and water vapor, adapted to extreme acidity and using sunlight as a source of energy. To make their case, Sagan and Morowitz pointed to earthly analogs: microbes thriving in the acidic hot springs of Yellowstone National Park in the United States. These springs are pools heated by geothermal energy, rich in minerals, and often highly acidic. Yet certain extremophiles, microbes adapted to harsh conditions, flourish there, using chemical reactions to survive. If life can adapt to boiling, acidic water on Earth, they reasoned, why not to acidic clouds on Venus? Their argument was speculative, but it cracked open the idea that life is not confined to Earth-like surfaces, which is significant because a large percentage of the planets in the universe don't even have a solid surface at all.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段天体生物学课的讲座。

女：一九六七年，天文学家卡尔·萨根与生物学家哈罗德·莫罗维茨在《自然》杂志发表了一篇挑衅性论文。当时多数科学家假定地外生命只能存在于有类地表面、适中温度、液态水与可站立的坚实地面的行星上。萨根与莫罗维茨挑战了这一假定。他们认为，虽然金星表面对生命过热——热到能熔化铅——但该行星上层云层是另一回事。地表上方约五十公里处，温度与气压类似地球表面。他们推测微生物生命可在那些云中存活，漂浮在硫酸与水蒸气液滴中，适应极端酸性并以阳光为能量源。为支持论点，萨根与莫罗维茨指向地球类比：在美国黄石国家公园酸性温泉中繁盛的微生物。这些温泉是地热加热的池子，富含矿物，常高度酸性。但某些极端微生物——适应严酷条件的微生物——在那里兴旺，用化学反应存活。他们推理：若生命能适应地球上沸腾的酸性水，为何不能适应金星的酸性云？其论证是推测性的，但撬开了生命不限于类地表面的想法；这很重要，因为宇宙中很大比例的行星甚至根本没有坚实表面。

versions.transcript: In 1967, astronomer Carl Sagan and biologist Harold Morowitz published a provocative paper in the journal Nature. At the time, most scientists assumed extraterrestrial life could only exist on planets with Earth like surfaces, moderate temperatures, liquid water, and a solid ground to stand on. Sagan and Morowitz challenged that assumption. They argued that while Venus' surface is far too hot for life, hot enough to melt lead, the planet's upper cloud layers were a different story. About 50 kilometers above the surface, temperatures and pressures resemble those on Earth's surface. They speculated that microbial life could survive in those clouds, floating in droplets of sulfuric acid and water vapor, adapted to extreme acidity and using sunlight as a source of energy. To make their case, Sagan and Morowitz pointed to earthly analogs, microbes thriving in the acidic hot springs of Yellowstone National Park in the United States. These springs are pools heated by geothermal energy, rich in minerals and often highly acidic. Yet certain extremophiles, microbes adapted to harsh conditions, flourish there, using chemical reactions to survive. If life can adapt to boiling acidic water on Earth, they reasoned, why not to acidic clouds on Venus? Their argument was speculative, but it cracked open the idea that life is not confined to Earth like surfaces, which is significant because a large percentage of the planets in the universe don't even have a solid surface at all.
versions.transcriptZh: 1967年，天文学家卡尔·萨根和生物学家哈罗德·莫罗维茨在《自然》杂志上发表了一篇引发争议的论文。 当时，大多数科学家认为地外生命只能存在于拥有类地表面、适中温度、液态水和可供站立的坚实地面的行星上。 萨根和莫罗维茨挑战了这一假设。 他们认为，虽然金星表面对于生命来说太热了，热到足以融化铅，但行星上层云层的情况却截然不同。 地表上方约50公里处，温度和压力与地球表面相似。 他们推测微生物生命可以在这些云层中存活，漂浮在硫酸和水蒸气的液滴中，适应极端的酸性并利用阳光作为能量来源。 为了支持他们的论点，萨根和莫罗维茨指出了地球上的类似情况，即在美国黄石国家公园的酸性温泉中茁壮成长的微生物。 这些泉水是由地热能加热的池子，富含矿物质且通常呈强酸性。 然而，某些嗜极生物，即适应恶劣条件的微生物，在那里繁衍生息，利用化学反应生存。 他们推断，如果生命能在地球上适应沸腾的酸性水，为什么不能适应金星上的酸性云层呢？ 他们的论点是推测性的，但它开辟了生命不局限于类地表面的想法，这一点意义重大，因为宇宙中很大一部分行星根本就没有固体表面。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an art history class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an art history class.
When we look at paintings, we often think of them as standalone creations, but they aren't always. Sometimes they converse with each other in surprising ways. Lubaina Himid, a British artist, was born in 1954 in what's now Tanzania in East Africa, and she was raised in London. London's where she also developed her career as an artist. According to Himid herself, her career expanded after 2010 when her work was shown at a gallery called Hollybush Gardens, a gallery in London. After that exhibit, critics paid more attention, and Himid began showing her work at larger museums and internationally outside of the United Kingdom. In her 1984 work titled Freedom and Change, Lubaina Himid shows two Black women dancing, or maybe running. They're holding hands in the air, and they just look so joyful. The scene reimagines a famous 1922 painting by the Spanish artist Pablo Picasso called Two Women Running on the Beach. Picasso's painting shows two women—white women—also dancing or running. They're in similar positions with similar facial expressions as the Black women in Himid's later work. This is an interesting reversal. By that I mean, Picasso was known for incorporating African elements into his work, like tribal masks. So I think it's only equitable that Himid then incorporated Picasso's elements into her own work. Makes it a fair back and forth, a conversation in a way, you see? It's just something that wasn't seen that often.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段艺术史课的讲座。
我们看画时，常以为画作是独立创作，其实并不总是如此。有时它们会以出人意料的方式彼此“对话”。英国艺术家 Lubaina Himid 1954 年生于今东非坦桑尼亚，在伦敦长大，也在伦敦发展艺术生涯。据她本人说，2010 年作品在伦敦 Hollybush Gardens 画廊展出后，事业得到扩展；此后评论界更关注她，她也开始在更大博物馆以及英国以外的国际场合展出。在 1984 年的作品《自由与改变》中，Himid 画了两名黑人女性在跳舞，或许是在奔跑，手牵手举在空中，神情欢快。这一场景重新演绎了西班牙艺术家毕加索 1922 年的名画《海滩上奔跑的两个女人》。毕加索画中是两名白人女性，同样在舞动或奔跑，姿势与表情和 Himid 画中的黑人女性相似。这是一种有趣的反转：毕加索以把非洲元素——如部落面具——融入作品而闻名，因此我认为 Himid 把毕加索的元素融入自己的作品，也完全公平。某种意义上，这是一次来回的对话，而这种做法过去并不常见。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a science podcast.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a science podcast. Nanoparticles are particles whose size is less than one ten-thousandth of a millimeter. Super tiny. Nanoparticles have numerous applications. My family had a picnic last Saturday. We used sunscreen to avoid sunburn. Our sunscreen contains titanium dioxide, which has been used in sunscreen for decades. You used to end up with these horrible-looking white smears all over your skin while wearing it. But our new sunscreen's titanium dioxide comes in nanoparticles. They block ultraviolet sunlight but are transparent. The sunblock's completely invisible on your skin, not smeary white. Another example: the metal silver has antimicrobial properties. The problem is, you can't put regular metal on a wound. But an ointment with silver nanoparticles, we can actually apply that to stop bacterial growth. We did it when my son scraped his knee at the picnic. Humans have actually used nanoparticles for millennia. Take ancient Rome's tesserae. Tesserae are tiny bits of highly colorful glass that the Romans arranged to create various images. Many Roman tesserae, especially pink ones, contain gold nanoparticles. The particles affect how light interacts with the glass and create the color. Did the Romans know what they were doing? Well, they probably didn't understand the physics of it. But some glass workshop could realize that gold foil beaten into an extremely thin layer produces bright colors when heated between glass layers. And the technique was perfected and spread. All pink tesserae contain gold nanoparticles at between 10 and 30 parts per million. That's so consistent, so it's definitely not random.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段科学播客的讲座。纳米颗粒是尺寸小于万分之一毫米的粒子。超级小。纳米颗粒有众多应用。我家上周六野餐。我们用防晒霜避免晒伤。我们的防晒霜含二氧化钛，已在防晒霜中用了数十年。过去用时皮肤上会留下难看的白色涂抹。但我们新防晒霜里的二氧化钛以纳米颗粒形式存在。它们阻挡紫外线却是透明的。防晒在皮肤上完全看不见，不是糊状白色。另一例子：金属银有抗菌性。问题是你不能把普通金属放在伤口上。但含银纳米颗粒的软膏，我们真能涂上阻止细菌生长。儿子野餐时擦伤膝盖我们就这么做了。人类其实用纳米颗粒已有数千年。以古罗马的镶嵌块为例。镶嵌块是罗马人排列成各种图像的极彩色小玻璃片。许多罗马镶嵌块尤其粉色的含金纳米颗粒。这些粒子影响光与玻璃如何作用并产生颜色。罗马人知道自己在做什么吗？他们大概不懂其中物理。但某个玻璃作坊能意识到：把金箔打成极薄层，夹在玻璃层间加热会出亮色。技法被完善并传播。所有粉色镶嵌块都含百万分之十到三十的金纳米颗粒。如此一致，绝对不是随机。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Narrator
transcriptSentences.text: Listen to a talk on a science podcast.

transcriptSentences.text: Super tiny.

transcriptSentences.text: Nanoparticles have numerous applications.

transcriptSentences.text: My family had a picnic last Saturday.

transcriptSentences.text: We used sunscreen to avoid sunburn.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 我们用防晒霜避免晒伤。

transcriptSentences.text: Our sunscreen contains titanium dioxide, which has been used in sunscreen for decades.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 我们的防晒霜含二氧化钛，已在防晒霜中用了数十年。

transcriptSentences.text: You used to end up with these horrible-looking white smears all over your skin while wearing it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 过去用时皮肤上会留下难看的白色涂抹。

transcriptSentences.text: But our new sunscreen's titanium dioxide comes in nanoparticles.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但我们新防晒霜里的二氧化钛以纳米颗粒形式存在。

transcriptSentences.text: They block ultraviolet sunlight but are transparent.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们阻挡紫外线却是透明的。

transcriptSentences.text: The sunblock's completely invisible on your skin, not smeary white.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 防晒在皮肤上完全看不见，不是糊状白色。

transcriptSentences.text: Another example: the metal silver has antimicrobial properties.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 另一例子：金属银有抗菌性。

transcriptSentences.text: The problem is, you can't put regular metal on a wound.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 问题是你不能把普通金属放在伤口上。

transcriptSentences.textZh: 但含银纳米颗粒的软膏，我们真能涂上阻止细菌生长。

transcriptSentences.text: We did it when my son scraped his knee at the picnic.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 儿子野餐时擦伤膝盖我们就这么做了。

transcriptSentences.text: Humans have actually used nanoparticles for millennia.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 人类其实用纳米颗粒已有数千年。

transcriptSentences.text: Take ancient Rome's tesserae.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 以古罗马的镶嵌块为例。

transcriptSentences.text: Tesserae are tiny bits of highly colorful glass that the Romans arranged to create various images.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 镶嵌块是罗马人排列成各种图像的极彩色小玻璃片。

transcriptSentences.text: Many Roman tesserae, especially pink ones, contain gold nanoparticles.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 许多罗马镶嵌块尤其粉色的含金纳米颗粒。

transcriptSentences.text: The particles affect how light interacts with the glass and create the color.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这些粒子影响光与玻璃如何作用并产生颜色。

transcriptSentences.text: Did the Romans know what they were doing?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 罗马人知道自己在做什么吗？

transcriptSentences.text: Well, they probably didn't understand the physics of it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 他们大概不懂其中物理。

transcriptSentences.text: But some glass workshop could realize that gold foil beaten into an extremely thin layer produces bright colors when heated between glass layers.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但某个玻璃作坊能意识到：把金箔打成极薄层，夹在玻璃层间加热会出亮色。

transcriptSentences.text: And the technique was perfected and spread.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 技法被完善并传播。

transcriptSentences.text: All pink tesserae contain gold nanoparticles at between 10 and 30 parts per million.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 所有粉色镶嵌块都含百万分之十到三十的金纳米颗粒。

transcriptSentences.text: That's so consistent, so it's definitely not random.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 如此一致，绝对不是随机。

versions.transcriptZh: 纳米粒子是尺寸小于毫米万分之一的粒子，非常微小。 纳米粒子有许多应用。 上周六我的家人去野餐了。 我们使用了防晒霜来避免晒伤。 我们的防晒霜含有二氧化钛，这种成分已经用于防晒霜几十年了。 过去使用它时，你的皮肤上会留下可怕的白色污迹。 但在我们新的防晒霜中，二氧化钛以纳米粒子的形式存在。 它们阻挡紫外线，但却是透明的。 这种防晒霜在你的皮肤上完全隐形，没有白色污迹。 另一个例子：金属银具有抗菌特性。 问题是不能将普通金属放在伤口上。 但是含有银纳米粒子的软膏，我们实际上可以将其用于阻止细菌生长。 我的儿子在野餐时擦伤了膝盖，我们就这样做了。 人类实际上使用纳米粒子已有数千年历史。 以古罗马的镶嵌玻璃为例。 镶嵌玻璃是色彩鲜艳的微小玻璃碎片，罗马人将其排列起来创造各种图像。 许多罗马镶嵌玻璃，特别是粉红色的，含有金纳米粒子。 这些粒子影响光与玻璃的相互作用并产生颜色。 罗马人知道他们在做什么吗？ 嗯，他们可能不理解其中的物理原理。 但一些玻璃作坊意识到，将金箔敲打成极薄的层，在玻璃层之间加热时会产生鲜艳的颜色，这项技术得到了完善和推广。 所有粉红色的镶嵌玻璃都含有10到30ppm的金纳米粒子。 这太一致了，所以绝不是随机的。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a marketing class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in a marketing class. Today we're diving into the dynamic and often unpredictable world of viral marketing. Viral marketing is a strategy that has redefined how brands connect with audiences in the digital age. Viral marketing harnesses the power of social networks, relying on individuals to share content that resonates, entertains, or provokes thought. When executed effectively, a viral campaign can generate massive exposure. This amplifies brand visibility at a fraction of the cost of traditional advertising methods. You don't need to pay for ads when the video or meme is exploding on its own. What makes viral marketing so compelling is its potential for exponential reach. A single post, video, or meme can cascade through online communities, crossing geographic and demographic boundaries in mere hours. But this strategy is far from foolproof. One of the biggest challenges is unpredictability. There's no guaranteed formula for virality. What resonates with one audience may be ignored by another. And content that's edgy or controversial may be more likely to go viral, but it can also spark backlash and damage a company's reputation. Another risk is loss of control. Once content goes viral, it's no longer in the hands of the brand. Memes, remixes, and commentary can distort the original message, sometimes in ways that conflict with the brand's values or goals. But despite these risks, viral marketing remains an invaluable tool, particularly for startups and emerging brands seeking rapid traction. Next, let's talk about some case studies of particularly effective viral marketing campaigns.

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an art history class. If you've ever looked at a Picasso painting and thought, "Wait, is that a face or a guitar?", you've already encountered the magic of Cubism. This revolutionary movement shook up the art scene in the early 20th century. It wasn't just a new style; it was a complete reimagining of how we see and represent reality. Artists like Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque broke away from the traditional rules of perspective and instead chose to depict objects from multiple angles at once. Imagine seeing every side of a coffee cup: top, bottom, and side, all in a single image. That's the kind of visual remix Cubism brought to the canvas. At first, people didn't know what to make of it. Critics called it chaotic, even nonsensical. But over time, Cubism proved to be a game changer, influencing not just painting and sculpture, but also music, literature, and architecture. It encouraged creators to rethink structure, narrative, and form, and to reconsider how we think about representation and abstraction. And it paved the way for other art movements, like Modernism. Modernism also embraced abstraction and conceptual depth, though in somewhat different ways.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a business class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in a business class. Today, let's dive into a cornerstone of modern marketing: market segmentation. Imagine trying to sell the same product to everyone: teenagers, retirees, athletes, and artists, with one generic message. It wouldn't work. That's where segmentation comes in. Market segmentation is the strategic process of dividing a broad audience into smaller groups based on shared traits, like age, lifestyle, income, or even values. This allows companies to craft tailored messages and products that speak directly to each group's unique needs. Why does this matter? First, it sharpens targeting. A company that understands its target audience can design product campaigns that feel personal, not generic. A running shoe company could create ads that feel relevant to teenagers and alternate ads for 30-year-olds. Second, segmentation helps businesses focus on high-potential markets, focusing on the most profitable segments. A cell phone company might discover that urban professionals buy new phones far more often than rural inhabitants. Instead of marketing to all regions, the company can concentrate its budget, messaging, and product development on the urban segment. Segmentation also boosts customer satisfaction. When consumers feel understood, they're more likely to stay loyal to a product or service. Personalized experiences, like curated recommendations or specialty product lines, can turn casual buyers into lifelong fans. However, implementing segmentation effectively requires rigorous data collection and analysis. Companies must gather insights from surveys, purchase histories, social media behavior, and more to define meaningful segments. Once identified, they need to monitor these groups continuously as consumer preferences evolve over time.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段商业课的讲座。今天深入现代营销的基石：市场细分。想象用同一通用信息向所有人——青少年、退休者、运动员与艺术家——推销同一产品。行不通。这就是细分的用武之地。市场细分是按共同特征——如年龄、生活方式、收入甚至价值观——把广泛受众划分成更小群体的战略过程。这使公司能打造直接回应各组独特需求的定制信息与产品。为何重要？首先，它锐化定位。理解目标受众的公司可设计感觉个性化而非笼统的产品宣传。跑鞋公司可做对青少年相关的广告，再做针对三十岁人群的另一套广告。其次，细分帮助企业聚焦高潜力市场，把重点放在最赚钱的细分上。手机公司可能发现城市专业人士比农村居民更常买新手机。与其向所有地区营销，公司可把预算、信息与产品开发集中在城市细分。细分也提升客户满意度。当消费者感到被理解时，更可能对产品或服务保持忠诚。个性化体验，如精选推荐或特色产品线，可把随意买家变成终身粉丝。但有效实施细分需要严格的数据收集与分析。公司须从调查、购买历史、社交媒体行为等收集洞见，以定义有意义的细分。一旦识别，还须随消费者偏好随时间演变而持续监测这些群体。

versions.transcriptZh: 今天，让我们深入探讨现代营销的一个基石：市场细分。 想象一下，试图用同一种通用的信息向所有人（包括青少年、退休人员、运动员和艺术家）销售同一种产品。 这行不通。 这就是市场细分发挥作用的地方。 市场细分是根据年龄、生活方式、收入甚至价值观等共同特征，将广泛受众划分为更小群体的战略过程。 这使得公司能够精心制作量身定制的信息和产品，直接针对每个群体的独特需求。 为什么这很重要？ 首先，它使定位更精准。 了解目标受众的公司可以设计出让人感觉个性化而非通用的产品营销活动。 一家跑鞋公司可以创作出让青少年感到相关的广告，并针对三十岁的人群更换不同的广告。 其次，市场细分帮助企业专注于高潜力市场，也就是最有利可图的细分市场。 一家手机公司可能会发现，城市职业人士购买新手机的频率远高于农村居民。 与其向所有地区进行营销，该公司可以将精力集中在回报最高的地方。 第三，市场细分可以建立更强的客户忠诚度。 当客户觉得一个品牌了解他们的需求时，他们更有可能坚持使用该品牌。 但市场细分并非静止不变。 一旦确定了这些群体，公司需要持续监测，因为消费者的偏好会随着时间的推移而演变。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk from a music podcast.

Man: During the early 20th century, technology was advancing rapidly, and music was no exception. Today, we're talking about electrophones, the predecessors of today's synthesizers. These early electronic instruments challenged musical conventions by creating sound not through vibrating strings or air columns, but through electronic means. One of the earliest and most famous electrophones is the theremin, which creates melodies through the manipulation of electromagnetic fields. The musician doesn't even touch the instrument. Instead, hand movements near two metal antennas control pitch and volume. Its eerie tones soon became associated with experimental compositions. Another important instrument was the Ondes Martenot, developed in France. It gave composers a wider expressive range and could be played by gliding a ring along a wire, kind of like moving a bow across violin strings. Together, the theremin and the Ondes Martenot set the stage for later synthesizers, which now dominate everything from pop to film scores. So while early electrophones may seem unusual today, they were crucial in making new musical ideas possible. They left a lasting mark on how people think about creating sound.

请听一段音乐播客的讲座。

男：二十世纪初，技术迅速进步，音乐也不例外。今天我们谈电鸣乐器——今日合成器的前身。这些早期电子乐器挑战音乐惯例，不通过振动弦或气柱，而通过电子方式发声。最早且最著名的电鸣乐器之一是特雷门琴，通过操控电磁场产生旋律。乐手甚至不碰乐器。相反，手在两根金属天线附近移动控制音高与音量。其诡异音色很快与实验性作品联系在一起。另一重要乐器是在法国开发的马特诺电琴。它给作曲家更广的表现范围，可通过沿导线滑动指环演奏，有点像弓在小提琴弦上移动。特雷门琴与马特诺电琴共同为后来的合成器铺路，而合成器现主导从流行到电影配乐的一切。因此，尽管早期电鸣乐器今天看起来不寻常，它们对使新音乐想法成为可能至关重要。它们在人们如何思考声音创造上留下了持久印记。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an art history class.

Man: Today, the Mexican visual artist Frida Kahlo is one of the most famous artists of the 20th century. But when Kahlo died in 1954, she was mostly known as the wife of another famous Mexican artist, Diego Rivera. Critics and the public had barely heard of her until decades later, probably after a Hollywood movie about her life came out in 2002. Kahlo's best-known works today are her paintings, especially her self-portraits. In many of these paintings, she shows herself with a serious expression, thick eyebrows, and traditional Mexican clothing. But today I want to talk about her drawings, which are still much less well known. One drawing that stands out is a self-portrait she made in 1946, probably intended as a gift for a Mexican politician. Like in her paintings, Kahlo drew herself with a serious facial expression. She looks directly at the viewer, almost as if she is asking, "What's my life's meaning?" Her eyebrows form the shape of a hummingbird, which seems ready to fly up onto her forehead, where cloud-like shapes appear. But my favorite part of the drawing is her hair. On one side, it is braided and modest; on the other, it is loose and wild. This contrast seems to show her inner struggle between being controlled and being free.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段艺术史课的讲座。

男：今天，墨西哥视觉艺术家弗里达·卡罗是二十世纪最著名的艺术家之一。但卡罗一九五四年去世时，她主要作为另一位著名墨西哥艺术家迭戈·里维拉的妻子为人所知。批评家与公众直到数十年后才几乎听说她，大概在二零〇二年一部关于她生平的好莱坞电影上映之后。卡罗如今最知名的作品是她的画作，尤其是自画像。在许多这些画中，她呈现严肃表情、浓眉与传统墨西哥服饰。但今天我想谈她的素描，它们仍远不为人所知。一幅突出的素描是她一九四六年所作的自画像，大概意在作为给一位墨西哥政客的礼物。与画作中一样，卡罗把自己画成严肃表情。她直视观者，几乎像在问「我生命的意义是什么？」她的眉毛形成蜂鸟形状，仿佛准备飞上前额，那里出现云状形状。但这幅素描我最爱的部分是她的头发。一侧编辫、朴素；另一侧松散狂野。这一对比似乎展现她在受控与自由之间的内心挣扎。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a biology class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in a biology class. Some animals have such odd features and habits that they almost seem mythical. One is the Indian pangolin. The Indian pangolin is a mammal about 100 centimeters long. It has a tail, and except for its belly, it's covered in large, overlapping scales that make it look kind of like an artichoke or a pinecone. These scales are like its own coat of armor. When it's threatened, the Indian pangolin curls into a tight ball, protecting its belly and using its scales as a shield against predators. This behavior is known as volvation. Think of a hedgehog. When threatened, a hedgehog will also curl into a ball, volvation, with its spikes facing outward for protection. Ingenious. The Indian pangolin is found in forests, grasslands, and even deserts. Wherever Indian pangolins are, there's two things they like: digging and ants. Pangolins are nocturnal, meaning they come out at night, and when they do, they're looking for ants. They eat about 200,000 of them, ants and termites, every day. This helps keep their ecosystem balanced. They also dig burrows, which are like holes or tunnels, to sleep or mate in, or to find ants. When Indian pangolins dig, they're disturbing the soil, which improves the soil by making it easier for air, water, and nutrients to circulate in the soil, similar to why farmers plow their fields. Pangolin digging helps contribute to the growth of new, healthy vegetation. Plus, the burrows, once they're abandoned, are good shelter and habitat for other animals.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段生物学课的讲座。有些动物特征与习性如此奇特，几乎像神话。一种是印度穿山甲。印度穿山甲是一种约一百厘米长的哺乳动物。它有尾巴，除腹部外覆以大而重叠的鳞片，看起来有点像朝鲜蓟或松果。这些鳞片像它自己的铠甲。受威胁时，印度穿山甲蜷成紧实的球，保护腹部并用鳞片作盾抵御捕食者。这一行为称为蜷球。想想刺猬。受威胁时刺猬也会蜷成球——蜷球——尖刺朝外保护自己。巧妙。印度穿山甲见于森林、草地甚至沙漠。无论在哪里，印度穿山甲喜欢两样东西：挖洞与蚂蚁。穿山甲夜行，意思是夜间出来，出来时在找蚂蚁。它们每天大约吃二十万只蚂蚁与白蚁。这有助保持其生态系统平衡。它们也挖洞穴——像洞或隧道——用于睡眠、交配或找蚂蚁。印度穿山甲挖洞时搅动土壤，使空气、水与养分更易在土壤中循环，从而改善土壤，类似农民为何耕地。穿山甲挖洞有助新健康植被生长。此外，洞穴被遗弃后，是其他动物的好庇护与栖息地。

transcriptSentences.text: This behavior is known as volvation.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这种行为被称为“卷曲防御”。

transcriptSentences.text: Think of a hedgehog.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 想想刺猬。

transcriptSentences.text: When threatened, a hedgehog will also curl into a ball, volvation, with its spikes facing outward for protection.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 当受到威胁时，刺猬也会蜷缩成一个球，进行卷曲防御，刺朝外以求保护。

transcriptSentences.text: Ingenious.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这很巧妙。

transcriptSentences.text: The Indian pangolin is found in forests, grasslands, and even deserts.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 印度穿山甲生活在森林、草原，甚至是沙漠中。

transcriptSentences.text: Wherever Indian pangolins are, there are two things they like: digging and ants.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 无论印度穿山甲在哪里，它们都喜欢两样东西：挖洞和蚂蚁。

transcriptSentences.text: Pangolins are nocturnal, meaning they come out at night.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 穿山甲是夜行动物，这意味着它们在夜间出来活动。

transcriptSentences.text: And when they do, they're looking for ants.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 当它们出来时，它们就在寻找蚂蚁。

transcriptSentences.text: They eat about 200,000 of them, ants and termites, every day.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们每天大约吃掉20万只蚂蚁和白蚁。

transcriptSentences.text: This helps keep their ecosystem balanced.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这有助于维持生态系统的平衡。

transcriptSentences.text: They also dig burrows, which are holes or tunnels, to sleep in, hide in, or raise their young.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们还会挖洞穴，也就是地洞或隧道，用来睡觉、躲藏或抚养幼崽。

transcriptSentences.text: As they dig, they disturb and loosen the soil.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 在挖洞时，它们会扰动并松动土壤。

transcriptSentences.text: That action mixes nutrients, lets air and water move through the ground more easily, and makes the soil healthier for plants to grow in.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这种行为能混合养分，让空气和水更容易通过地面，并使土壤更健康，有利于植物生长。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a linguistics class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a linguistics class.
Linguists have designed experiments to study infant language learning. Take the now-famous Wug test. In the test, a child is shown a drawing of a made-up creature called a wug. Then they're shown two of them and asked, "Now there are two." Most children say "wugs," adding the plural "s," although they've never heard the word before. This shows young kids not only memorize words, but apply grammatical rules to words they've never heard before. Another study investigated how babies learn word boundaries. From the sound of spoken language, it isn't obvious where one word ends and another begins. You can tell that only if you already know a lot about the language. So how can children pick out the words and learn them? In an experiment, eight-month-old infants listened to a stream of made-up syllables with no pauses. After just two minutes, researchers tested the babies using the head-turn preference method. They played two types of audio: one with sound patterns that are like real words and that had appeared frequently in the stream, and another with random syllables. Babies tended to turn their heads and listen longer to the familiar sounds. This showed they had picked up on statistical patterns, like which syllables tended to follow each other, and used that to segment speech. Turns out, babies are highly sophisticated pattern seekers. This suggests language learning might be linked to other cognitive abilities, like attention and memory. Do they correlate? Let's discuss some studies on that next.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段语言学课的讲座。
语言学家设计了实验来研究婴儿如何学习语言。以著名的 Wug 测试为例。测试中，孩子先看到一种虚构生物“wug”的画，再看到两只，并被问：“现在有两只——”大多数孩子会说“wugs”，加上复数 s，尽管从未听过这个词。这说明幼儿不仅记单词，还会把语法规则用到从未听过的词上。另一项研究考察婴儿如何学会词界。仅从口语声音听，并不清楚一词在哪里结束、下一词在哪里开始；只有已经很懂这种语言才能判断。那孩子怎么切出词并学会它们？实验中，八个月大的婴儿听一串没有停顿的虚构音节。仅两分钟后，研究者用转头偏好法测试：播放两类音频，一类是流中频繁出现、像真词的模式，一类是随机音节。婴儿更常把头转向熟悉声音并听得更久。这说明他们抓住了统计规律——比如哪些音节常前后相随——并据此切分语流。原来婴儿是高度成熟的模式搜寻者。这提示语言学习可能与注意、记忆等其他认知能力相关。它们相关吗？接下来我们讨论一些研究。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.
Sea turtles are endangered marine species, and survival rates for sea turtle hatchlings are extremely low: about one in a thousand reaches adulthood. Even under natural conditions survival is difficult, and human activity makes it worse. One of the most significant problems is artificial light. Sea turtles lay their eggs on sandy beaches in tropical and subtropical waters. For millions of years, newly hatched turtles have relied on moonlight and starlight reflected off the water to find the sea. However, where beachfront development overlaps with nesting beaches, bright lights from hotels, streets, and homes overwhelm these natural cues. Older lighting technologies, such as fluorescent bulbs and cool-white lights, emit short-wavelength light that hatchlings are especially sensitive to, causing them to crawl inland instead of toward the sea. Many die from dehydration or traffic. Fortunately, there is a solution. Some older bulbs have been replaced with red or amber lights. These colors have longer wavelengths that are nearly invisible to hatchlings, allowing them to follow moonlight and starlight toward the water. Unlike dangers such as climate change and plastic pollution, which are global problems requiring broader action, light pollution can be addressed locally through small-scale efforts.

海龟是濒危海洋物种，幼龟存活率极低：大约一千只中只有一只能长到成年。即使在自然条件下也很难，人类活动更使情况恶化。最严重的问题之一是人工光。海龟在热带、亚热带沙滩产卵。数百万年来，刚出壳的幼龟靠水面反射的月光和星光找到大海。然而当滨海开发与筑巢沙滩重叠时，酒店、街道和住宅的强光淹没了这些自然线索。荧光灯、冷白光等较旧的照明发出短波光，幼龟特别敏感，会爬向内陆而不是大海，许多死于脱水或交通事故。幸好有解决办法：一些旧灯泡换成了红色或琥珀色灯，波长更长，幼龟几乎看不见，从而能跟随月光星光朝水走。与气候变化、塑料污染这类需要全球行动的问题不同，光污染可以通过本地小规模努力来解决。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a history of technology podcast.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a history of technology podcast. You've probably used many remote controls for things: televisions, smart devices, and other electronics. My wife uses one to open the gate to her parking lot at work. Now, remote controls for televisions have been around since the 1950s. Wired remote controls had been used before then, back to around 1870, mostly for unpiloted military vehicles. Later, the inventor Nikola Tesla developed a wireless remote control for military vehicles in 1898. As for TV remotes, the first really popular one was developed in 1950. It was called the Lazy Bones. It was pretty expensive. Unfortunately, the Lazy Bones was connected to the TV by a long wire, which of course was annoying and a trip hazard. It's kind of hard to imagine this was more practical for most people than just getting up and turning the dial on the television yourself. A few years later, in 1955, a wireless remote was introduced: the Flash-Matic. To use the Flash-Matic, you'd point it at one of the corners of your TV screen. This would shine a light beam at the chosen corner. Now, each corner had its own purpose: channel up or down, power, or mute. Each corner had a photoelectric cell to convert the light beam into an electrical signal to do what you wanted. Trouble was, the photoelectric cells responded to other light sources too, like light from a light bulb or even sunlight. Imagine turning on a light bulb and your TV suddenly turns on too.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段技术史播客的讲座。你大概用过许多东西的遥控器：电视、智能设备与其他电子产品。我妻子用一个打开她工作停车场的门。电视遥控器自一九五〇年代起就有了。在此之前有线遥控器已被使用，可回溯到约一八七〇年，多用于无人驾驶军用车辆。后来发明家尼古拉·特斯拉在一八九八年为军用车辆开发了无线遥控器。至于电视遥控，第一个真正流行的于一九五〇年开发。它叫 Lazy Bones。相当贵。不幸的是，Lazy Bones 用长线连到电视，当然令人烦，也是绊脚危险。很难想象这对多数人比自己站起来拧电视旋钮更实用。几年后，一九五五年，无线遥控推出：Flash-Matic。使用 Flash-Matic 时，你把它对准电视屏幕的一个角。这会向所选角落射出光束。每个角有自己的用途：频道上下、电源或静音。每个角有光电管，把光束转为电信号以执行你想要的操作。问题是，光电管也对其他光源响应，如灯泡光甚至阳光。想象打开灯泡，电视突然也开了。

versions.transcript: You've probably used many remote controls for things like televisions, smart devices, and other electronics. My wife uses one to open the gate to her parking lot at work. Now remote controls for TVs have been around since the 1950s. Wired remote controls had been used before then, back to around 1870, mostly for unpiloted military vehicles. Later, the inventor Nikola Tesla developed a wireless remote control for military vehicles in 1898. As for TV remotes, the first really popular one was developed in 1950. It was called the Lazy Bones and was pretty expensive. Fortunately, the Lazy Bones was connected to the TV by a long wire, which of course was annoying and a trip hazard. It's kind of hard to imagine this was more practical for most people than just getting up and turning the dial on the television yourself. A few years later, in 1955, a wireless remote was introduced, the Flashmatic. To use the Flashmatic, you'd point it at one of the corners of your TV screen. This would shine a light beam at the chosen corner. Now each corner had its own purpose, channel up or down, power or mute. Each corner had a photoelectric cell to convert the light beam into an electrical signal to do what you want. Trouble was, the photoelectric cells responded to other light sources too, like from a lightbulb or even sunlight. Imagine turning on a lightbulb and your TV suddenly turns on too.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a creative writing class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a creative writing class.

Woman: Have you ever stared at a blank page, trying to come up with an idea of what to write about, waiting for inspiration? Storytelling dice are a simple way to break through that creative block. Yes, I'm talking about dice, similar to ones you roll in some common board games to generate random numbers. But instead of numbers, each die is covered with pictorial symbols, like a tree or a lightning bolt. A typical set could have nine six-sided dice. The magic lies in their unpredictability. You might roll a dragon, a locked door, and a storm. Suddenly, you're weaving a tale of, say, hidden realms and daring escapes. Storytelling dice are not just for writers. They can also serve as icebreakers at social gatherings. Imagine this: the party feels a little stiff, so you pull out the dice and say, 'Everyone, roll three.' Someone gets a dragon, a ladder, and a smiley face. Another rolls a spaceship, shoes, and a storm cloud. Soon, people are laughing as they connect these random images into a wild story. 'The dragon was stuck on a ladder during a thunderstorm, and then a spaceship landed to rescue it.' It's silly, spontaneous, and gets everyone talking. But now, let's get back to creative writing and talk about a short story that a previous student of mine wrote last semester. While reading the story, try to guess what three images she rolled on her dice that inspired her to write it.

请听一段创意写作课的讲座。

女：你是否曾盯着空白页，想写出什么、等待灵感？故事骰是突破创作瓶颈的简单方法。对，我说的是骰子，类似常见桌游里掷出随机数的那种。但不是数字，每颗骰子覆盖着图画符号，比如树或闪电。一套典型可有九颗六面骰。魔力在于不可预测。你可能掷出龙、上锁的门与风暴。突然间你就在编织比方说隐秘国度与大胆逃脱的故事。故事骰不只给写作者。它们也可在社交聚会中当破冰工具。想象一下：聚会有点僵，你拿出骰子说「大家各掷三颗」。有人得到龙、梯子与笑脸。另一人掷出飞船、鞋子与暴风云。很快人们边笑边把这些随机图像连成狂野故事。「龙在雷雨中卡在梯子上，然后一艘飞船降落来救它。」傻气、自发，让人人开口。但现在回到创意写作，谈上学期我一位学生写的短篇。读故事时，试着猜她掷出哪三幅图像启发她写它。

versions.transcript: Have you ever stared at a blank page, trying to come up with an idea of what to write about, waiting for inspiration? Storytelling dice are a simple way to break through that creative block. Yes, I'm talking about dice similar to ones you roll in some common board games to generate random numbers. But instead of numbers, each die is covered with pictorial symbols, like a tree, a key, or a lightning bolt. A typical set could have nine six sided dice. The magic lies in their unpredictability. You might roll a dragon, a locked door, and a storm. Suddenly, you're weaving a tale of, say, hidden realms and daring escapes. Storytelling dice are not just for writers. They can also serve as icebreakers at social gatherings. Imagine this. The party feels a little stiff, so you pull out the dice and say, Everyone roll three. Someone gets a dragon, a ladder, and a smiley face. Another rolls a spaceship, shoes, and a storm cloud. Soon, people are laughing as they connect these random images into a wild story. The dragon was stuck on a ladder during a thunderstorm. And then a spaceship landed to rescue it. It's silly, spontaneous, and gets everyone talking. But now, let's get back to creative writing and talk about a short story that a previous student of mine wrote last semester. While reading the story, try to guess what three images she rolled on her dice that inspired her to write it.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a biology podcast.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a biology podcast.
Did you ever see a little bug scuttle past you quickly and wonder what it was? If you see one that has a long, wiggly body and a lot of legs, you might want to know—after you've possibly shrieked at it—whether it was a centipede or a millipede. Well, both centipedes and millipedes may be a few centimeters long and have bodies made up of many segments. That's why they're considered relatives in the animal kingdom. Oh, and they've both got poor vision, or no ability to see. The name centipede comes from Latin and means a hundred feet, and millipede means a thousand feet. Well, millipedes do have more legs, sometimes more than a thousand, but probably not exactly a thousand. And centipedes don't really have a hundred either. Now, millipedes have two sets of legs for each segment of their body, and those two sets of legs are right beneath their body. By contrast, centipedes have just one set of legs for each body segment, and those single sets are jointed and positioned on the side of the centipede's body. So these leg locations would make it more obvious which critter you're looking at if you come across one. What they do when threatened is also different. Centipedes might bite, though it is generally harmless to humans, and then run away. Millipedes will roll themselves up and emit a stinky odor.

versions.transcript: Did you ever see a little bug scuttle past you quickly and wonder what it was? If you see one that has a long, wiggly body and a lot of legs, you might wanna know, after you've possibly shrieked at it, whether it was a centipede or a millipede. Well, both centipedes and millipedes may be a few centimeters long and have bodies made up of many segments. That's why they're considered relatives in the animal kingdom. Oh, and they've both got poor vision or no ability to see. The name centipede comes from Latin and means 100 feet, and then millipede means 1,000 feet. Well, millipedes do have more legs, sometimes more than 1,000, but probably not exactly 1,000, and centipedes don't really have 100 either. Now, millipedes, they have two sets of legs for each segment of their body, and those two sets of legs are under, right beneath their body. That's their position. By contrast, centipedes have just one set of legs for each body segment, and those single sets are jointed and positioned on the side of the centipede's body. So these leg locations would make it more obvious which critter you're looking at if you come across one. What they do is different also. Centipedes might bite, though it's generally harmless to humans. Then they run away, but millipedes will roll themselves up and then emit a stinky odor. Hard to decide which is worse.
