versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in an archaeology class.
Okay, let's go back to 1700 BCE to a site now known as Poverty Point, located in what today is Louisiana in the United States. Imagine a bustling community of people building something so innovative that it would still intrigue us thousands of years later. Poverty Point is a testament to the advanced engineering skills of pre-Columbian societies in North America. Now, what makes this site so remarkable? The builders created massive earthen mounds, some arranged in concentric half-circles. They made six rows of raised earth stretching across 1.2 kilometers. These mound formations aren't just random. What I find truly fascinating is that they show a level of planning and design that required significant understanding of geometry. Now, these structures were made without metal tools, wheels, or the help of animals like horses or oxen. Instead, builders used simple tools like baskets and their own hands, moving massive amounts of earth. This was a monumental task that required a highly organized labor force. But it wasn't just about moving dirt. The site was a hub of activity. Artifacts found here, like stone tools and pottery, can be traced back to sources as far as the Appalachian Mountains and the Great Lakes. This demonstrates an impressive range of trade connections. Living so close to the Mississippi River meant these people were not isolated, but were part of a vast network. In essence, Poverty Point defies our assumptions about ancient societies in North America.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段考古学课的讲座。
好，让我们回到公元前一七〇〇年，到一个如今称为 Poverty Point 的遗址，位于今天美国的路易斯安那。想象一个忙碌的社区在建造某种如此创新、数千年后仍让我们着迷的东西。Poverty Point 证明了北美前哥伦布社会先进的工程技能。那是什么使这个遗址如此非凡？建造者建造了巨大土丘，有些排成同心半圆。他们筑了六排隆起的土，绵延一点二公里。这些土丘形态不只是随意的。我觉得真正迷人的是它们展现需要深刻几何理解的规划与设计水平。这些结构在没有金属工具、轮子，或马、牛等动物帮助下建成。建造者改用篮子与双手等简单工具，搬运大量泥土。这是需要高度组织劳动力的浩大工程。但它不只是运土。该遗址是活动枢纽。在此发现的石器与陶器等文物，可追溯到来自远至阿巴拉契亚山脉与五大湖的来源。这显示令人印象深刻的贸易联系范围。住得如此靠近密西西比河意味着这些人并不孤立，而是庞大网络的一部分。本质上，Poverty Point 挑战我们对北美古代社会的假设。

choices.label: To highlight an ancient site that required large-scale planning
choices.labelZh: 强调一处需要大规模规划的古代遗址

choices.label: To compare different types of prehistoric earthen mounds

choices.explanationZh: 未比较不同类型土墩，仅详述Poverty Point单个遗址特征，无对比结构。

choices.explanationZh: 原文关键句：‘builders used simple tools like baskets and their own hands, moving massive amounts of earth. This was a monumental task…’ 强调纯人力搬运巨量泥土，即大量手工劳动。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a music podcast.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a music podcast. Have you ever wondered how music influences our eating habits? Well, it turns out that the kind of music playing in the background when we dine can significantly shape our culinary experience. Recent research has demonstrated that fast music, music with a rapid tempo, can make us eat more quickly, while slower tunes encourage us to savor our meals. And, you know, my doctor's been telling me eating slowly is good for digestion and health. It's important to chew the food well. Anyway, music isn't just about speed. It's about taste perception as well. For instance, a study found that high-pitched music can enhance the sweetness of a dish, while a lower pitch might accentuate its bitterness. Restaurants have started to take note of these findings and are curating playlists to improve their patrons' dining experiences. This auditory seasoning, as some call it, is becoming an essential part of the ambiance. Now, some argue that auditory manipulation can detract from the authenticity of the food experience. It can make diners more susceptible to overeating or misjudging the quality of their meal. This isn't just theory. Take the example of a high-end restaurant that experimented with soundscapes by playing ocean sounds. They found that diners rated seafood dishes more favorably, feeling as if they were right by the sea. While this kind of thing might revolutionize dining, some diners prefer a more genuine taste experience, free from any auditory influence.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段音乐播客的讲座。你是否想过音乐如何影响我们的饮食习惯？结果发现，用餐时背景播放的音乐类型可显著塑造我们的味觉体验。最近研究表明，快音乐——节奏快的音乐——可让我们吃得更快，而较慢的曲调鼓励我们细细品味。而且，你知道，我的医生一直告诉我慢吃对消化与健康有益。把食物嚼好很重要。无论如何，音乐不只关乎速度。也关乎味觉感知。例如，一项研究发现高音音乐会增强菜肴甜味，而较低音高可能突出苦味。餐厅已开始注意这些发现，并策划播放列表以改善顾客用餐体验。这种有人称为听觉调味的做法正成为氛围的重要部分。现在有人认为听觉操控会削弱食物体验的真实性。它可使用餐者更易过量进食或误判餐食质量。这不只是理论。以一家高端餐厅为例，它通过播放海洋声做声景实验。他们发现用餐者对海鲜菜肴评价更积极，感觉仿佛就在海边。尽管这类做法可能革命化用餐，一些用餐者更偏好不受任何听觉影响的更真实味觉体验。

choices.label: Higher-pitched music can cause people to eat more quickly.
choices.labelZh: 较高音高的音乐可能导致人们吃得更快。
choices.explanationZh: 吃得更快来自 fast tempo；higher pitch 对应的是 sweetness。

questions.promptTextZh: 利用音乐来影响食物感知有何批评？

choices.explanationZh: 讲座没有把问题归因于个人口味差异导致结果不可预测。

versions.label: Wofo M33
versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a history class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class.
During the Roman Empire, soldiers had a lot of, uh, weapons and armor, and they needed a place to store them. Their arms and armor. Soldiers used boxes called armariums to store this gear. Armariums were big, portable wooden storage boxes. Later, people, including civilians, kept using armariums in their homes, but to store items like clothing, books, or other valuables.
In France in the 16th century, wealthy people had them and called them armoires. Armoire is a term we still use today for a large, standalone piece of wooden furniture for storing things. Around the same time, some homes in England started to have what they called closets. But these closets were more like, uh, small studies where people could store things, or also just read or be alone. Someone might play their guitar in one to relax. So both the armoire and the English closet, they were kind of precursors to the modern closet.
If we fast forward to the mid-1800s, in the early United States, we're starting to see closets that are built directly into homes as part of the floor plan. The big benefit of these was that they were less pricey than armoires. Way cheaper. People had less clothing then than they do today, and they'd usually use a small chest to store clothes, or hang them on a peg or hook. Coat hangers weren't invented until the late 1800s. But still, closets in the home were handy places to store other belongings.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段历史课的讲座。
罗马帝国时期，士兵有许多，呃，武器与盔甲，需要地方存放。他们的兵器与盔甲。士兵用称为 armarium 的箱子存放这些装备。Armarium 是大型便携木制储物箱。后来包括平民在内的人们继续在家使用 armarium，但用来存放衣物、书籍或其他贵重物品。
十六世纪的法国，富人拥有它们并称为 armoire。Armoire 是我们今天仍用于大型独立木制储物家具的词。大约同时，英格兰一些住宅开始有他们称为 closet 的空间。但这些 closet 更像，呃，可存放物品、也可只是阅读或独处的小书房。有人可能在里面弹吉他放松。因此 armoire 与英格兰 closet 都有点像现代壁橱的前身。
若快进到十九世纪中期，在早期美国，我们开始看到作为平面图一部分直接建入住宅的壁橱。其大好处是比 armoire 更不贵。便宜得多。那时人们衣服比现在少，通常用小箱子存衣，或挂在钉或钩上。衣架直到十九世纪末才发明。但家中的壁橱仍是存放其他物品的便利地方。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker mainly discuss?

choices.label: The ways that modern homes imitate a Roman design

choices.explanationZh: 错误。未主张现代住宅模仿罗马设计，而是追溯储物空间的历时演变。

choices.label: The evolution of storage spaces in European and United States homes
choices.labelZh: 欧洲和美国家庭储物空间的演变
choices.explanationZh: 正确。全文按时间线展开：罗马armarium→法国armoire/英国closet→美国内置closet，覆盖欧、美地域与时代变迁。

choices.label: The usefulness of wood as a building material in homes
choices.labelZh: 木材作为住宅建筑材料的实用性
choices.explanationZh: 错误。虽多次提‘wooden’，但未讨论木材性能或建材优势。

choices.label: The reasons that armoires and closets were popular among wealthy people
choices.labelZh: 衣柜和壁橱在富人中受欢迎的原因
choices.explanationZh: 错误。未分析流行原因，且16世纪法国armoires被描述为实用家具，非侧重装饰性。

questions.promptText: Based on the talk, how were French armoires different from Roman armariums?
questions.promptTextZh: 根据讲座，法国衣柜与罗马储物柜有何不同？

choices.label: French armoires held a different category of items

choices.labelZh: 法国衣柜更大、更重
choices.explanationZh: 尺寸对比未出现，‘larger and heavier’无文本支持。

choices.label: French armoires were made of a different kind of wood
choices.labelZh: 法国衣柜由不同种类的木材制成
choices.explanationZh: 木材种类未被说明，‘different kind of wood’属无依据推断。

choices.label: French armoires were mostly decorative
choices.labelZh: 法国衣柜主要用于装饰
choices.explanationZh: 功能始终是储物（‘for storing things’），未提装饰性用途，‘mostly decorative’曲解原意。

versions.transcript: During the Roman Empire, soldiers had a lot of weapons and armor, and they needed a place to store them, their arms and armor. Soldiers used boxes called armariums to store this gear. Armariums were big portable wooden storage boxes. Later, people including civilians kept using armariums in their homes, but to store items like clothing, books, or other valuables. In France in the sixteenth century, wealthy people had them and called them armoires. Armoire is a term we still use today for a large standalone piece of wooden furniture for storing things. Around the same time, some homes in England started to have what they called closets. But these closets were more like small studies, where people could store things, or also just read or be alone. Someone might play their guitar in one to relax. So both the armoire and the English closet were kind of precursors to the modern closet. If we fast forward to the mid 1800s in the early United States, we're starting to see closets that are built directly into homes as part of the floor plan. The big benefit of these was that they were less pricey than armoires, way cheaper. People had less clothing then than they do today, and they'd usually use a small chest to store clothes or hang them on a peg or hook. Coat hangers weren't invented until the late 1800s, but still closets in the home were handy places to store other belongings.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to part of a history lecture.
versions.transcript:
Listen to part of a history lecture.
In the year 1453, the Byzantine Empire ended with the conquest of its capital, Constantinople. After that happened, many Greek scholars who lived there fled to Italy, and they brought to Italy their knowledge of ancient Greek language, philosophy, etc., which hadn't been preserved particularly well there. Now, this knowledge came in the form of manuscripts, which naturally were in ancient Greek. They were written way back before the start of the Byzantine Empire. So, the Greek scholars taught Greek to the Italian scholars they met and worked with Italian translators who could translate Greek literature into their own language. This provided new access to ancient Greek knowledge. It led Italian scholars to shift from mainly studying theology to also studying the humanities, like history and art. This influence lasted throughout the Renaissance. Ah, as you know, the Renaissance is an important period in European history, which began in Italy and which saw renewed interest in learning, science, and the arts. The city of Venice, Italy, had a large Greek community that grew after 1453 with the influx of Greek scholars. Venice then turned into a hub of classical Greek studies and culture. For one thing, it became a leader in the printing industry and helped spread Greek works in book form. It also became the home of Greek churches and a center for that religious tradition, which still has a presence throughout Italy.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听历史讲座的一部分。
一四五三年，拜占庭帝国随其首都君士坦丁堡被征服而终结。此后许多住在那里的希腊学者逃往意大利，并把古希腊语言、哲学等知识带到意大利，而这些在当地保存得并不特别好。这些知识以手稿形式到来，自然是古希腊文。它们写于拜占庭帝国开始很久以前。因此希腊学者向他们遇见的意大利学者教希腊文，并与能把希腊文学译成自己语言的意大利译者合作。这提供了对古希腊知识的新途径。它使意大利学者从主要研究神学转向也研究人文学科，如历史与艺术。这一影响贯穿整个文艺复兴。啊，如你所知，文艺复兴是欧洲史上重要时期，始于意大利，见证了对学问、科学与艺术的重新兴趣。意大利威尼斯城有一个在一四五三年后随希腊学者涌入而壮大的大型希腊社区。威尼斯随后成为古典希腊研究与文化的中心。一方面，它成为印刷业领袖，并帮助以书籍形式传播希腊作品。它也成为希腊教堂所在地与该宗教传统的中心，这一传统在意大利各地仍有存在。

versions.transcriptZh: 1453年，拜占庭帝国随着其首都君士坦丁堡的陷落而告终。 此事发生后，许多曾居住在那里的希腊学者逃往意大利，他们将对古希腊语言、哲学等知识带到意大利，而这些知识在那里并没有得到很好的保存。 这些知识以手稿的形式出现，这些手稿自然是古希腊语的。 它们早在拜占庭帝国开始之前就已经写成了。 因此，希腊学者向他们遇到的意大利学者教授希腊语，并与意大利翻译家合作，将希腊文学翻译成他们自己的语言。 这为获取古希腊知识提供了新的途径。 它使得意大利学者从主要研究神学转向也研究历史和艺术等人文学科。 这种影响持续了整个文艺复兴时期。 众所周知，文艺复兴是欧洲历史上一个重要时期，它始于意大利，并重新激发了人们对学习、科学和艺术的兴趣。 意大利威尼斯市拥有一个庞大的希腊社区，在1453年希腊学者涌入后，这个社区不断壮大。 威尼斯随后成为古典希腊研究和文化的中心。 一方面，它成为印刷业的领导者，并帮助以书籍形式传播希腊作品。 它也成为希腊教堂的所在地和该宗教传统的中心，这种传统至今仍在意大利各地存在。

transcriptSentences.text: The city of Venice, Italy had a large Greek community that grew after 1453 with the influx of Greek scholars.

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a history of technology podcast. You've probably used many remote controls for things: televisions, smart devices, and other electronics. My wife uses one to open the gate to her parking lot at work. Now, remote controls for televisions have been around since the 1950s. Wired remote controls had been used before then, back to around 1870, mostly for unpiloted military vehicles. Later, the inventor Nikola Tesla developed a wireless remote control for military vehicles in 1898. As for TV remotes, the first really popular one was developed in 1950. It was called the Lazy Bones. It was pretty expensive. Unfortunately, the Lazy Bones was connected to the TV by a long wire, which of course was annoying and a trip hazard. It's kind of hard to imagine this was more practical for most people than just getting up and turning the dial on the television yourself. A few years later, in 1955, a wireless remote was introduced: the Flash-Matic. To use the Flash-Matic, you'd point it at one of the corners of your TV screen. This would shine a light beam at the chosen corner. Now, each corner had its own purpose: channel up or down, power, or mute. Each corner had a photoelectric cell to convert the light beam into an electrical signal to do what you wanted. Trouble was, the photoelectric cells responded to other light sources too, like light from a light bulb or even sunlight. Imagine turning on a light bulb and your TV suddenly turns on too.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a materials science class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in a materials science class. Big-city skyscrapers are so tall they seem to defy gravity, right? Well, they're made possible by a material called reinforced concrete, really a feat of modern engineering. Reinforced concrete integrates two very different materials: concrete and steel. Concrete has excellent compressive strength, meaning it can be squeezed hard without breaking, the same way that a chair doesn't crumble when you sit in it. But concrete cracks under tensile stress, when it's being pulled on. Think of lifting a grocery bag with a heavy bowling ball in it. The bag might tear apart when you lift it, right? And steel is just the opposite: it has tensile strength, but is not so great under compression. By joining these two, engineers created a material that resists both compression and tension, making it indispensable for constructing resilient structures like tall buildings. But how exactly do they work together? For one thing, concrete and steel expand and contract at nearly identical rates in response to temperature variations. All materials expand slightly when they get warmer and contract when they cool. If the rates at which two combined materials do so are different, cracks may develop over time. But here, we don't have this problem. Now, reinforced concrete isn't perfect. Environmental factors, particularly in regions with salty air, like coastal areas, can lead to steel corrosion, which affects its strength. Alternatives like stainless steel or fiberglass are being explored, but they come with higher costs.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段材料科学课的讲座。大城市摩天楼高得仿佛无视重力，对吧？它们靠一种叫钢筋混凝土的材料成为可能，真是现代工程的壮举。钢筋混凝土整合两种截然不同的材料：混凝土与钢。混凝土抗压强度极好，意思是可被用力挤压而不碎，就像椅子不会因你坐下而崩塌。但混凝土在拉应力下会裂，也就是被拉扯时。想象提起装着重保龄球的购物袋。一提袋子可能撕裂，对吧？钢恰恰相反：有抗拉强度，但抗压不那么强。把二者结合，工程师创造出既抗压又抗拉的材料，对建造摩天楼这类韧性结构不可或缺。它们究竟如何协同？其一，混凝土与钢随温度变化膨胀收缩速率几乎相同。所有材料变热时略胀、变冷时收缩。若两种结合材料速率不同，久之可能开裂。但这里没有这个问题。钢筋混凝土并非完美。环境因素，尤其在海岸等盐雾地区，可导致钢腐蚀，影响强度。不锈钢或玻璃纤维等替代材料正在探索，但成本更高。

transcriptSentences.text: Reinforced concrete integrates two very different materials: concrete and steel.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 钢筋混凝土整合两种截然不同的材料：混凝土与钢。

transcriptSentences.text: Concrete has excellent compressive strength, meaning it can be squeezed hard without breaking, the same way that a chair doesn't crumble when you sit in it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 混凝土抗压强度极好，意思是可被用力挤压而不碎，就像椅子不会因你坐下而崩塌。

transcriptSentences.text: But concrete cracks under tensile stress, when it's being pulled on.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但混凝土在拉应力下会裂，也就是被拉扯时。

transcriptSentences.text: Think of lifting a grocery bag with a heavy bowling ball in it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 想象提起装着重保龄球的购物袋。

transcriptSentences.text: The bag might tear apart when you lift it, right?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 一提袋子可能撕裂，对吧？

transcriptSentences.text: And steel is just the opposite: it has tensile strength, but is not so great under compression.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 钢恰恰相反：有抗拉强度，但抗压不那么强。

transcriptSentences.text: By joining these two, engineers created a material that resists both compression and tension, making it indispensable for constructing resilient structures like tall buildings.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 把二者结合，工程师创造出既抗压又抗拉的材料，对建造摩天楼这类韧性结构不可或缺。

transcriptSentences.text: But how exactly do they work together?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们究竟如何协同？

transcriptSentences.text: For one thing, concrete and steel expand and contract at nearly identical rates in response to temperature variations.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 其一，混凝土与钢随温度变化膨胀收缩速率几乎相同。

transcriptSentences.text: All materials expand slightly when they get warmer and contract when they cool.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 所有材料变热时略胀、变冷时收缩。

transcriptSentences.text: If the rates at which two combined materials do so are different, cracks may develop over time.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 若两种结合材料速率不同，久之可能开裂。

transcriptSentences.text: But here, we don't have this problem.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但这里没有这个问题。

transcriptSentences.text: Now, reinforced concrete isn't perfect.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 钢筋混凝土并非完美。

transcriptSentences.text: Environmental factors, particularly in regions with salty air, like coastal areas, can lead to steel corrosion, which affects its strength.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 环境因素，尤其在海岸等盐雾地区，可导致钢腐蚀，影响强度。

transcriptSentences.text: Alternatives like stainless steel or fiberglass are being explored, but they come with higher costs.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 不锈钢或玻璃纤维等替代材料正在探索，但成本更高。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker mainly discuss?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者主要讨论了什么？

choices.label: The reasons that skyscrapers have been built taller over time
choices.labelZh: 摩天大楼随时间越建越高的原因
choices.explanationZh: skyscrapers 只是开头引出 reinforced concrete 的例子；讲座没有解释摩天楼为什么越来越高。

choices.label: The combination of two materials to build strong structures
choices.labelZh: 两种材料结合以建造坚固结构
choices.explanationZh: 正确：讲座主线是 concrete 和 steel 如何互补，合成 reinforced concrete 来同时抵抗 compression 和 tension。

choices.label: The processes used to make different building materials
choices.labelZh: 制造不同建筑材料的过程
choices.explanationZh: 讲座讲材料性能和配合方式，不讲不同建材的制造流程。

choices.label: The best and worst options for construction materials
choices.labelZh: 建筑材料的最佳与最差选择
choices.explanationZh: 结尾只提 reinforced concrete 的缺点和替代材料成本高，不是在比较最好和最差建材。

questions.promptText: Why does the speaker mention a grocery bag?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者为何提到一个杂货袋？

choices.label: To compare the weights of concrete and steel
choices.labelZh: 为了比较混凝土和钢材的重量
choices.explanationZh: grocery bag 的例子不是比较 concrete 和 steel 的重量，而是说明被拉扯时会撕裂。

choices.label: To explain why concrete can become squeezed
choices.labelZh: 为了解释为何混凝土会被挤压
choices.explanationZh: concrete 被挤压不碎是 compressive strength，speaker 用 chair 解释；grocery bag 讲的是 tensile stress。

choices.label: To illustrate what happens when tensile strength is absent
choices.labelZh: 为了说明没有抗拉强度时会发生什么
choices.explanationZh: 正确：装着重物的袋子被提起时可能撕裂，正好说明缺少 tensile strength 时材料承受不了拉力。

choices.label: To point out a difference between paper and plastic
choices.labelZh: 为了指出纸与塑料的区别
choices.explanationZh: 讲座没有比较纸袋和塑料袋；bag 只是用来解释拉力问题。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker say about temperature variations?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者对温度变化有何说法？

choices.label: They improve the strength of reinforced concrete.
choices.labelZh: 它们增强了钢筋混凝土的强度。
choices.explanationZh: temperature variations 没有被说成能增强 reinforced concrete；重点是两种材料热胀冷缩速率接近。

choices.label: They worsen the effect of salt on buildings.
choices.labelZh: 它们加剧了盐对建筑物的影响。
choices.explanationZh: salt corrosion 是另一个环境问题，和 temperature variations 不是同一个因果关系。

choices.label: Concrete and steel react to them in similar ways.
choices.labelZh: 混凝土和钢材对它们的反应相似。
choices.explanationZh: 正确：speaker 明确说 concrete and steel expand and contract at nearly identical rates，所以温度变化下反应相似。

choices.label: If they are extreme, cracks in buildings will form.
choices.labelZh: 如果变化剧烈，建筑物裂缝会形成。
choices.explanationZh: 原文说如果两种材料膨胀收缩速率不同才可能 crack，不是温度极端就一定形成裂缝。

questions.promptText: What does the speaker imply about stainless steel and fiberglass?
questions.promptTextZh: 演讲者对不锈钢和玻璃纤维有何暗示？

choices.label: They may be better than reinforced concrete in coastal areas.
choices.labelZh: 它们在沿海地区可能优于钢筋混凝土。
choices.explanationZh: 正确：coastal areas 的 salty air 会导致 steel corrosion，speaker 随后说 stainless steel 和 fiberglass 正被探索，暗示它们可能更适合这种环境。

choices.label: They may work together to improve resistance to environmental factors.
choices.labelZh: 它们可能协同作用以提高抗环境因素能力。
choices.explanationZh: 原文说它们是 alternatives，没有说 stainless steel 和 fiberglass 要组合使用。

choices.label: They are simpler to produce than reinforced concrete.
choices.labelZh: 它们比钢筋混凝土更易于生产。
choices.explanationZh: 讲座只说这些替代材料成本更高，没有说生产更简单。

choices.label: They tend to corrode in a similar way as reinforced concrete does.
choices.labelZh: 它们与钢筋混凝土的腐蚀方式相似。
choices.explanationZh: 它们被提到是因为 salty air 会让 reinforced concrete 中的 steel 腐蚀；不是说这些替代材料也同样腐蚀。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a biology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a biology class.
So today, I want to tell you about the stargazer fish, a creature that not only excels in camouflage but also uses an unexpected twist in its predatory tactics. The stargazer fish is recognized for its distinct eyes. They face upward, and the stargazer buries itself within the sandy ocean floor, rendering itself practically invisible. This remarkable method of concealment serves as an effective hunting tool. However, the stargazer doesn't stop there. It's got specialized electric organs that can deliver a shock that's potent enough to paralyze its prey. So, the evolutionary advantage of this electrifying adaptation is pretty evident, right? The stargazer can conserve some energy with its hiding because it minimizes the need to chase prey, thereby increasing its chances of securing a meal. Yet, as often is the case, this adaptation is not without its trade-offs. The energy required to develop and maintain these electric organs is substantial, potentially rendering the stargazer more susceptible to environmental stressors, such as temperature changes or reduced food availability. So, the stargazer, it raises intriguing questions about energy trade-offs in evolutionary biology. How do organisms balance the benefits of a specialized adaptation against the costs of maintaining it?
isms navigate the complexities of balancing the advantages of specialized adaptations against their metabolic demands or a changing environment. The stargazer embodies this intricate balance of survival, showcasing that nature, in its profound complexity, often revolves around finding equilibrium between innovation and sustainability.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段生物学课的讲座。
今天我想讲讲瞻星鱼——一种不仅擅长伪装，还在捕食策略上使用意外手法的生物。瞻星鱼因其独特的眼睛而闻名。眼睛朝上，瞻星鱼把自己埋进沙质海底，使自己几乎看不见。这种非凡的隐蔽方法充当有效的狩猎工具。然而瞻星鱼不止于此。它有特化的发电器官，可释放足以麻痹猎物的电击。因此，这种电击适应的进化优势相当明显，对吧？瞻星鱼可通过隐藏节省一些能量，因为它减少追逐猎物的需要，从而提高获得一餐的机会。然而，一如既往，这种适应并非没有代价。发育并维持这些发电器官所需的能量可观，可能使瞻星鱼更易受环境压力影响，如温度变化或食物减少。因此瞻星鱼引发关于进化生物学中能量权衡的有趣问题。生物如何在特化适应的益处与维持它的成本之间取得平衡？生物如何在特化适应的优势与其代谢需求或变化环境之间驾驭复杂的平衡。瞻星鱼体现这种精妙的生存平衡，表明自然在其深刻复杂性中，往往围绕在创新与可持续之间找到均衡。

questions.promptText: What is the main focus of the talk?
questions.promptTextZh: 讲座的主要内容是什么？

choices.label: The camouflage techniques of marine animals
choices.labelZh: 海洋动物的伪装技术
choices.explanationZh: 仅提及其他海洋动物的伪装属干扰信息，全文聚焦于星眼鱼一种物种。

choices.label: How adaptations help a marine species survive and hunt
choices.labelZh: 适应性如何帮助海洋物种生存和捕猎
choices.explanationZh: 全文围绕星眼鱼如何通过伪装与放电适应生存与捕食，并分析其利弊，核心即‘适应如何助其生存与捕食’。

choices.label: The energy costs of living in the ocean
choices.labelZh: 在海洋中生存的能量成本
choices.explanationZh: ‘海洋生活能量成本’过于宽泛，文中特指星眼鱼放电器官的代谢代价，非泛论海洋环境。

choices.label: How hunting strategies have evolved in different species of fish
choices.labelZh: 不同鱼类捕猎策略的演变
choices.explanationZh: 未比较不同鱼类策略，仅深入分析星眼鱼单一物种的策略。

questions.promptText: How does the stargazer fish primarily capture prey?
questions.promptTextZh: 瞻星鱼主要如何捕捉猎物？

choices.label: By actively pursuing it
choices.labelZh: 通过主动追逐
choices.explanationZh: 文中明确说它‘埋入沙中’‘无需追逐猎物’，故非主动追捕。

choices.label: By floating completely motionlessly
choices.labelZh: 通过完全静止地漂浮
choices.explanationZh: ‘完全静止’不准确：它虽隐蔽但会放电攻击，并非被动漂浮。

choices.label: By utilizing a combination of camouflage and electrical discharges
choices.labelZh: 通过结合伪装和电放电
choices.explanationZh: 原文‘excelling in camouflage’且‘got specialized electric organs to paralyze prey’，直接对应此选项。

choices.label: By creating sound waves
choices.labelZh: 通过产生声波
choices.explanationZh: 全文未提及声波相关机制。

questions.promptText: According to the speaker, what is a significant drawback associated with the stargazer's hunting adaptation?
questions.promptTextZh: 根据说话者的描述，与瞻星鱼的捕猎适应性相关的一个显著缺点是什么？

choices.label: Increased visibility to predators
choices.labelZh: 更容易被天敌发现
choices.explanationZh: 文中未提及其因伪装而更易被天敌发现。

choices.label: High energy levels needed for certain organs
choices.labelZh: 某些器官需要高能量
choices.explanationZh: 原文明确指出‘the energy required to develop and maintain these electric organs is substantial’，即特定器官需高能量维持。

choices.label: Limited speed and agility
choices.labelZh: 速度和敏捷性有限
choices.explanationZh: 未讨论其运动速度或灵活性受限。

choices.label: Impaired vision due to eyes that face upward
choices.labelZh: 因眼睛朝上而导致视力受损
choices.explanationZh: 朝上的眼睛是伪装适应，文中未称其损害视力。

questions.promptText: According to the speaker, what aspect of evolutionary biology is illustrated by the stargazer's adaptation?
questions.promptTextZh: 根据说话者的描述，瞻星鱼的适应性体现了进化生物学的哪个方面？

choices.label: The simplicity of natural adaptations
choices.labelZh: 自然适应性的简单性
choices.explanationZh: 全文强调适应的‘权衡’（trade-offs），非简化性。

choices.label: The elegance of predatory tactics
choices.labelZh: 捕食策略的精妙性
choices.explanationZh: ‘捕食技巧优雅’是主观描述，非演讲主旨。

choices.label: The balance between adaptive advantages and metabolic costs
choices.labelZh: 适应性优势与代谢成本之间的平衡
choices.explanationZh: 结尾句‘How do organisms balance the benefits... against the costs...’及‘intricate balance’直接点明此核心。

choices.label: The unpredictability of marine life evolution
choices.labelZh: 海洋生物进化的不可预测性
choices.explanationZh: ‘不可预测性’未被强调；演讲突出的是可分析的平衡机制。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a music history class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a music history class.
Imagine taking a regular piano and transforming its sound by inserting everyday objects like screws, bolts, and rubber erasers between the strings. This is what's known as a prepared piano. It was developed by the avant-garde composer John Cage in 1940. Cage was working at a university in Seattle, and he needed to write music with percussion to accompany dances. But the performance space's stage wasn't big enough for percussion instruments like drums. So, he made the sounds with just the piano by placing objects between the strings. Now, Cage spent time searching for items that made the kind of sounds he was looking for. It had a feel of improvisation. Cage himself said that looking for items was kind of like walking on the beach and looking for shiny or beautiful seashells that you liked. That is, he didn't know ahead of time what items he wanted to use. He just kept looking around and seeing what suited his needs. Cage ended up composing a collection of music for prepared piano in the mid-1940s. He included specific instructions for how to prepare the piano. For this collection, Cage was inspired by ancient Hindu theory about eight essential emotions. He wanted his listeners to sense eight essential emotions from Hindu philosophy. The result is a blending of sounds that would be familiar to a Western audience, plus sounds reminiscent of Indonesian gamelan. Gamelan is traditional Indonesian percussion music. This prepared piano music really raised John Cage's profile in the music world.

请听一段音乐史课的讲座。
想象把普通钢琴通过在琴弦间插入螺丝、螺栓与橡皮等日常物品来改变其声音。这就是所谓预制钢琴。它由先锋作曲家约翰·凯奇于一九四〇年开发。凯奇在西雅图一所大学工作，需要写带打击的音乐为舞蹈伴奏。但表演空间的舞台放不下鼓等打击乐器。于是他只靠钢琴，通过把物品放在琴弦间来制造声音。凯奇花时间寻找能发出他想要声音的物品。这带有即兴感。凯奇自己说找物品有点像在海滩上找你喜欢的闪亮或美丽贝壳。也就是说，他事先不知道想用什么物品。他只是不断四处看，看什么适合他的需要。凯奇最终在一九四〇年代中期为预制钢琴创作了一组音乐。他附上了如何预制钢琴的具体说明。对这组作品，凯奇受古代印度教关于八种基本情感理论的启发。他希望听众感受到印度教哲学中的八种基本情感。结果是对西方听众熟悉的声音与令人联想到印尼加美兰的声音的融合。加美兰是传统印尼打击乐。这些预制钢琴音乐真正提升了约翰·凯奇在音乐界的地位。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a physics class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a physics class.

Man: We've been talking about the law of inertia. An object moving in a straight line will continue to move in a straight line unless it is acted upon by another force. So what does this mean in the real world? Let's look at something many people do all the time, riding a bicycle. Think about riding along in a straight line. Once the bike is moving, inertia will keep it going in a straight line. But we don't just ride in straight lines, do we? We turn at corners and steer around things that are in our way. So how do you get the bicycle not to go straight? Easy, right? Don't you just need to turn the front wheel in the direction you want to turn? In fact, if you only turn the front wheel, you're likely to end up on the pavement. The wheel will turn, but because of inertia, your body and the rest of the bike will want to keep moving straight ahead. So how does a cyclist avoid this? The key is to lean in. Weight needs to shift in the direction of the turn so that the force of gravity can work against the force of inertia. Professional cyclists who move at high speeds need to hit a sweet spot. They must lean more to keep their bicycles from sliding out of turns, but not too much. At a certain point, gravity will bring both rider and bicycle down to the ground.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段物理课的讲座。

男：我们一直在谈惯性定律。沿直线运动的物体会继续沿直线运动，除非有另一力作用其上。现实中这意味着什么？来看许多人常做的事：骑自行车。想想沿直线骑行。车一旦动起来，惯性会让它保持直行。但我们不只走直线，对吧？我们转弯、绕开路上的东西。那如何让自行车不直行？简单，对吧？只需把前轮转到想转的方向？其实若只转前轮，你多半会摔到路上。轮子会转，但因惯性，身体与车身其余部分仍想继续向前。骑车人如何避免？关键是向内倾。体重需向转弯方向移动，让重力对抗惯性。高速骑行的职业车手需找到最佳点。他们必须多倾以防止出弯打滑，但又不能过。到某一点，重力会把人车都带倒在地。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an archaeology class. Often when we think of mummies, we think of ancient Egyptians and their elaborate methods of preserving bodies. We used to think Egyptians were the only people practicing mummification during the Bronze Age about 4,000 years ago, because typical mummies are found in places with very dry climates like Egypt. But then archaeologists discovered a site in Scotland with evidence of mummification, and Scotland is wet and rainy. This site is called Cladh Hallan, the only place in Britain where we found prehistoric Bronze Age mummies. Researchers unearthed skeletons there, including a man and a woman from around 1500 BCE. Since these were just skeletons, the researchers did not realize at first that they had actually been mummies. Radiocarbon dating revealed that the man and woman had died several hundred years before being buried. Normally, such a long wait would turn a body into a pile of bones, not an actual skeleton. So their bodies must have been purposely preserved for hundreds of years before burial. The bodies were preserved, mummified in a peat bog. Peat bogs are like swamps, except their conditions prevent organic materials like bodies from fully breaking down. Prehistoric people in Scotland used to preserve animal fat like butter in peat bogs, so they definitely had the concept.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a history class.
Today, let's talk about the ancient Maya civilization and explore a fascinating revelation about its decline. A vast civilization with impressive cities and flourishing culture that suddenly crumbled into history. For years, scholars have debated what might have happened, and now, recent research has brought stalagmites into the spotlight. Stalagmites, those formations rising up from the floor of a cave, are more than just geological wonders. They serve as climate records, capturing changes in precipitation over thousands of years. In 2025, scientists analyzed stalagmites from caves near the former Maya heartlands. The data revealed a series of prolonged droughts that coincided with periods of decline for the Maya society. Now, Maya were heavily dependent on agriculture, with water being a critical resource for their survival. When these droughts occurred, the scarcity of water likely put immense pressure on their food production and societal structures. Imagine cities struggling without enough water for crops, leading to food shortages and social unrest. It's important to note, though, that while these climate changes were significant, they weren't the sole cause. Other factors like warfare and politics played a role too. Yet, the revelation from these stalagmites provides a clearer picture of how environmental changes can trigger societal shifts. This discovery not only sheds light on the past but also serves as a reminder of our vulnerability to climate change today.

请听一段历史课的讲座。
今天我们谈谈古代玛雅文明，并探讨关于其衰落的一个迷人发现。一个拥有宏伟城市与繁荣文化、却突然崩塌进历史的庞大文明。多年来学者争论可能发生了什么，现在最近研究把石笋推到聚光灯下。石笋——那些从洞穴地面向上生长的构造——不只是地质奇观。它们充当气候记录，捕捉数千年间降水变化。二零二五年，科学家分析了靠近原玛雅中心地带洞穴中的石笋。数据揭示一系列与玛雅社会衰落时期重合的长期干旱。玛雅高度依赖农业，水是其生存的关键资源。当这些干旱发生时，水短缺很可能给粮食生产与社会结构带来巨大压力。想象城市在作物缺水下挣扎，导致粮食短缺与社会动荡。但要注意，尽管这些气候变化重要，它们并非唯一原因。战争与政治等其他因素也起作用。然而这些石笋的发现更清楚地说明环境变化如何触发社会转变。这一发现不仅照亮过去，也提醒我们今天对气候变化的脆弱。

versions.transcript:
Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
We've been talking about the iconic North American monarch butterflies. Many monarch butterflies migrate annually between the northern United States, where they spend summer, and Mexico, where they spend winter. Previously, however, researchers could only guess at some details of monarch butterfly migrations. They knew where the butterflies started and ended their journey, but not what happened in between. Now, with the help of new tracking devices, scientists can track precise routes, including stopover points and even detours. This level of detail could reveal how climate patterns and habitat loss affect migration success. Early data have already revealed surprises. For example, some monarch butterflies take far longer pauses than we ever imagined. Specifically, several butterflies that were tagged with the tracking devices in Kansas lingered for nearly two weeks in central Texas before continuing southward. These extended stopovers may help butterflies refuel and recover energy, reshaping how conservationists think about preserving habitats along the migration corridor. The technology isn't without challenges, however. The tracking devices depend on sunlight for power, so dense cloud cover along migration routes can limit data collection. Despite these and other hurdles, the knowledge gained could be vital for saving one of nature's most iconic creatures.

versions.transcript: We've been talking about the iconic North American monarch butterflies. Many monarch butterflies migrate annually between the northern United States, where they spend summer, and Mexico, where they spend winter. Previously, however, researchers could only guess at some details of monarch butterfly migrations. They knew where the butterflies started and ended their journey, but not what happened in between. Now, with the help of new tracking devices, scientists can track precise routes, including stopover points and even detours. This level of detail could reveal how climate patterns and habitat loss affect migration success. Early data have already revealed surprises. For example, some monarch butterflies take far longer pauses than we ever imagined. Specifically, several butterflies that were tagged with the tracking devices in Kansas lingered for nearly two weeks in central Texas before continuing southward. These extended stopovers may help butterflies refuel and recover energy, reshaping how conservationists think about preserving habitats along the migration corridor. The technology isn't without challenges, however. The tracking devices depend on sunlight for power, so dense cloud cover along migration routes can limit data collection. Despite these and other hurdles, the knowledge gained would be vital for saving one of nature's most iconic creatures.
versions.transcriptZh: 我们一直在讨论标志性的北美帝王蝶。 许多帝王蝶每年在它们度过夏季的美国北部和度过冬季的墨西哥之间迁徙。 然而，在此之前，研究人员只能猜测帝王蝶迁徙的一些细节。 他们知道蝴蝶从哪里开始和结束它们的旅程，但不知道中间发生了什么。 现在，借助新的追踪设备，科学家可以追踪精确的路线，包括中途停留点甚至绕道。 这种详细程度可以揭示气候模式和栖息地丧失如何影响迁徙的成功。 早期数据已经揭示了一些惊喜。 例如，一些帝王蝶停留的时间比我们想象的要长得多。 具体来说，几只在堪萨斯州被标记的带有追踪设备的蝴蝶在德克萨斯州中部停留了近两周，然后才继续南下。 这些延长的停留可能有助于蝴蝶补充能量和恢复体力，从而改变了环保主义者对保护迁徙走廊沿线栖息地的看法。 然而，这项技术并非没有挑战。 追踪设备依靠阳光供电，因此迁徙路线上的密云可能会限制数据收集。 尽管存在这些和其他障碍，但所获得的知识对于拯救大自然最具代表性的生物之一至关重要。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a business podcast.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a business podcast. When launching a new business, entrepreneurs face countless decisions, from choosing a target market to deciding which features to include in their first product. These choices can be overwhelming, especially when resources are limited and time is short. To address these challenges, some startups adopt a strategy that emphasizes speed, experimentation, and customer feedback. This approach, known as the Lean Startup methodology, was popularized by Eric Ries and has gained traction in the tech world and beyond. One of its core practices is building a minimum viable product, or MVP. This is a basic version of a new product that can be released quickly to gather feedback from early users. The goal is to learn what works and what doesn't, so that future development is guided by actual user experience rather than assumptions. Another key principle is validated learning. Instead of doing traditional market research like surveys or focus groups, entrepreneurs test their ideas by putting the product out in the real world. This helps them figure out whether their product actually meets the needs of their customers. In all fairness, I should point out that this approach isn't perfect. Rapid iteration and constant feedback can sometimes lead to confusion or a lack of clear direction. And in the pursuit of efficiency, some teams may cut corners, which could affect product quality. Still, many entrepreneurs find the Lean Startup methodology helpful for navigating the uncertainties of launching a new business.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段商业播客的讲座。启动新企业时，创业者面临无数决策，从选择目标市场到决定首款产品包含哪些功能。这些选择可能令人不堪重负，尤其在资源有限、时间紧迫时。为应对这些挑战，一些初创采用强调速度、实验与客户反馈的策略。这一路径称为精益创业方法论，由埃里克·里斯推广，已在科技界及其他领域获得关注。其核心实践之一是打造最小可行产品，即 MVP。这是可快速发布以收集早期用户反馈的新产品基本版本。目标是了解什么有效、什么无效，使后续开发由真实用户体验而非假设引导。另一关键原则是验证性学习。创业者不是做调查或焦点小组等传统市场研究，而是把产品放到真实世界中检验想法。这帮助他们弄清产品是否真满足客户需求。公平地说，我应指出这一路径并不完美。快速迭代与持续反馈有时会导致混乱或缺乏明确方向。在追求效率时，有些团队可能走捷径，从而影响产品质量。尽管如此，许多创业者仍觉得精益创业方法论有助于驾驭启动新企业的不确定性。

versions.label: Koala 01-21
versions.transcript: When launching a new business, entrepreneurs face countless decisions, from choosing a target market to deciding which features to include in their first product. These choices can be overwhelming, especially when resources are limited and time is short. To address these challenges, some startups adopt a strategy that emphasizes speed, experimentation, and customer feedback. This approach, known as the Lean Startup methodology, was popularized by Eric Ries and has gained traction in the tech world and beyond. One of its core practices is building a minimum viable product, or MVP. This is a basic version of a new product that can be released quickly to gather feedback from early users. The goal is to learn what works and what doesn't, so that future development is guided by actual user experience rather than assumptions. Another key principle is validated learning. Instead of doing traditional market research like surveys or focus groups, entrepreneurs test their ideas by putting the product out in the real world. This helps them figure out whether their product actually meets the needs of their customers. In all fairness, I should point out that this approach isn't perfect. Rapid iteration and constant feedback can sometimes lead to confusion or a lack of clear direction. And in the pursuit of efficiency, some teams may cut corners, which could affect product quality. Still, many entrepreneurs find the Lean Startup methodology helpful for navigating the uncertainties of launching a new business.
versions.transcriptZh: 在创办新企业时，创业者面临着无数决策，从选择目标市场到决定在首款产品中包含哪些功能。 这些选择可能会让人感到应接不暇，尤其是在资源有限且时间紧迫的情况下。 为了应对这些挑战，一些初创公司采用了一种强调速度、实验和客户反馈的策略。 这种被称为精益创业（Lean Startup）的方法论由 Eric Ries 推广，并在科技界及其他领域获得了认可。 其核心实践之一是构建最小可行产品，即 MVP。 这是新产品的一个基础版本，可以快速发布，以便从早期用户那里收集反馈。 其目标是了解哪些方案可行，哪些不可行，从而使未来的开发由实际的用户体验而非假设来引导。 另一个关键原则是验证性学习。 创业者不是进行调查或焦点小组等传统市场研究，而是通过将产品投放并置于现实世界中来测试他们的想法。 这有助于他们确定自己的产品是否真正满足了客户的需求。 公平地说，我应该指出这种方法并不完美。 快速迭代和不断的反馈有时会导致混乱或缺乏明确的方向。 并且在追求效率的过程中，一些团队可能会偷工减料，这可能会影响产品质量。 尽管如此，许多创业者发现精益创业方法论对于应对创办新企业的不确定性非常有帮助。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk on a science podcast.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a science podcast.

Woman: Let's talk a bit about bird migration. Migratory birds travel vast distances between their breeding and wintering grounds, often covering thousands of miles. These journeys are driven by the need to find suitable habitats with adequate food supplies and favorable climate conditions. One of the most remarkable aspects of migration is a bird's ability to navigate accurately over such long distances. Birds use a variety of navigational cues, such as the position of the sun, stars, and, incredibly, Earth's magnetic field. Certain bird species have a special protein in their eyes that allows them to see magnetic fields, and this helps them stay on course. Migratory birds play key roles in ecosystems by dispersing seeds and controlling pests, so their decline can cause imbalances throughout food webs. Of course, a migration over hundreds or even thousands of miles will be fraught with risk. Obvious dangers include harsh weather conditions, predators, and the risk of exhaustion and starvation. Less obviously, human activities also pose significant threats to migratory birds. Habitat destruction, pollution and climate change have led to a decline in many migratory bird populations. At night, light pollution can disorient birds that navigate by the stars, causing them to become lost or collide with buildings. Protecting key habitats and reducing light pollution are a few of the steps that can help safeguard migrating birds. Solutions include bird friendly building design and programs that encourage turning off unnecessary lights during peak migration seasons.

请听一段科学播客的讲座。

女：我们来谈一点鸟类迁徙。候鸟在繁殖地与越冬地之间飞行遥远距离，常达数千英里。这些旅程受寻找食物充足、气候适宜的栖息地驱动。迁徙最非凡的方面之一是鸟在如此长距离上精确导航的能力。鸟使用多种导航线索，如太阳位置、星辰，以及——难以置信地——地球磁场。某些鸟种眼中有特殊蛋白质，使它们能看见磁场，从而帮助保持航线。候鸟通过传播种子与控制害虫在生态系统中起关键作用，因此其衰退可导致整个食物网失衡。当然，数百甚至数千英里的迁徙充满风险。明显危险包括恶劣天气、捕食者，以及精疲力竭与饥饿风险。不那么明显的是，人类活动也对候鸟构成重大威胁。栖息地破坏、污染与气候变化已导致许多候鸟种群下降。夜间，光污染可使靠星辰导航的鸟迷失方向，导致迷路或撞上建筑。保护关键栖息地、减少光污染是有助守护候鸟的若干步骤。解决办法包括对鸟友好的建筑设计，以及在迁徙高峰季节鼓励关闭不必要灯光的项目。

versions.transcript:
Listen to part of a lecture in a history class.
Earlier in class, we talked about the Dutch tulip craze of the early 1600s, a time when tulip bulbs became luxury symbols, prices soared, and fortunes vanished almost overnight. It was one of history's first economic bubbles, fueled by speculation and status. America had its own version in the early 19th century when the country was swept up in the mulberry craze. The idea sounded simple: plant mulberry trees, raise the silkworms that eat their leaves, collect the silk from the worms' cocoons, and rake in the profits. Silk was a prized luxury import, and producing it locally promised enormous wealth. Farmers and investors rushed to buy mulberry saplings. Prices for the young trees soared from pennies to several dollars. Classic bubble behavior. And the speculation wasn't all about money. Silk itself, the idea of silk, carried powerful symbolism: refinement, status, and aspiration. For a brief moment, middle-class Americans imagined silk dresses as attainable, blurring old class distinctions. But reality intervened. Silkworms are delicate, requiring precise care and stable climates. Harsh winters wiped out silkworm populations across the country. Mulberry groves lost their purpose. The trees lost their value. The bubble burst, and by the mid-1840s, folks who'd invested their fortunes in the venture were ruined financially. And the bottom line, I mean, for us today, well...
Just like tulip mania in the Netherlands, the American mulberry craze shows how ambition and hype can outpace ecological and practical limits. This is a cautionary tale for modern-day investment booms.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a science podcast.
If you were to take a walk in the Arctic tundra, you'd be walking over permafrost, a soil layer that has remained frozen for thousands of years. As global temperatures rise, however, the stability of this permafrost is compromised. And this brings something into play that you might not expect: microbes. Now, you might wonder, why do such tiny organisms even matter? It's because when permafrost thaws, dormant microbes activate and decompose organic material, releasing greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane. Okay, so this actually initiates a feedback loop. The emission of gases accelerates warming, and that warming leads to further thawing of permafrost. This kind of cycle is a relatively recent discovery, and it's more influential than previously assumed. To put it into perspective, permafrost holds about double the carbon present in the entire atmosphere. This means that we have to understand microbial activities if we want to forecast future climate trends. To address this issue, researchers use sophisticated models, analyzing a number of elements, including the specific microbial species in these thawing soils. But what are the implications if these feedback loops persist? Well, it could lead to a significant rise in global warming. That's why scientists emphasize the necessity of monitoring permafrost regions and coming up with strategies to mitigate these effects. Change isn't just about ice caps melting dramatically; it also involves invisible, underground processes that hold the potential to tip the scales.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段科学播客的讲座。
若你在北极苔原散步，你走在冻土上——一层冻结了数千年的土壤。然而随着全球气温上升，这层冻土的稳定性受威胁。这把你或许想不到的东西带入：微生物。你也许会想，如此微小的生物为何重要？因为冻土融化时，休眠微生物被激活并分解有机物，释放二氧化碳与甲烷等温室气体。好，这实际上启动一个反馈环。气体排放加速变暖，而变暖导致冻土进一步融化。这类循环是相对新近的发现，其影响比先前假定更大。为有个量级概念：冻土所含碳约为整个大气中碳的两倍。这意味着若要预测未来气候趋势，我们必须理解微生物活动。为应对此问题，研究者使用复杂模型，分析若干要素，包括这些融化土壤中的特定微生物物种。但若这些反馈环持续，含义是什么？可能导致全球变暖显著上升。这就是为何科学家强调监测冻土区域并制定缓解这些影响的策略的必要性。变化不只是冰盖剧烈融化；它还涉及可能改变天平的、看不见的地下过程。

versions.transcript: If you were to take a walk in the Arctic tundra, you'd be walking over permafrost, a soil layer that has remained frozen for thousands of years. As global temperatures rise, however, the stability of this permafrost is compromised. And this brings something into play that you might not expect: microbes. Now, you might wonder, why do such tiny organisms even matter? It's because when permafrost thaws, dormant microbes activate and decompose organic material, releasing greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane. Okay, so this actually initiates a feedback loop. The emission of gases accelerates warming, and that warming leads to further thawing of permafrost. This kind of cycle is a relatively recent discovery, and it's more influential than previously assumed. To put it into perspective, permafrost holds about double the carbon present in the entire atmosphere. This means that we have to understand microbial activities if we want to forecast future climate trends. To address this issue, researchers use sophisticated models, analyzing a number of elements, including the specific microbial species in these thawing soils. But what are the implications if these feedback loops persist? Well, it could lead to a significant rise in atmospheric greenhouse gases, intensifying global warming. That's why scientists emphasize the necessity of monitoring permafrost regions and coming up with strategies to mitigate these effects. Climate change isn't just about ice caps melting dramatically. It also involves invisible underground processes that hold the potential to tip the scales.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in an architecture class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an architecture class. The Eastgate Centre in Harare, Zimbabwe, is a mixed-use complex combining retail spaces and offices. When the architect Mick Pearce was asked to design the building in the early 1990s, he faced a big challenge: how to keep all its shops and offices cool without traditional air conditioning, and do it during an economic crisis. Energy costs were high, and importing advanced air conditioners was impossible. To solve this dilemma, Pearce looked to termite mounds. Termites are insects that live in large colonies. They build big mounds on the ground throughout the African savanna. The mounds are amazing structures. Some rise three meters above ground and extend another one to three meters below the ground. The underground chambers connect to the above-ground chimneys through a maze of tunnels. And this entire system works as natural climate control. Warm air rises and escapes through the top, while cooler air flows in from below. The thick walls of soil and clay absorb heat during the day and release it at night. Termites fine-tune airflow by opening and closing vents, adding or removing soil to enlarge or seal passages. On hot days, they open more vents for cooling. At night, they close them to keep warmth in. Pearce borrowed these ideas. The Eastgate Centre's walls are made from thick materials like concrete and brick, and there's a system of ducts and adjustable louvers throughout the building to mimic those vents. The result? A building that uses far less energy than its conventional counterparts.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段建筑学课的讲座。津巴布韦哈拉雷的东门中心是集零售与办公于一体的综合体。建筑师 Mick Pearce 在一九九〇年代初受邀设计该建筑时面临大挑战：如何在不用传统空调的情况下让所有商铺与办公室保持凉爽，而且还是在经济危机期间。能源成本高，进口先进空调又不可能。为解此困，Pearce 求教于白蚁丘。白蚁是群居昆虫。它们在非洲稀树草原各地地面筑起大丘。蚁丘是惊人结构。有的高出地面三米，地下再延伸一到三米。地下腔室通过隧道迷宫与地面烟囱相连。整套系统起到自然气候控制作用。热空气上升从顶部逸出，较冷空气从下方流入。厚土与黏土墙白天吸热、夜间释放。白蚁通过开闭通风口、加减泥土扩大或封闭通道，微调气流。热天开更多通风口降温。夜间关闭以保暖。Pearce 借用了这些想法。东门中心的墙用混凝土与砖等厚材料，整栋楼有管道与可调百叶系统模仿那些通风口。结果？能耗远低于传统同类建筑的一座楼。

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk on a biology podcast. Picture a creature that is smaller than a mouse, yet as territorial as a lion. It is the Scarlet badis, a freshwater fish about 2 centimeters long. In the wild, it thrives peacefully in slow moving streams of India. Because of its size and attractive coloring, it is popular for aquariums. However, in aquariums, males are more aggressive. They chase and nip at other males if they enter their territory, so it is crucial to include lots of vegetation. Plants act as hiding places and borderlines between male territories. Male Scarlet badis are vivid orangish red with light bluish stripes. When a male is not in a confrontation, his scarlet is less bright and can almost resemble the dull gray female coloring. versions.mediaTitle: Listen to part of a talk in a psychology class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to part of a talk in a psychology class.
Imagine you're a painter. Now, would your passion for painting be driven purely by internal motivation? In other words, would you paint just for the joy of it? What if you're being paid for your paintings? Intuitively, we might assume that an external reward or financial incentive would amplify your motivation. But that's not the case. Paradoxically, the opposite often occurs, a phenomenon known in psychology as the overjustification effect. Intrinsic motivation decreases when external incentives come into play. Let me describe an experiment from the 1970s. Children who naturally gravitated toward drawing with markers were observed. Some children were promised rewards for their drawings. Then, during free time, the group that expected rewards spent significantly less time drawing compared to other kids, suggesting that extrinsic rewards can lower an individual's interest. The underlying mechanism here is a perceived shift in autonomy. So, take an activity that's initially pursued just for the fun of it. Introduce an external reward, and individuals feel their actions are no longer self-driven, but driven by the reward itself. The activity feels more like an obligation than a passion. And you can imagine implications across various fields: education, business...
where encouraging intrinsic motivation is crucial. Students or employees who are rewarded for activities they already enjoy could lose their natural enthusiasm over time. Understanding the overjustification effect can help us when we're creating settings intended to nurture, not suppress, intrinsic motivation.

请听一段心理学课讲座的节选。

transcriptSentences.textZh: 然后，在自由活动时间，那些期望获得奖励的孩子比其他孩子花在绘画上的时间显著减少，这表明外在奖励会降低个人的兴趣。

transcriptSentences.text: The underlying mechanism here is a perceived shift in autonomy.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这里潜在的机制是自主性感知上的转变。

transcriptSentences.text: So take an activity that's initially pursued just for the fun of it.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 所以，假设一项活动最初只是为了好玩而进行的。

transcriptSentences.text: Introduce an external reward, and individuals feel their actions are no longer self driven but driven by the reward itself.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 引入外部奖励后，个体就会觉得他们的行为不再是自我驱动的，而是由奖励本身驱动的。

transcriptSentences.text: The activity feels more like an obligation than a passion.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这项活动感觉更像是一种义务，而不是一种热情。

transcriptSentences.text: And you can imagine implications across various fields, education and business, where encouraging intrinsic motivation is crucial.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 你可以想象这在教育和商业等各个领域都有影响，在这些领域中，鼓励内在动机至关重要。

transcriptSentences.text: Students or employees who are rewarded for activities they already enjoy could lose their natural enthusiasm over time.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 学生或员工如果因为他们已经喜欢的活动而获得奖励，可能会随着时间的推移失去他们天生的热情。

transcriptSentences.text: Understanding the overjustification effect can help us when we're creating settings intended to nurture, not suppress, intrinsic motivation.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 理解过度理由效应可以帮助我们在创建旨在培养而非抑制内在动机的环境时。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a physics podcast.
Have you ever wondered why ice floats on water? It's a curious phenomenon that has puzzled scientists for centuries. Normally, solids are denser than liquids because their molecules are packed more closely together. But water has a unique molecular structure and it behaves differently. As water molecules cool and form ice, they arrange themselves in a crystalline structure that occupies more space than when they are in liquid form. This arrangement causes ice to be less dense than liquid water, enabling it to float. But why is this important beyond just curiosity? Well, imagine a world where ice sank. Lakes and ponds would freeze from the bottom up, and this could have a huge impact on aquatic ecosystems. Aquatic life relies on ice forming at the surface, which creates an insulating layer that prevents the entire body of water from freezing. This insulation is vital for the survival of fish and other animals during harsh winters. Even if the top layer is frozen, they can survive in the water underneath. Floating ice, especially in polar regions, also reflects a significant amount of sunlight back into space. This helps regulate global temperatures. If ice sank, it wouldn't remain on the surface to reflect sunlight. It'd disappear beneath the water, allowing more solar energy to be absorbed by the darker ocean or lake surfaces. This would lead to warmer water temperatures, accelerating global warming and disrupting climate patterns worldwide.
versions.transcriptZh:
请听一段物理播客的讲座。
你是否想过为何冰浮在水上？这是困扰科学家数世纪的奇特现象。通常固体比液体密度大，因为分子堆得更紧。但水有独特分子结构，表现不同。当水分子冷却并形成冰时，它们排列成比液态时占据更多空间的晶体结构。这种排列使冰密度小于液态水，从而能浮起。但除了好奇之外这为何重要？想象一个冰会下沉的世界。湖泊与池塘会从底部向上结冰，这可能对水生生态系统产生巨大影响。水生生命依赖冰在表面形成，从而创造防止整片水体结冰的绝缘层。这种绝缘对鱼和其他动物在严冬中存活至关重要。即便表层结冰，它们仍可在下方水中存活。浮冰，尤其在极地，也把大量阳光反射回太空。这有助调节全球温度。若冰下沉，它不会留在表面反射阳光。它会消失在水下，让更多太阳能被较暗的海洋或湖面吸收。这将导致水温升高，加速全球变暖并扰乱全球气候模式。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a psychology class.

Man: Positive reinforcement is a powerful concept in psychology and behavior training. It means giving a reward after someone performs an action you want them to do again. The basic idea is that when a behavior leads to a positive outcome, it's more likely to be repeated. In other words, we tend to repeat actions that bring us something positive. This principle applies to both humans and animals, but the way it works can differ. Animals need to receive rewards immediately after the desired behavior. For example, if a dog sits and gets a treat right away, it learns that sitting leads to something good. If the reward comes too late, the connection is lost. Humans, however, can understand delayed rewards. They might work hard today because they're aiming for a future goal, like earning a degree. Or they might feel motivated by praise even if the reward isn't tangible or instant. But rewards must be used carefully. If a parent gives a child candy to stop whining, the child may learn that whining gets rewarded. It's like watering weeds instead of flowers. You're encouraging the wrong behavior. And if rewards are given too frequently, they can reduce a person's internal motivation, making them rely more on external incentives to take action. So while positive reinforcement is effective, it works best when applied thoughtfully and with clear intent.

请听一段心理学课的讲座。

男：正强化是心理学与行为训练中有力的概念。意思是在某人做出你希望他再做的动作之后给予奖励。基本想法是：行为带来积极结果时，更可能被重复。换句话说，我们倾向重复能带来积极事物的动作。这一原则适用于人类与动物，但作用方式可能不同。动物需要在目标行为后立刻得到奖励。例如狗坐下马上得到零食，就学会坐下带来好事。奖励太晚会失去联结。人类却能理解延迟奖励。他们可能今天努力是为了未来目标，比如拿学位。也可能被表扬激励，即便奖励不具体或不即时。但奖励必须谨慎使用。若父母给孩子糖果让其停止哭闹，孩子可能学会哭闹会得奖。就像给杂草浇水而不是花。你在鼓励错误行为。奖励给得太频繁，还会削弱内在动机，使人更依赖外部激励才行动。因此正强化虽有效，最好经深思熟虑、意图明确地使用。

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a health podcast.

Woman: Today we're going to talk about the importance of sleep for cognitive function. Sleep is crucial for maintaining various aspects of brain health. One of the key benefits of sleep is the consolidation of memory. During sleep, particularly during the deep sleep stages, the brain processes and stores information acquired during the day, making it easier to recall later. During deep sleep, the brain also undergoes a process that flushes out neurotoxins like beta amyloid, which are linked to Alzheimer's disease. Sleep helps in learning new skills and knowledge by strengthening neural connections, and it allows the brain to enhance problem solving abilities by reorganizing information. Studies have shown that sleep deprivation affects cognitive functions like attention and decision making. Another crucial aspect of sleep is its role in emotional regulation. During sleep, the brain can process emotional experiences, which helps maintain emotional stability. REM sleep in particular plays a key role in recalibrating the brain's emotional circuits, helping people better manage fear and anxiety responses. People who do not get enough sleep are more likely to experience mood swings, anxiety, and depression. Despite the clear benefits of sleep, many people still struggle with getting enough rest. It's essential to prioritize sleep and adopt good sleep hygiene practices such as maintaining a regular sleep schedule, avoiding caffeine and electronic screens before bedtime, and creating a comfortable sleep environment. By doing so, individuals can improve their cognitive function and overall well being.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a sociology podcast.
Social networks are not just digital online platforms. They're fundamental to understanding how people connect and interact. One powerful tool for analyzing these networks is the sociogram. A sociogram is a visual map that charts relationships within a group. It looks a little like a spider's web. Sociograms illustrate who interacts with whom, how frequently, and in what patterns. And by making invisible social structures visible, they reveal dynamics such as influence, isolation, and centrality. Rather than focusing on individual behavior as traditional studies would, sociograms emphasize the web of connections that shape group outcomes. In classrooms, they can identify students who are socially isolated or those who act as bridges between different social groups. In workplaces, sociograms help uncover informal hierarchies and where communication breaks down. In public health, they're used to trace contact patterns and predict how diseases might spread from person to person. Sociograms are valuable in marketing as well, where understanding who influences purchasing decisions can guide advertising strategy. However, sociograms do have limitations. By reducing relationships to lines in a web of interactions, they may overlook the subtleties of human interaction, such as trust, conflict, or emotional intensity that aren't easily captured in a diagram. Understanding these qualitative aspects often requires complementary methods like interviews or observation to fully appreciate. Still, when used thoughtfully and alongside other tools, sociograms remain a vital resource for visualizing and analyzing social networks. Their strength lies in turning abstract social dynamics into concrete, interpretable visuals, making them indispensable across disciplines.

请听一段社会学播客的讲座。
社交网络不只是数字在线平台。它们对理解人们如何连接与互动至关重要。分析这些网络的一个有力工具是社会关系图。社会关系图是绘制群体内关系的视觉地图。它看起来有点像蜘蛛网。社会关系图说明谁与谁互动、多频繁、以何种模式。通过使不可见的社会结构可见，它们揭示影响、孤立与中心性等动态。与传统研究聚焦个体行为不同，社会关系图强调塑造群体结果的连接网。在教室中，它们可识别社交孤立的学生或充当不同社交群体桥梁的人。在工作场所，社会关系图帮助揭示非正式层级以及沟通在哪里断裂。在公共卫生中，它们用于追踪接触模式并预测疾病如何人际传播。社会关系图在营销中也有价值，理解谁影响购买决定可指导广告策略。然而社会关系图也有局限。通过把关系简化为互动网中的线条，它们可能忽略人际互动的细微处，如信任、冲突或不易在图中捕捉的情绪强度。理解这些定性方面常需要访谈或观察等互补方法才能充分把握。不过，当被审慎使用并与其他工具并用时，社会关系图仍是可视化与分析社交网络的关键资源。其力量在于把抽象社会动态变成具体、可解读的视觉，使它们在各学科中不可或缺。

Listen to part of a talk on a science podcast.
Have you ever experienced a sudden change in mood after you eat a meal? It's plausible that your gut microbiome played a role in that emotional shift. 

Okay, so the microbiome is an intricate network of bacteria, fungi, and various other microorganisms. Trillions of these tiny entities make up your microbiome. In recent years, our understanding of the microbiome has greatly expanded. We used to think of microbes primarily as pathogens, but we now recognize that microbes play an essential role in our health.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a geography class.

Woman: Urbanization is frequently associated with negative outcomes: pollution, overcrowding, and especially traffic congestion. In many cities, poor planning has led to increased noise and emissions as well as reduced quality of life. However, urbanization doesn't have to be this way. If approached thoughtfully, an alternative to traffic jams and congested city streets is to foster sustainable transportation. Copenhagen in Denmark, for instance, has made bicycles a central part of its urban design. The city's extensive network of protected bike lanes and pro cycling policies have encouraged residents to choose bicycles over cars. In addition to lowering automobile emissions, this shift has also improved public health and reduced traffic related stress. Also, when kept in control and planned properly, urbanization, in this case compact urban living, minimizes land use and energy consumption. Compared to sprawling suburban development, suburban neighborhoods require large plots of land for individual homes, roads and parking. When housing, services and infrastructure are concentrated, this can actually preserve surrounding natural areas and agricultural lands. So, even though this may seem strange, urban growth is actually more compatible with environmental conservation. Urbanization also, by necessity, has led to some innovative thinking, especially concerning the efficient use of land and space. Many cities are incorporating such innovation in food production by creating rooftop farms and using vertical agriculture, which grows crops in stacked vertical layers. In particular, Singapore has invested in high tech urban farming systems that grow vegetables in controlled environments, helping increase local food supply and reduce dependence on imports.

versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in an art history class. Expressionism is an influential modernist art movement that emerged in the early 20th century. This movement is characterized by its focus on representing emotional experience rather than physical reality. Expressionist artists aim to convey their inner feelings and perceptions through distorted and exaggerated forms, vivid colors, and bold brushstrokes. One of the most famous Expressionist artists is Edvard Munch. His painting The Scream shows an agonized person crying out. It eventually became an icon of the movement's focus on intense personal experience. Expressionism was not limited to visual arts, however. It also influenced literature, theater and cinematic arts. In literature, authors like Franz Kafka explored themes of alienation and existential angst. Expressionist theater often used dramatic lighting and intense performances to evoke emotional responses. Sets sometimes featured oversized symbolic objects. In Elmer Rice's 1923 play The Adding Machine, a giant adding machine represents the dehumanizing forces of technology. Similarly, German Expressionist film used innovative techniques. Despite its impact, Expressionism faced criticism for departure from traditional aesthetics and emphasis on the personal. Critics argued that its focus on subjective emotion robbed works of broader content or meaning. Nonetheless, Expressionism paved the way for later movements such as Surrealism.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
Researchers are studying how sensory experiences can affect human behavior, like the use of ambient scent. Ambient scent is the strategic use of a certain fragrance, smell, in a space to set a specific mood, for example, or to cause people to associate a scent with a particular brand. Like a hotel chain, and each hotel's lobby smells like, say, pine trees. Customers experience that ambient scent every time they enter one of these hotels, and it can increase their loyalty to that hotel chain. One experiment involved participants in a room that smelled like freshly baked cookies, while others were in a scentless environment. Those who had the pleasant aroma around them were significantly more likely to volunteer for a charitable cause later. It's as if the warm and inviting scent triggered a sense of goodwill and community feeling in these participants. Why does this happen? Well, scents stimulate our limbic system. The limbic system is the part of the brain that's responsible for emotions and memory. So, fragrances can really make our brains connect with our emotional state and access our memories. When we encounter a comforting smell, like fresh bread, it might remind us of home or childhood, nudging us toward kindness and cooperation. The implications of this are intriguing, especially in marketing or organizational behavior. Imagine using lavender, which has a calming effect, in a high-pressure work environment. Something as simple as smell can have a profound effect on actions and decisions.

versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk on a history podcast.
The Western Roman Empire, which flourished for about the first five centuries of the first millennium, is often celebrated for its engineering marvels. But one of its lesser-known achievements is its contribution to urban planning. Roman towns were laid out with remarkable precision, often following a grid system which was quite advanced for its time. Streets intersected at right angles, dividing the city into organized blocks that made navigation easier and promoted efficient trade, communication, and administration. At the heart of every Roman city was the forum, a multi-functional space that served as the civic, commercial, and social hub. It was the heart of public life, where citizens gathered for various activities ranging from political discussions to socializing. Surrounding it were carefully zoned areas: residential quarters, marketplaces, temples, and public buildings, each with a designated place in the urban fabric. This early form of zoning helped maintain order and efficiency. Romans also prioritized infrastructure. Roads were paved and well-drained, and public amenities like baths, latrines, and fountains were strategically placed to serve dense populations. Their cities were designed not just for grandeur but for functionality, though that balance wasn't always perfect. In poorer districts, overcrowded housing led to sanitation problems and fire hazards, revealing the limits of even the most advanced planning. Still, Roman urban design laid the groundwork for modern city planning. Concepts like grid layouts, centralized public spaces, and functional zoning trace their roots to these ancient innovations. The legacy of Roman urbanism lives on in many cities today.

西罗马帝国在公元第一个千年的大约前五个世纪繁荣，常因其工程奇迹而受到称颂。但其较少为人知的成就之一，是对城市规划的贡献。罗马城镇布局极为精确，常采用在当时相当先进的网格系统。街道直角相交，把城市分成有序街区，使通行更容易，并促进高效的贸易、通信与行政。每座罗马城市的中心是广场，一个多功能空间，充当公民、商业与社交枢纽。它是公共生活的心脏，公民在此聚集，从事从政治讨论到社交等各类活动。其周围是精心分区的区域：住宅区、市场、神庙与公共建筑，各在城市肌理中有指定位置。这种早期分区有助维持秩序与效率。罗马人也重视基础设施。道路铺装且排水良好，浴场、公厕与喷泉等公共设施战略性地布置，以服务密集人口。他们的城市设计不只为宏伟，也为实用，尽管这种平衡并不总是完美。在较穷街区，过度拥挤的住房导致卫生问题与火灾隐患，揭示即便最先进规划也有局限。尽管如此，罗马城市设计为现代城市规划奠定了基础。网格布局、集中公共空间与功能分区等概念，其根源可追溯到这些古代创新。罗马城市主义的遗产仍活在许多今日城市中。

transcriptSentences.text: At the heart of every Roman city was the forum, a multi-functional space that served as the civic, commercial, and social hub.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 每座罗马城市的中心是广场，一个多功能空间，充当公民、商业与社交枢纽。

transcriptSentences.text: It was the heart of public life, where citizens gathered for various activities ranging from political discussions to socializing.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它是公共生活的心脏，公民在此聚集，从事从政治讨论到社交等各类活动。

transcriptSentences.text: Surrounding it were carefully zoned areas: residential quarters, marketplaces, temples, and public buildings, each with a designated place in the urban fabric.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 其周围是精心分区的区域：住宅区、市场、神庙与公共建筑，各在城市肌理中有指定位置。

transcriptSentences.text: This early form of zoning helped maintain order and efficiency.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这种早期分区有助维持秩序与效率。

transcriptSentences.text: Romans also prioritized infrastructure.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 罗马人也重视基础设施。

transcriptSentences.text: Roads were paved and well-drained, and public amenities like baths, latrines, and fountains were strategically placed to serve dense populations.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 道路铺装且排水良好，浴场、公厕与喷泉等公共设施战略性地布置，以服务密集人口。

transcriptSentences.text: Their cities were designed not just for grandeur but for functionality, though that balance wasn't always perfect.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 他们的城市设计不只为宏伟，也为实用，尽管这种平衡并不总是完美。

transcriptSentences.text: In poorer districts, overcrowded housing led to sanitation problems and fire hazards, revealing the limits of even the most advanced planning.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 在较穷街区，过度拥挤的住房导致卫生问题与火灾隐患，揭示即便最先进规划也有局限。

transcriptSentences.text: Still, Roman urban design laid the groundwork for modern city planning.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 尽管如此，罗马城市设计为现代城市规划奠定了基础。

transcriptSentences.text: Concepts like grid layouts, centralized public spaces, and functional zoning trace their roots to these ancient innovations.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 网格布局、集中公共空间与功能分区等概念，其根源可追溯到这些古代创新。

transcriptSentences.text: The legacy of Roman urbanism lives on in many cities today.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 罗马城市主义的遗产仍活在许多今日城市中。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a podcast about political science.
versions.transcript: Listen to a podcast about political science. Soft power refers to a country's ability to influence others through attraction, culture, and collaboration. The term was introduced by political scientist Joseph Nye in 1990. He noticed that some countries gain support not by using force or money, but by being admired and respected. What Nye contributed wasn't just a name. He offered a clear framework for understanding this kind of influence. He explained that power works in three ways: by forcing others, by paying them, or by attracting them. That third kind, attraction, is what he called soft power. A modern example is South Korea's cultural wave, which has sparked global interest in Korean pop music, language, and food. This kind of appeal fits directly into Nye's idea of attraction. Now, soft power takes time because it's built on trust, reputation, and emotional connection. It spreads through cultural events, learning opportunities, and other shared experiences, things that grow gradually but once established, it tends to last, often shaping how future generations view a country.

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a literature class.
versions.transcript: Listen to a talk in a literature class. A common theme in literature is isolation. Isolation can be a powerful motif, reflecting the psychological effects of being separated from society. One classic example is Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, where the creature experiences profound isolation due to his monstrous appearance and the fear he instills in people. This isolation leads to anger and a desire for revenge. Another example is The Catcher in the Rye, whose protagonist Holden Caulfield feels disconnected from the world. Another example that ends badly is Moby Dick. Captain Ahab's obsessive, vengeful quest for the white whale leads to his isolation and propels him and his ship toward a destructive end. However, isolation is not always negative. In Jane Eyre, Jane experiences isolation at various points, but she is resilient in the face of isolation, becoming strong and independent.
versions.transcriptZh: 请听一段文学课的讲座。文学中常见主题是孤立。孤立可以是有力母题，反映与社会隔绝的心理效应。经典例子之一是玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》，其中造物因丑陋外表与在人们心中引发的恐惧而经历深刻孤立。这种孤立导致愤怒与复仇欲望。另一例子是《麦田里的守望者》，主人公霍尔顿·考尔菲德感到与世界脱节。结局糟糕的另一例子是《白鲸》。亚哈船长对白鲸偏执复仇的追逐导致他孤立，并把他与船推向毁灭结局。然而孤立并不总是负面的。在《简·爱》中，简在多个时刻经历孤立，但她面对孤立坚韧，变得坚强独立。

versions.mediaTitle: Listen to a talk in a physics class.
versions.transcript:
Listen to a talk in a physics class.
Imagine a time when the only lights available were flickering candles or oil lamps. Now fast forward to today, where life is illuminated by the glow of energy-efficient LED lights. So what makes these tiny light-emitting diodes so revolutionary? Well, the first practical visible spectrum LED was developed in 1962. It was a breakthrough that altered the landscape of lighting technology and set us on a path toward reduced energy consumption. LEDs, uh, that's short for light-emitting diodes, are a type of solid-state lighting. They use a semiconductor to convert electricity directly into light. Unlike traditional incandescent bulbs, which waste a lot of energy as heat, LEDs are incredibly efficient. That's their biggest benefit. They use about 75% less energy than incandescent bulbs and last 25 times longer. So that lowers electricity bills and also significantly reduces the carbon footprint. But the impact of LEDs goes beyond energy savings. They've enabled new lighting designs that were previously unimaginable. That's because of their small size, which allows LEDs to be integrated into flexible strips, smart bulbs, and even clothing. So virtually endless possibilities in architecture, art, and everyday consumer products. And they're still developing. With ongoing research, we could see such intriguing possibilities as LEDs that purify the air, improve your mood through human-centric lighting, or even transmit data in a system known as Li-Fi, a kind of wireless communication using light from LEDs.

想象只有摇曳烛火或油灯照明的时代。再快进到今天，生活被节能 LED 灯的光芒照亮。那这些微小的发光二极管为何如此革命性？实用的可见光光谱 LED 于一九六二年开发。这一突破改变了照明技术格局，把我们带上降低能耗之路。LED，呃，是发光二极管的缩写，是一种固态照明。它们用半导体把电直接转化为光。与把大量能量浪费为热的传统白炽灯不同，LED 极其高效。这是其最大益处。它们比白炽灯少用约百分之七十五的能量，寿命长二十五倍。因此降低电费，也显著减少碳足迹。但 LED 的影响超出节能。它们使以前难以想象的新照明设计成为可能。那是因为体积小，使 LED 可集成到柔性灯带、智能灯泡甚至服装中。因此在建筑、艺术与日常消费品中几乎有无限可能。它们仍在发展。随着持续研究，我们可能看到诸如净化空气的 LED、通过以人为本的照明改善情绪，甚至在称为 Li-Fi 的系统中传输数据——一种用 LED 光的无线通信——等诱人可能。

transcriptSentences.speaker: Narrator
transcriptSentences.text: Listen to a talk in a physics class.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 请听一段物理课的讲座。

transcriptSentences.text: Imagine a time when the only lights available were flickering candles or oil lamps.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 想象只有摇曳烛火或油灯照明的时代。

transcriptSentences.text: Now fast forward to today, where life is illuminated by the glow of energy-efficient LED lights.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 再快进到今天，生活被节能 LED 灯的光芒照亮。

transcriptSentences.text: So what makes these tiny light-emitting diodes so revolutionary?
transcriptSentences.textZh: 那这些微小的发光二极管为何如此革命性？

transcriptSentences.text: Well, the first practical visible spectrum LED was developed in 1962.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 实用的可见光光谱 LED 于一九六二年开发。

transcriptSentences.text: It was a breakthrough that altered the landscape of lighting technology and set us on a path toward reduced energy consumption.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这一突破改变了照明技术格局，把我们带上降低能耗之路。

transcriptSentences.text: LEDs, uh, that's short for light-emitting diodes, are a type of solid-state lighting.
transcriptSentences.textZh: LED，呃，是发光二极管的缩写，是一种固态照明。

transcriptSentences.text: They use a semiconductor to convert electricity directly into light.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们用半导体把电直接转化为光。

transcriptSentences.text: Unlike traditional incandescent bulbs, which waste a lot of energy as heat, LEDs are incredibly efficient.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 与把大量能量浪费为热的传统白炽灯不同，LED 极其高效。

transcriptSentences.text: That's their biggest benefit.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这是其最大益处。

transcriptSentences.text: They use about 75% less energy than incandescent bulbs and last 25 times longer.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们比白炽灯少用约百分之七十五的能量，寿命长二十五倍。

transcriptSentences.text: So that lowers electricity bills and also significantly reduces the carbon footprint.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 因此降低电费，也显著减少碳足迹。

transcriptSentences.text: But the impact of LEDs goes beyond energy savings.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但 LED 的影响超出节能。

transcriptSentences.text: They've enabled new lighting designs that were previously unimaginable.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们使以前难以想象的新照明设计成为可能。

transcriptSentences.text: That's because of their small size, which allows LEDs to be integrated into flexible strips, smart bulbs, and even clothing.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 那是因为体积小，使 LED 可集成到柔性灯带、智能灯泡甚至服装中。

transcriptSentences.text: So virtually endless possibilities in architecture, art, and everyday consumer products.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 因此在建筑、艺术与日常消费品中几乎有无限可能。

transcriptSentences.text: And they're still developing.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们仍在发展。

transcriptSentences.text: With ongoing research, we could see such intriguing possibilities as LEDs that purify the air, improve your mood through human-centric lighting, or even transmit data in a system known as Li-Fi, a kind of wireless communication using light from LEDs.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 随着持续研究，我们可能看到诸如净化空气的 LED、通过以人为本的照明改善情绪，甚至在称为 Li-Fi 的系统中传输数据——一种用 LED 光的无线通信——等诱人可能。
