versions.label: Koala 09-05
versions.transcript: Archaeologists can learn a great deal from pottery, stone tools, and buildings because those materials may survive for thousands of years. But agriculture presents a special problem. Most plants decay. So if we want to know exactly what ancient people planted in a field or garden, the evidence may seem to have disappeared. One technique helps researchers recover some of that missing information. When a root or other plant material decays underground, it can sometimes leave an empty space in the soil. Archaeologists can carefully inject liquid plaster into one of these cavities. After the plaster hardens, they remove the surrounding soil. What remains is a cast - a three dimensional copy of the space once occupied by the decayed root or plant material. The purpose isn't to strengthen the soil or protect surviving roots. The cast preserves the shape and position of material that is no longer there. When many casts are mapped together, researchers can sometimes reconstruct planting rows, spacing patterns, and even the kinds of agricultural systems used by ancient communities. This has been useful in studying agriculture in different parts of the world. In some Maya communities in Central America, for example, farmers grew several crops together rather than planting a field with only one species. Maize could provide a tall structure for climbing beans. Beans could contribute nutrients to the soil, and squash could spread across the ground, helping retain moisture and limit weeds. The important feature was that different crops supported one another. Archaeologists have also applied similar methods to gardens associated with ancient Roman settlements. Roman gardens were not always divided neatly into beautiful areas and useful areas. A single garden might contain roses and other decorative flowers together with herbs, fruit trees, vegetables, or vines. That combination tells us something about Roman garden design. Gardeners clearly cared about appearance, but they also valued practical uses such as food, medicine, shade, and fragrance. So a garden could be attractive and productive at the same time. Techniques such as soil casting are valuable because they let archaeologists study activities that usually leave little visible evidence. A space that looks like ordinary soil today may preserve a surprisingly detailed record of how people organized and used plants centuries or even thousands of years ago.
versions.transcriptZh: 考古学家可以从陶器、石器和建筑中了解很多，因为这些材料可以保存数千年。 但农业却带来了一个特殊的问题。 大多数植物都会腐烂。 所以，如果我们想确切地知道古代人在田地或花园里种植了什么，证据可能似乎已经消失了。 有一种技术可以帮助研究人员找回一些缺失的信息。 当根或其他植物材料在地下腐烂时，有时会在土壤中留下一个空隙。 考古学家可以小心地将液态石膏注入其中一个空腔。 石膏硬化后，他们会移除周围的土壤。 剩下的是一个铸模——一个曾经被腐烂的根或植物材料占据的空间的三维复制品。 其目的不是为了加固土壤或保护存活的根系。 这个铸模保留了已经不存在的材料的形状和位置。 当许多铸模被绘制在一起时，研究人员有时可以重建种植行、间距模式，甚至古代社区使用的农业系统类型。 这在研究世界不同地区的农业方面非常有用。 例如，在中美洲的一些玛雅社区，农民将几种作物一起种植，而不是只种植单一物种。 玉米可以为攀援的豆类提供高大的结构。 豆类可以为土壤提供养分，南瓜可以蔓延到地面，帮助保持水分并限制杂草。 重要的特点是不同的作物相互支持。 考古学家还将类似的方法应用于与古罗马定居点相关的花园。 罗马花园并非总是整齐地分为美观区和实用区。 一个花园可能同时包含玫瑰和其他观赏花卉，以及草药、果树、蔬菜或藤蔓。 这种组合告诉我们一些关于罗马花园设计的信息。 园艺师显然很注重外观，但他们也重视实用价值，如食物、医药、遮荫和芬芳。 因此，一个花园可以同时兼具美观和生产力。 土壤铸模等技术之所以有价值，是因为它们让考古学家能够研究通常留下很少可见证据的活动。 今天看起来像普通土壤的空间，可能保存着令人惊讶的详细记录，记录着数百甚至数千年前人们如何组织和使用植物。

versions.label: Koala 09-02
versions.transcript: When you think of an animal flying over the ocean, a squid probably isn't the first thing that comes to mind. But several species of squid can actually leave the water and travel through the air for short distances. Flying squirrels don't truly fly. They climb to a high point and then glide downward using a membrane of skin between their legs. Flying squid are different because they can actually propel themselves upward from the water. Like other squid, they move underwater by taking water into their bodies and forcing it out through a tube called a siphon. When they approach the surface at high speed, that jet of water can launch them into the air. Once airborne, the squid spreads its fins and extends its arms and tentacles. Thin membranes between the arms and tentacles form a broad surface that functions somewhat like wings and helps stabilize the animal in the air. Some squid can travel many meters before returning to the water. Scientists aren't completely certain why squid do this. Escaping predators is one possible explanation. But researchers have also observed this behavior in groups of squid traveling together. Many flying squid make seasonal migrations, moving between different feeding and breeding areas at particular times of year. So their aerial behavior may be connected not only with avoiding predators but also with movement over long migration routes. Whatever the reason, it's a remarkable example of an animal using a form of movement we normally don't associate with life in the ocean.
versions.transcriptZh: 当你想到一种在海洋上空飞行的动物时，鱿鱼可能不是你首先想到的。 但有几种鱿鱼实际上可以离开水面，在空中短距离飞行。 飞鼠并不是真正意义上的飞行。 它们爬到高处，然后利用腿之间的皮肤薄膜滑翔而下。 飞鱿鱼则不同，因为它们实际上可以从水中向上推进自己。 像其他鱿鱼一样，它们通过将水吸入体内并通过一个叫做虹吸管的管子将其喷出来在水下移动。 当它们高速接近水面时，那股水流可以将它们发射到空中。 一旦飞到空中，鱿鱼就会展开鱼鳍，伸展手臂和触手。 手臂和触手之间的薄膜形成一个宽阔的表面，其功能有点像翅膀，有助于稳定动物在空中的姿态。 有些鱿鱼能在空中移动许多米，然后才回到水中。 科学家们并不完全确定鱿鱼为什么会这样做。 逃避捕食者是一种可能的解释。 但研究人员也观察到成群结队的鱿鱼一起迁徙时有这种行为。 许多飞鱿鱼会进行季节性迁徙，在一年中的特定时间在不同的觅食区和繁殖区之间移动。 因此，它们的空中行为可能不仅与躲避捕食者有关，还与长距离迁徙路线上的移动有关。 无论原因如何，这都是一个了不起的例子，说明了一种动物使用我们通常不与海洋生物联系在一起的运动方式。

versions.label: Koala 06-02
versions.transcript: When you think of nineteenth century inventors, maybe you think of an inventor alone in his laboratory, tinkering with devices no one else had dreamed of. Actually, there were often multiple people working on similar inventions at once. They improved on each other's work, competed, or collaborated. Louis Latimer invented one kind of early air conditioner and improved toilet systems in trains, but as a Black man he was excluded from many opportunities that his white peers enjoyed in the United States. He never attended high school, but taught himself drafting, making technical drawings. Latimer's drawings were so skillful they were practically works of art. He wrote poetry, and his poetic sensibility can be seen in his drafting work. Later, working with Hiram Maxim, Latimer developed and patented a major innovation in carbon filaments, the thin wires inside light bulbs that glow with electricity. Latimer made these filaments stronger, longer lasting, and easier to make, a major step in making lighting feasible and affordable for the general public.
versions.transcriptZh: 当你想到19世纪的那些发明家时，也许你会认为他们是独自在实验室里，摆弄着别人从未梦想过的装置。 实际上，当时经常有多人同时在研究相似的发明。 他们在彼此工作的基础上进行改进，相互竞争，或者进行合作。 路易斯·拉蒂默发明了一种早期的空调，并改进了火车上的厕所系统，但作为一名黑人，他在美国被排斥在许多白人同龄人所享有的机会之外。 他从未上过高中，但自学了制图，也就是制作技术图纸。 拉蒂默的图纸画得非常精湛，简直就是艺术品。 他写诗，他的诗意感知力可以在他的制图工作中看出来。 后来，在与海勒姆·马克沁合作期间，拉蒂默在碳丝方面取得了一项重大创新并申请了专利，碳丝就是灯泡内通电发光的细线。 拉蒂默使这些碳丝更坚固、更耐用，也更容易制造，这是让公众能够切实且负担得起照明的重大一步。

versions.transcript: Today we're going to look at Cubism, one of the most influential artistic movements of the early twentieth century. Cubism is closely associated with Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque, but its importance goes beyond the work of those two painters. It changed how artists thought about representation itself. For centuries, much European painting had tried to create the illusion of looking through a window. An object was normally shown from one fixed viewpoint, with perspective used to make the space look realistic. Cubist artists questioned that convention. They asked: Why should a painting show an object from only one position when, in real life, we understand an object by moving around it and seeing it from many directions? Imagine a coffee cup sitting on a table. From the side, you see the handle clearly, but the circular opening at the top appears compressed. From above, the opening looks circular, while the handle changes shape. A Cubist artist might combine several of those views in a single image. The cup could be broken into geometric planes and then reorganized so that different sides seem visible at the same time. That's why Cubist paintings can initially look fragmented or distorted. And when Cubism first appeared, not everyone admired it. Some critics thought the paintings looked unfinished, confusing, or even ugly. The rejection of normal perspective seemed to them like a rejection of artistic skill. But Cubism turned out to be enormously influential. It encouraged later artists to think of a painting not simply as a picture of reality but as an independent arrangement of shapes, lines, and surfaces. Its influence spread into sculpture, graphic design, architecture, and other visual fields. This is one reason Cubism is so important to the broader history of Modernism. Modernist artists and designers were experimenting with new forms and questioning inherited traditions. Cubism became one of the clearest demonstrations that even something as basic as visual perspective could be rethought. So the movement mattered not only because Picasso and Braque created unusual paintings. Cubism helped transform expectations about what art could do, and its effects continued long after the first Cubist works stopped shocking the public.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天我们将探讨立体主义，它是二十世纪初最具影响力的艺术运动之一。 立体主义与巴勃罗·毕加索和乔治·布拉克密切相关，但其重要性超越了这两位画家的作品。 它改变了艺术家对再现本身的看法。 几个世纪以来，许多欧洲绘画都试图创造透过窗户看东西的幻觉。 物体通常从一个固定的视角展示，并使用透视法使空间看起来真实。 立体派艺术家质疑了这一传统。 他们问道：为什么一幅画只能从一个角度展示一个物体，而现实生活中，我们通过围绕物体移动并从多个方向观察它来理解它呢？ 想象一个放在桌子上的咖啡杯。 从侧面看，你能清楚地看到把手，但顶部的圆形开口看起来是扁平的。 从上方看，开口是圆形的，而把手则改变了形状。 一位立体派艺术家可能会将这些不同的视角组合在一幅画中。 杯子可以被分解成几何平面，然后重新组织，使不同的侧面似乎同时可见。 这就是为什么立体派绘画最初看起来支离破碎或扭曲的原因。 当立体主义首次出现时，并不是所有人都欣赏它。 一些评论家认为这些画看起来未完成、令人困惑，甚至丑陋。 对正常透视的拒绝在他们看来是对艺术技巧的拒绝。 但立体主义最终产生了巨大的影响。 它鼓励后来的艺术家将绘画不仅仅视为现实的图画，而是形状、线条和表面的独立排列。 它的影响传播到雕塑、平面设计、建筑和其他视觉领域。 这也是立体主义对更广阔的现代主义历史如此重要的原因之一。 现代主义艺术家和设计师正在尝试新的形式并质疑传统。 立体主义成为最清晰的证明之一，即即使是像视觉透视这样基本的东西也可以被重新思考。 所以这项运动之所以重要，不仅仅是因为毕加索和布拉克创作了不同寻常的画作。 立体主义帮助改变了人们对艺术能做什么的期望，它的影响在第一批立体主义作品不再震惊公众之后很久仍在继续。

versions.transcript: Archaeology is not limited to digging on land. Underwater archaeology is a subfield that studies human activity preserved beneath oceans, lakes, rivers, and former harbors. The basic questions are the same ones archaeologists ask on land: Who lived here? What did people make? How did they travel, trade, and organize their societies? But working underwater requires different equipment and preservation methods. One interesting advantage is that waterlogged environments can preserve some materials that usually disappear quickly on dry land. Wood and textiles normally decay because microorganisms break them down. In low oxygen underwater conditions, however, that process can be much slower. So archaeologists may recover ship timbers, rope, baskets, or pieces of cloth that would rarely survive at an ordinary land site. Of course, not every underwater site belongs to only one culture. Consider the region around Ephesus in present day Turkey. Ephesus was occupied and used over long periods by different civilizations, including Greek and Roman communities. Archaeological evidence from the wider site reflects these different periods. That's important because archaeologists are often reconstructing a long sequence of human activity rather than one single moment. Shipwrecks provide especially valuable evidence about trade. A famous example is the Uluburun shipwreck found off the coast of Turkey. The ship carried materials from many regions: copper, tin, glass, pottery, and luxury goods. Some objects came from places separated by very large distances. The shipwreck therefore gave researchers evidence about trade networks in the ancient Mediterranean. It showed that communities were exchanging raw materials and finished goods across extensive routes much earlier and on a larger scale than someone might assume from studying a single settlement. So underwater archaeology is valuable not simply because shipwrecks are dramatic discoveries. It can preserve unusual materials and reveal connections among ancient societies that are difficult to reconstruct from land sites alone.
versions.transcriptZh: 考古学不局限于陆地挖掘。 水下考古学是一个分支领域，研究保存在海洋、湖泊、河流和旧港口下方的人类活动。 基本问题和陆地考古学家问的问题一样：谁住在这里？ 人们制造了什么？ 他们如何旅行、贸易和组织社会？ 但在水下工作需要不同的设备和保存方法。 一个有趣的优点是，水浸环境可以保存一些在陆地上通常很快消失的材料。 木材和纺织品通常会因为微生物分解而腐烂。 然而，在低氧的水下环境中，这个过程会慢得多。 因此，考古学家可能会找到在普通陆地遗址上很少能保存下来的船只木材、绳索、篮子或布料碎片。 当然，并非每个水下遗址都只属于一种文化。 考虑一下今土耳其的以弗所地区。 以弗所曾长期被不同的文明占领和使用，包括希腊和罗马社区。 更广阔遗址的考古证据反映了这些不同的时期。 这很重要，因为考古学家通常是在重建人类活动的一个漫长序列，而不是一个单一的时刻。 沉船为贸易提供了特别有价值的证据。 一个著名的例子是在土耳其海岸附近发现的乌鲁布伦沉船。 这艘船载有来自许多地区的材料：铜、锡、玻璃、陶器和奢侈品。 有些物品来自相距遥远的地方。 因此，这艘沉船为研究人员提供了关于古代地中海贸易网络的证据。 它表明，社区之间通过广阔的路线交换原材料和成品，其时间比人们仅凭研究单一聚居地所能想象的要早得多，规模也大得多。 所以水下考古学的价值不仅仅在于沉船是戏剧性的发现。 它能保存不寻常的材料，揭示仅凭陆地遗址难以重建的古代社会之间的联系。

versions.label: Koala 09-13
versions.transcript: The blue ringed octopus is small, visually striking, and extremely venomous. Its blue rings become especially vivid when the animal feels threatened. But the most important part of its defense system is a powerful neurotoxin called tetrodotoxin, or TTX. Tetrodotoxin is also scientifically interesting because compounds from unusual marine animals sometimes have medical applications. That's one reason researchers compare animals such as the blue ringed octopus with creatures like the horseshoe crab. Horseshoe crab blood contains compounds that have become important in medical testing, while tetrodotoxin has been studied for possible medical uses, including pain related research. To understand the octopus's venom, we need to talk briefly about nerve cells. Nerve cells communicate using electrical signals. Sodium channels in the cell membrane open and allow sodium ions to move across the membrane. That movement is essential for an electrical impulse to travel along the nerve. Tetrodotoxin blocks those sodium channels. So when the toxin enters the body of prey, nerves can no longer transmit normal signals to muscles. The prey may remain conscious for some time, but its muscles become paralyzed. In other words, the animal becomes unable to move, which makes it much easier for the octopus to capture. Now, here's an obvious question. If an animal contains or delivers a powerful toxin, why doesn't the toxin disable the animal itself? This problem appears in other venomous animals too. Some spiders, for example, have changes in the molecular structure of their own nerve channels that make them much less sensitive to components of their venom. Similar protective mechanisms can prevent a venomous animal from poisoning itself. The blue ringed octopus also has biological protection against the toxin associated with its venom system. So venom is not simply a chemical weapon. Its effectiveness depends on the interaction between the toxin, the target's nervous system, and the venomous animal's own mechanisms for avoiding self harm.

versions.label: Koala 07-04
versions.transcript: Today we'll look at a painter whose artistic style changed significantly over the course of her career. She showed talent from a young age, and her parents supported her education by sending her to France to study art. That experience exposed her to museums, teachers, and artistic communities that helped shape her early work. At first, her paintings tended to balance expressiveness with realism. In one work from this early period, the subject is still recognizable, and the scene is presented with attention to real objects and human experience. At the same time, the painting is not merely documentary; it uses color and composition to communicate emotion. Later in her career, however, her work became increasingly abstract. Instead of focusing on realistic representation, she placed greater emphasis on shapes, color relationships, and emotional suggestion. This shift shows how an artist can begin with recognizable subjects and gradually move toward a more personal and abstract visual language.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天我们将关注一位在其职业生涯中艺术风格发生了显著变化的画家。 她从小就展现出天赋，她的父母为了支持她的教育，送她去法国学习艺术。 那段经历让她接触到了博物馆、老师和艺术群体，这些都帮助塑造了她的早期作品。 起初，她的绘画倾向于在表现力与写实主义之间寻找平衡。 在这一早期阶段的一件作品中，主题仍然是可以辨认的，场景的呈现关注真实物体和人类体验。 同时，这幅画不仅仅是纪实性的；它利用色彩和构图来传达情感。 然而，在职业生涯的后期，她的作品变得越来越抽象。 她不再专注于写实表现，而是更加强调形状、色彩关系和情感暗示。 这种转变展示了一位艺术家是如何从可辨认的主题开始，逐渐转向一种更具个人色彩和抽象的视觉语言的。

versions.label: Koala 10-05
versions.transcript: During the early 20th century, technology was advancing rapidly, and music was undergoing a transformation of its own. Electrophones were at the forefront of this evolution. All right, so electrophones. They're the predecessors of today's synthesizers. And electrophones challenged established musical conventions. They create sound using electronic means, a groundbreaking innovation for their time. Take, for example, the theremin. The theremin is an instrument that lets you create melodies through the manipulation of electromagnetic fields. You don't even touch it. There's no direct physical contact with the instrument. The theremin made its mark on the landscape of music, and its tones became synonymous with experimental compositions. Similarly, the ondes Martenot gave musicians a new and expressive range of sounds. You play it by gliding a ring along a wire, kind of like how you move a bow across the strings of a violin. These electrophones, the theremin and the ondes Martenot, set the stage for the synthesizers that dominate today's music. Electrophones enabled composers of the early 20th century to explore new musical ideas. Despite being overshadowed by modern electronics, these early electrophones made an important and lasting mark on music. And they continue to influence music making. Artists are going to keep looking forward in their quest to redefine musical boundaries. But we can also look back to acknowledge the foundational role these early electrophones played in shaping the history of music.

versions.transcript: Isolation appears in many novels, but authors can use it in very different ways. Today I want to look at how isolation is represented through individual characters and how it can shape what those characters become. Let's begin with Mary Shelley's *Frankenstein*. The creature is isolated largely because of his appearance. People react to him with fear before they learn anything about his personality. He wants companionship and initially tries to observe and understand human society, but repeated rejection turns him into an outcast. So in this case, isolation is imposed from the outside. His appearance causes other people to exclude him. Now compare that with Captain Ahab in Herman Melville's *Moby Dick*. Ahab is physically surrounded by a crew, so he isn't isolated in the simple sense of being alone. But his obsession with hunting the white whale increasingly separates him emotionally and psychologically from the people around him. Ahab becomes less willing to listen to other perspectives. His private obsession dominates every decision he makes, and eventually he pulls the whole ship into his destructive pursuit. His isolation therefore has tragic consequences. It doesn't affect only Ahab; it contributes to disaster for nearly everyone around him. Jane Eyre provides another variation. Jane experiences isolation at several points in Charlotte Brontë's novel. As a child, she is excluded within her relatives' household, and later she spends long periods separated from people with whom she feels emotionally connected. But Jane doesn't respond to solitude in the same way as Frankenstein's creature or Ahab. At important moments, being alone gives her space to think through what she believes and what she wants. She develops independence and becomes more confident in making decisions based on her own moral judgment. So isolation is not automatically destructive in literature. It can expose vulnerability, intensify obsession, or encourage self knowledge, depending on the character and the circumstances. When we compare these characters, the useful question isn't simply, Is this person isolated? Instead, ask what caused the isolation, how the character responds to it, and what effect it has on the character's development and choices.
versions.transcriptZh: 孤独出现在许多小说中，但作者可以以截然不同的方式运用它。 今天我想探讨一下，孤独是如何通过个体角色来体现的，以及它是如何塑造这些角色的。 让我们从玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》开始。 这个怪物之所以被孤立，主要是因为他的外貌。 人们在了解他的个性之前，就因为恐惧而对他产生排斥。 他渴望陪伴，最初试图观察和理解人类社会，但反复的拒绝使他成为一个被排斥的人。 因此在这种情况下，孤独是由外部强加的。 他的外貌导致其他人排斥他。 现在，我们把它与赫尔曼·麦尔维尔的《白鲸》中的亚哈船长进行比较。 亚哈身体上被船员包围着，所以他并非简单意义上的独处。 但他对捕猎白鲸的执念，使他与周围的人在情感上和心理上日益疏远。 亚哈变得越来越不愿意听取其他观点。 他的私人执念主宰了他做出的每一个决定，最终他把整艘船都拖入了毁灭性的追逐中。 因此，他的孤独带来了悲剧性的后果。 它不仅影响了亚哈；它导致了几乎所有他周围的人的灾难。 《简·爱》提供了另一种变化。 简在夏洛特·勃朗特的小说中，多次经历孤独。 小时候，她在亲戚家被排斥，后来她长时间与那些她在情感上感到亲近的人分离。 但简对孤独的反应与弗兰肯斯坦的怪物或亚哈不同。 在关键时刻，独处给了她思考自己所信仰和渴望的空间。 她培养了独立性，并更加自信地根据自己的道德判断做出决定。 所以，孤独在文学中并非自动具有破坏性。 它可能暴露脆弱性，加剧执念，或鼓励自我认知，这取决于角色和具体情况。 当我们比较这些角色时，有用的问题不仅仅是，这个人是否被孤立了？ 相反，要问是什么导致了孤独，角色如何回应它，以及它对角色的发展和选择有什么影响。

versions.label: Koala 09-13
versions.transcript: Mimicry is common in nature. An animal may resemble another organism, or part of its environment, in a way that helps it avoid predators or approach prey. Some mimicry is relatively fixed. Consider the owl butterfly. The large circular patterns on its wings resemble the eyes of a much larger animal. The butterfly does not create those patterns when a predator approaches. They are always present. Dynamic mimicry is different. It involves changing appearance or behavior in real time. One of the best examples is the mimic octopus. This animal can rapidly change its color, body pattern, posture, and movement. Depending on the situation, it may flatten its body, stretch out its arms, or arrange itself in ways that resemble other marine animals. That's why the owl butterfly is useful as a comparison. It helps us distinguish a fixed form of mimicry from dynamic mimicry, in which the animal actively changes what a predator sees. Changing shape alone, however, may not be enough. A convincing imitation often requires several signals at once. Shape, color, movement, and posture may all need to work together. If an octopus takes the outline of another animal but keeps the wrong color pattern or moves in the wrong way, a predator may still recognize it. The octopus's rapid color changes depend partly on specialized skin cells called chromatophores. Each chromatophore contains pigment and is controlled by muscles. You can imagine a tiny colored balloon. When the surrounding muscles pull it open, the colored area becomes larger and more visible. When the muscles relax, the area becomes smaller. By expanding and contracting thousands of these pigment cells in coordinated patterns, the octopus can change its appearance remarkably quickly. So dynamic mimicry is not one single trick. It is a coordinated system in which several parts of the animal's body work together to produce a temporary and highly adaptable disguise.

versions.label: Koala 06-02
versions.transcript: Migration involves the regular, often seasonal movement of animals from one region to another, typically in search of food, breeding grounds, or better climates. It is observed in birds, mammals, fish, and insects. Monarch butterflies travel thousands of miles from North America to Central Mexico to escape the cold winter, and the journey involves multiple generations because no single butterfly makes the round trip. Humpback whales travel from polar feeding grounds to tropical breeding areas. Birds like the Arctic tern undertake one of the longest migrations, traveling from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back each year. Animals migrate vast distances with precision, but migration is challenging because of predators, adverse weather, and human made obstacles like buildings and roads. Protecting habitats and reducing human interference can help maintain migration.
versions.transcriptZh: 迁徙涉及动物从一个地区到另一个地区的定期、通常是季节性的移动，通常是为了寻找食物、繁殖地或更好的气候。 在鸟类、哺乳动物、鱼类和昆虫中都能观察到这种现象。 黑脉金斑蝶为了躲避寒冷的冬天，从北美飞往墨西哥中部，航程长达数千英里，这段旅程涉及几代蝴蝶，因为没有一只蝴蝶能独自完成往返。 座头鲸从极地的觅食地游向热带的繁殖区。 北极燕鸥等鸟类进行着最长的迁徙之一，每年往返于北极和南极之间。 虽然动物们能够精准地进行长距离迁徙，但由于掠食者、恶劣天气以及建筑物和道路等人造障碍物，迁徙充满了挑战。 保护栖息地和减少人为干扰有助于维持迁徙。

versions.label: Koala 07-04
versions.transcript: Today we're going to discuss Joseph Campbell's idea of the monomyth, sometimes called the hero's journey. Campbell argued that myths from many parts of the world often follow a similar narrative pattern. In this pattern, a hero is called away from ordinary life into an adventure. The hero faces trials, receives help, confronts a major fear or crisis, and eventually experiences some kind of transformation. At the end of the journey, the hero returns to the community with new wisdom, power, or insight that can benefit others. This pattern appears in many traditional stories and has also influenced modern novels and films. Campbell's theory has been criticized. Some scholars argue that it oversimplifies myths and ignores important cultural differences. Not every culture tells stories in the same way, and forcing all myths into one pattern can hide what makes them unique. Still, the theory has remained influential because it speaks to a common human belief: struggle can lead to growth, and a person who returns from a difficult journey is no longer the same person who began it.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天我们将讨论约瑟夫·坎贝尔的“单一神话”概念，有时也被称为“英雄之旅”。 坎贝尔认为，来自世界许多地区的神话往往遵循类似的叙事模式。 在这种模式中，英雄被从平凡的生活中召唤去参加一场冒险。 英雄面临考验，获得帮助，对抗重大的恐惧或危机，并最终经历某种转变。 在旅程结束时，英雄带着新的智慧、力量或洞察力回到社区，这些都能造福他人。 这种模式出现在许多传统故事中，也影响了现代小说和电影。 坎贝尔的理论也受到过批评。 一些学者认为，该理论过度简化了神话，并忽视了重要的文化差异。 并非每种文化都以相同的方式讲述故事，将所有神话强行纳入一种模式可能会掩盖它们的独特之处。 尽管如此，这一理论仍然具有影响力，因为它触及了一个人类共同的信念：奋斗可以带来成长，而一个从艰难旅程中归来的人，已经不再是出发时的那个人了。

versions.transcript: You know, modern LED light bulbs have really changed the way we light our homes and workplaces. They're extremely energy efficient. But before LEDs took over, incandescent bulbs were the norm for everyday lighting needs. Incandescent bulbs give off a warm, full spectrum glow, including the wavelength called near infrared light, which is invisible to the human eye. Now, LEDs are designed to shine in the visible range, about 400 to 700 nanometers, a relatively narrow band of the spectrum, which is great for saving energy and thus for reducing costs. But by cutting out near infrared from the artificial light we're exposed to, we might be missing out on some subtle, but important health benefits. Research suggests that exposure to near infrared light may support cardiovascular health, reduce stress, and even boost your mood, kind of like the light from a campfire or a bright sunny day. Incandescent bulbs, though less efficient, might offer physiological benefits that LEDs lack. Despite these limitations, LED bulbs remain a positive, popular and practical choice. But the question is, are the downsides worth it? Many experts say no, and they're advocating instead for advanced LED systems that bring near infrared back into the mix. Such systems do exist, but they're pricey, sometimes ten times more than regular LEDs. So, for now at least, they're mostly used in specialized medical settings.

versions.label: Koala 05-27
versions.transcript: You've probably heard of nanotechnology. But just what is it? In technical terms, it is the manipulation of matter at the atomic and molecular scale, typically below 100 nanometers. In more common parlance, it's creating things that are really, really small. Nanotechnology has opened up new possibilities for innovations across various industries. One of its most important applications is in medicine. In that industry, nanotechnology is being used to create more effective drug delivery systems. These systems ensure that medications are released at the right place and time in the body. Another field benefiting from nanotechnology is electronics. There, the technology has led to the production of smaller, faster, and more efficient components of electronic devices. For example, nanomaterials are used to enhance the performance of batteries, making them last longer and charge faster. This feature has significant implications for consumer electronics, electric vehicles, and renewable energy storage. Nanotechnology also holds promise for environmental applications. Nanomaterials can be used to clean up pollutants in water and air more efficiently than traditional methods. This application of the technology can help address some of the most pressing environmental challenges we face today. I should point out, though, that there are potential negative aspects of nanotechnology. Some medical professionals harbor concerns about the potential health and environmental risks associated with nanoparticles. Because they are so small, nanoparticles can easily enter biological systems, and their long term effects are not yet fully understood. This particular aspect of nanotechnology will certainly require much more research going forward.
versions.transcriptZh: 你可能听说过纳米技术。 但它究竟是什么呢？ 从技术层面来说，它是在原子和分子尺度上对物质的操作，通常在100纳米以下。 用更通俗的话说，就是制造非常非常小的东西。 纳米技术为各个行业的创新开辟了新的可能性。 它最重要的应用之一是在医学领域。 在该行业，纳米技术正被用于创建更有效的药物输送系统。 这些系统确保药物在体内的正确部位和时间释放。 另一个受益于纳米技术的领域是电子产品。 在那里，这项技术带动了更小、更快、更高效的电子设备组件的生产。 例如，纳米材料被用来提升电池的性能，使其寿命更长，充电更快。 这一特性对消费电子、电动汽车和可再生能源存储具有重要意义。 纳米技术在环境应用方面也大有可为。 纳米材料可以比传统方法更有效地清除水和空气中的污染物。 这项技术的应用可以帮助解决我们今天面临的一些最紧迫的环境挑战。 不过，我应该指出，纳米技术也存在潜在的负面影响。 一些医学专业人士对纳米颗粒相关的潜在健康和环境风险表示担忧。 由于纳米颗粒非常小，它们很容易进入生物系统，而它们的长期影响尚未被完全了解。 纳米技术的这一特定方面在未来肯定需要更多的研究。

versions.label: Koala 04-26
versions.transcript: Today, I want to talk about the forces that shape our coastlines, specifically the process of coastal erosion. This is the wearing away of land and the removal of beach or dune sediments by wave action, tidal currents, and other natural phenomena. Let's focus on the two main drivers. The first, and most obvious, is wave action. This happens in two ways. First, there's hydraulic action, which is simply the sheer force of the water crashing against the coast, compressing air in cracks and breaking rocks apart. Then there's abrasion, where waves pick up sand and pebbles and hurl them against the cliff face, essentially sandblasting it. Another important factor is longshore drift. This is the process where waves hit the beach at an angle, carrying sediment up the beach, and then the water returns straight back, pulling the sediment with it. This creates a zigzag movement of material along the coast. The intensity of these processes can vary. Think about a storm, for instance. The waves are much more powerful, carrying more energy, and this can cause significant erosion in a very short time. So, the combination of constant wave action and the gradual movement from longshore drift constantly reshapes our shores.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天，我想谈谈塑造我们海岸线的力量，特别是海岸侵蚀的过程。 这是指由于波浪作用、潮汐流和其他自然现象而导致的陆地磨损以及海滩或沙丘沉积物的搬移。 让我们关注两个主要的驱动因素。 第一个也是最明显的一个，就是波浪作用。 这通过两种方式发生。 首先是水力作用，这仅仅是水冲向海岸的纯粹力量，它会压缩裂缝中的空气并使岩石破碎。 然后是磨蚀作用，即波浪卷起沙子和鹅卵石，并将其猛烈地撞击在悬崖峭壁上，实际上起到了喷砂清理的效果。 另一个重要因素是沿岸漂沙。 在这个过程中，波浪以一定角度冲击海滩，将沉积物带向海滩上方，然后海水直接退回，同时带走沉积物。 这在海岸边形成了一种物质的“之”字形移动。 这些过程的强度是会变化的。 例如，想想暴风雨吧。 波浪更加汹涌，携带更多能量，这可能在极短的时间内造成严重的侵蚀。 因此，持续的波浪作用和沿岸漂沙的逐渐移动相结合，不断重塑着我们的海岸。

versions.label: Koala 04-26
versions.transcript: Today, I want to talk about a concept that’s becoming increasingly common: the Internet of Things, or IoT. So, what exactly is it? Simply put, the IoT is a vast network of physical devices from home appliances to industrial sensors that are embedded with software and other technologies to connect and exchange data over the internet. To give you a concrete example, let's look at a smart home. Your thermostat can learn your schedule and adjust the temperature automatically to save energy. Your refrigerator might track your groceries and add milk to your online shopping list when you’re running low. These devices communicate with each other and with you through your smartphone. However, this interconnectedness also presents a significant challenge: security. Every connected device is a potential entry point for a cyberattack. For instance, a hacker could potentially exploit a vulnerability in your smart lightbulb to gain access to your entire home Wi Fi network. As a result, manufacturers are in a constant race to improve security protocols, but consumers also need to be aware of the risks. The convenience of IoT is undeniable, but it comes with a responsibility to manage its security.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天，我想谈谈一个变得越来越普遍的概念：物联网，简称 IoT。 那么，它究竟是什么呢？ 简单来说，物联网是一个庞大的物理设备网络，从家用电器到工业传感器，这些设备都嵌入了软件和其他技术，通过互联网连接并交换数据。 为了给你们一个具体的例子，让我们来看看智能家居。 你的恒温器可以学习你的作息，并自动调节温度以节省能源。 你的冰箱可能会追踪你的食品，并在你库存不足时将牛奶添加到你的网上购物清单中。 这些设备之间以及它们与你之间通过智能手机进行通信。 然而，这种互联性也带来了一个重大的挑战：安全。 每一个联网设备都是网络攻击的潜在切入点。 例如，黑客可能会利用智能灯泡中的漏洞来获取进入你整个家庭 Wi-Fi 网络的权限。 因此，制造商在不断地竞争以改进安全协议，但消费者也需要意识到这些风险。 物联网的便捷性是不可否认的，但它也伴随着管理其安全性的责任。

versions.label: Koala 09-13
versions.transcript: Today I'd like to discuss the American painter Jacob Lawrence, and in particular one work that represents many of the qualities associated with his career: The Migration Series. Lawrence was born in 1917 and became known for paintings that told stories about African American history and everyday life. He often worked in groups of paintings rather than relying on one large canvas. The Migration Series is probably his best known example. Lawrence created it when he was only in his early twenties, which is one reason the achievement is so impressive. The series consists of sixty panels describing the Great Migration, the movement of millions of African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West during the twentieth century. Each panel includes a short caption. The paintings and captions work together almost like pages in a visual history book. Lawrence shows reasons people left the South, including discrimination and limited economic opportunity, and he also shows the challenges and opportunities they encountered after moving north. The series is representative of Lawrence's style. His figures are often simplified into strong shapes, with bold areas of color and repeated visual patterns. The style can look deceptively simple. Lawrence had already shown a strong interest in African American history before The Migration Series. He created earlier groups of paintings about important historical figures. One of those figures was Harriet Tubman, the abolitionist who helped enslaved people escape through the Underground Railroad. Mentioning Tubman helps us see that Lawrence's historical storytelling did not begin with the Great Migration. Not every critic immediately valued Lawrence's simplified style. Some observers treated work that looked less realistic or less technically elaborate as if it were somehow less advanced. But that judgment missed the deliberate organization of Lawrence's compositions and the way he used repetition, shape, and color to connect many individual scenes into a unified story. The Migration Series became a major achievement early in Lawrence's career and remains an important example of how modern painting can combine visual design with social and historical narrative.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天我想和大家讨论一下美国画家雅各布·劳伦斯，尤其是他的一件代表了他职业生涯中许多特质的作品：《大迁徙系列》。 劳伦斯出生于1917年，以描绘非裔美国人历史和日常生活的绘画而闻名。 他经常以系列画作的形式创作，而不是依赖于一张大幅画布。 《大迁徙系列》可能是他最著名的例子。 劳伦斯创作它时年仅二十出头，这也是这项成就如此令人印象深刻的原因之一。 该系列由六十幅画板组成，描绘了“大迁徙”——二十世纪数百万非裔美国人从南部农村迁徙到北部和西部城市的故事。 每幅画板都附有简短的说明文字。 画作和说明文字共同作用，几乎就像一本视觉历史书的页面。 劳伦斯展示了人们离开南方的原因，包括歧视和有限的经济机会，他还展示了他们迁往北方后遇到的挑战和机遇。 这个系列代表了劳伦斯的风格。 他的人物形象通常被简化为强烈的形状，色彩大胆，并带有重复的视觉模式。 这种风格看起来可能出奇地简单。 在《大迁徙系列》之前，劳伦斯就已经对非裔美国人历史表现出浓厚兴趣。 他曾创作过关于重要历史人物的早期系列画作。 其中一位人物是哈里特·塔布曼，这位废奴主义者曾帮助受奴役的人们通过地下铁路逃脱。 提到塔布曼有助于我们看到，劳伦斯的历史叙事并非始于大迁徙。 并非所有评论家都立即认同劳伦斯的简化风格。 一些观察者认为那些看起来不那么写实或技术上不那么精湛的作品，仿佛它们在某种程度上不那么先进。 但这种判断忽略了劳伦斯作品中精心设计的构图，以及他如何运用重复、形状和色彩将许多独立的场景连接成一个统一的故事。 《大迁徙系列》成为劳伦斯职业生涯早期的一项重大成就，至今仍是现代绘画如何将视觉设计与社会和历史叙事结合起来的重要范例。

versions.label: Koala 04-13
versions.transcript: Today I'd like to discuss urban heat islands. Cities often become warmer than surrounding rural areas because pavement, rooftops, and buildings absorb and retain heat during the day, then release it slowly at night. Trees and other vegetation usually cool an area through shade and evaporation, but cities often have less plant cover. Human activity also contributes: vehicles, air conditioners, and industrial equipment all release additional heat. This matters because higher temperatures can increase energy use, worsen air pollution, and create health risks during heat waves. One effective response is to add green roofs and plant more trees, which lower surface temperatures and provide shade. Another is to use lighter colored roofing materials that reflect more sunlight instead of absorbing it. None of these strategies eliminates urban heat entirely, but together they can make cities noticeably cooler and more comfortable.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天我想讨论城市热岛效应。 城市通常比周围的农村地区更温暖，因为路面、屋顶和建筑在白天吸收并保留热量，然后在夜间缓慢释放。 树木和其他植被通常通过遮荫和蒸发来使一个区域降温，但城市往往缺乏植物覆盖。 人类活动也是原因之一：汽车、空调和工业设备都会释放额外的热量。 这一点很重要，因为气温升高会增加能源使用，加剧空气污染，并在热浪期间带来健康风险。 一种有效的应对措施是增加绿色屋顶并种植更多树木，这可以降低地表温度并提供遮荫。 另一种方法是使用浅色的屋顶材料，以反射更多的阳光而不是吸收它。 这些策略都不能完全消除城市热量，但结合起来，它们可以使城市明显变得更凉爽、更舒适。

versions.label: Koala 08-08
versions.transcript: Today we'll examine how the Industrial Revolution reshaped European cities. Before industrialization, many European cities still had features that dated back to the medieval period: narrow streets, defensive walls, and neighborhoods organized around markets, churches, or craft workshops. But industrialization changed both the economy and the physical layout of cities. Factories needed workers, access to transportation, and space for machinery. As a result, populations grew rapidly, and cities expanded beyond their older boundaries. One of the most visible changes was the removal of city walls. Originally, walls had been built for defense, but by the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries they often limited expansion and interfered with transportation. Industrial cities needed rail lines, wider roads, canals, and later streetcar routes. Old walls were frequently demolished so that goods and workers could move more efficiently. The land where walls had stood was sometimes converted into boulevards, parks, or new commercial districts. Industrial workplaces also changed the daily experience of urban life. In earlier craft production, work often took place in small workshops or even in the home. With industrialization, large numbers of workers traveled to factories according to a more rigid schedule. This contributed to the separation of residential, industrial, and commercial areas. Working class housing often developed near factories because workers needed to live close to their jobs, but these neighborhoods could be crowded and polluted. Smoke from factories, waste from production, and poor sanitation created serious public health problems. The street layout of industrial cities changed too. Wider streets and more regular grids were introduced in some places to improve traffic flow and allow carts, carriages, and later public transit to move more easily. These changes had consequences beyond transportation. They encouraged the growth of commercial centers and made it easier for city governments to provide services such as lighting, sewers, and police patrols. So when we study industrial cities, we are not just studying factories. We are studying how economic change altered space, movement, health, and daily life.
versions.transcriptZh: 今天我们将探讨工业革命是如何重塑欧洲城市的。 在工业化之前，许多欧洲城市仍然保留着可以追溯到中世纪的特征：狭窄的街道、防御城墙，以及围绕市场、教堂或手工作坊组织的社区。 但是工业化改变了经济和城市的物理布局。 工厂需要工人、便利的交通以及放置机器的空间。 结果，人口迅速增长，城市扩展到了旧有的边界之外。 最显著的变化之一是拆除城墙。 最初，城墙是为防御而建的，但到了18世纪和19世纪，它们经常限制城市的扩张并妨碍交通。 工业城市需要铁路线、更宽的道路、运河，以及后来的有轨电车路线。 旧城墙经常被拆除，以便货物和工人能够更高效地移动。 城墙曾经矗立的土地有时被改造成林荫大道、公园或新的商业区。 工业工作场所也改变了城市生活的日常体验。 在早期的手工生产中，工作通常在小作坊甚至家里进行。 随着工业化，大量工人按照更严格的时间表前往工厂上班。 这促成了住宅区、工业区和商业区的分离。 工人阶级的住房通常在工厂附近发展，因为工人需要住得离工作地点近，但这些社区可能很拥挤且污染严重。 工厂的烟雾、生产废料和恶劣的卫生条件造成了严重的公共卫生问题。 工业城市的街道布局也发生了变化。 一些地方引入了更宽的街道和更规则的网格布局，以改善交通流量，并使手推车、马车以及后来的公共交通工具能够更顺畅地移动。 这些变化的影响超出了交通领域。 它们鼓励了商业中心的增长，并使市政府更容易提供照明、下水道和警察巡逻等服务。 因此，当我们研究工业城市时，我们不仅仅是在研究工厂。 我们是在研究经济变革如何改变了空间、交通、健康和日常生活。

transcriptSentences.text: Today we'll examine how the Industrial Revolution reshaped European cities.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 今天我们将探讨工业革命是如何重塑欧洲城市的。

transcriptSentences.text: Before industrialization, many European cities still had features that dated back to the medieval period: narrow streets, defensive walls, and neighborhoods organized around markets, churches, or craft workshops.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 在工业化之前，许多欧洲城市仍然保留着可以追溯到中世纪的特征：狭窄的街道、防御城墙，以及围绕市场、教堂或手工作坊组织的社区。

transcriptSentences.text: But industrialization changed both the economy and the physical layout of cities.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 但是工业化改变了经济和城市的物理布局。

transcriptSentences.text: Factories needed workers, access to transportation, and space for machinery.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 工厂需要工人、便利的交通以及放置机器的空间。

transcriptSentences.text: As a result, populations grew rapidly, and cities expanded beyond their older boundaries.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 结果，人口迅速增长，城市扩展到了旧有的边界之外。

transcriptSentences.text: One of the most visible changes was the removal of city walls.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 最显著的变化之一是拆除城墙。

transcriptSentences.text: Originally, walls had been built for defense, but by the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries they often limited expansion and interfered with transportation.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 最初，城墙是为防御而建的，但到了18世纪和19世纪，它们经常限制城市的扩张并妨碍交通。

transcriptSentences.text: Industrial cities needed rail lines, wider roads, canals, and later streetcar routes.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 工业城市需要铁路线、更宽的道路、运河，以及后来的有轨电车路线。

transcriptSentences.text: Old walls were frequently demolished so that goods and workers could move more efficiently.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 旧城墙经常被拆除，以便货物和工人能够更高效地移动。

transcriptSentences.text: The land where walls had stood was sometimes converted into boulevards, parks, or new commercial districts.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 城墙曾经矗立的土地有时被改造成林荫大道、公园或新的商业区。

transcriptSentences.text: Industrial workplaces also changed the daily experience of urban life.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 工业工作场所也改变了城市生活的日常体验。

transcriptSentences.text: In earlier craft production, work often took place in small workshops or even in the home.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 在早期的手工生产中，工作通常在小作坊甚至家里进行。

transcriptSentences.text: With industrialization, large numbers of workers traveled to factories according to a more rigid schedule.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 随着工业化，大量工人按照更严格的时间表前往工厂上班。

transcriptSentences.text: This contributed to the separation of residential, industrial, and commercial areas.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这促成了住宅区、工业区和商业区的分离。

transcriptSentences.text: Working class housing often developed near factories because workers needed to live close to their jobs, but these neighborhoods could be crowded and polluted.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 工人阶级的住房通常在工厂附近发展，因为工人需要住得离工作地点近，但这些社区可能很拥挤且污染严重。

transcriptSentences.text: Smoke from factories, waste from production, and poor sanitation created serious public health problems.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 工厂的烟雾、生产废料和恶劣的卫生条件造成了严重的公共卫生问题。

transcriptSentences.text: The street layout of industrial cities changed too.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 工业城市的街道布局也发生了变化。

transcriptSentences.text: Wider streets and more regular grids were introduced in some places to improve traffic flow and allow carts, carriages, and later public transit to move more easily.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 一些地方引入了更宽的街道和更规则的网格布局，以改善交通流量，并使手推车、马车以及后来的公共交通工具能够更顺畅地移动。

transcriptSentences.text: These changes had consequences beyond transportation.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 这些变化的影响超出了交通领域。

transcriptSentences.text: They encouraged the growth of commercial centers and made it easier for city governments to provide services such as lighting, sewers, and police patrols.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 它们鼓励了商业中心的增长，并使市政府更容易提供照明、下水道和警察巡逻等服务。

transcriptSentences.text: So when we study industrial cities, we are not just studying factories.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 因此，当我们研究工业城市时，我们不仅仅是在研究工厂。

transcriptSentences.text: We are studying how economic change altered space, movement, health, and daily life.
transcriptSentences.textZh: 我们是在研究经济变革如何改变了空间、交通、健康和日常生活。

versions.transcript: Have you ever been so absorbed in an activity that you lost track of time? Maybe you were playing a sport, painting, solving a difficult problem, or playing a musical instrument. Psychologists use the term flow to describe this kind of deep, focused involvement. The concept is strongly associated with psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi. In a flow state, people are highly concentrated on what they are doing. They often feel that their actions are happening smoothly, distractions fade away, and their sense of time changes. Flow has several common characteristics. The activity usually has a clear goal, and people receive some kind of immediate feedback about how well they are doing. Most importantly, the difficulty of the task has to match the person's skill level. Athletes and artists are often used as examples because their activities can create these conditions. A tennis player immediately sees the result of each shot. A musician hears whether a passage sounds right. A painter can continuously respond to what appears on the canvas. These people are not the only ones who experience flow, but their activities make the idea easy to understand. Researchers have also found that people who regularly experience flow often report greater happiness and a stronger sense of fulfillment. That does not mean every difficult activity automatically produces flow. The balance between challenge and skill is critical. If a task is too easy, a person may become bored. If it is far too difficult, the person may become anxious or frustrated. So one challenge is identifying activities that are demanding enough to require full attention, but still within a person's ability to succeed. As skills improve, the challenge often has to increase too. That helps explain why people who are deeply involved in a sport, an art, or another complex activity keep seeking new goals. Flow is not simply relaxation. It is intense engagement produced by the right combination of skill, challenge, focus, and feedback.
versions.transcriptZh: 你有没有过因为全神贯注于一项活动而忘记了时间？ 也许你当时在进行体育运动、绘画、解决一个难题，或者演奏乐器。 心理学家用“心流”这个词来描述这种深度专注的投入。 这个概念与心理学家米哈里·契克森米哈里密切相关。 在心流状态下，人们高度专注于他们正在做的事情。 他们常常觉得自己的行动流畅自如，干扰消失，时间感也随之改变。 心流有几个共同的特征。 这项活动通常有一个明确的目标，人们会立即收到关于他们做得如何的某种反馈。 最重要的是，任务的难度必须与个人的技能水平相匹配。 运动员和艺术家经常被用作例子，因为他们的活动可以创造这些条件。 网球运动员会立即看到每一次击球的结果。 音乐家会听到某段乐章听起来是否正确。 画家可以不断地回应画布上出现的内容。 这些人并不是唯一经历心流的人，但他们的活动使这个概念易于理解。 研究人员还发现，经常体验心流的人通常会报告更高的幸福感和更强的成就感。 这并不意味着每项困难的活动都会自动产生心流。 挑战与技能之间的平衡至关重要。 如果一项任务太容易，一个人可能会感到无聊。 如果任务太难，一个人可能会变得焦虑或沮丧。 因此，一个挑战是识别那些既需要全神贯注又在个人能力范围内能够成功的活动。 随着技能的提高，挑战也通常必须增加。 这有助于解释为什么那些深度投入体育、艺术或其他复杂活动的人会不断寻求新的目标。 心流不仅仅是放松。 它是通过技能、挑战、专注和反馈的正确组合所产生的强烈投入。
